```ts
/** pkt-line framing for a raw upload-pack conversation. */
const pkt = (s: string) => `${(4 + Buffer.byteLength(s)).toString(16).padStart(4, '0')}${s}`
/** A raw v0 want for the commit only refs/heads/secret holds. A client that skips git's own unadvertised-object check would send exactly this. */
const hiddenWant = (n: Nuance) => pkt(`want ${n.secret} multi_ack\n`) + '0000' + pkt('done\n')

/** In-process io: stdin from `stdin` (empty by default), with stdout bytes and stderr text collected. */
function captureIo(stdin = '') {
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = []
  let err = ''
  return {
    io: { stdin: new Blob([stdin]).stream(), stdout: { write: (b: Uint8Array) => { chunks.push(b) } }, stderr: { write: (s: string) => { err += s } } },
    out: () => Buffer.concat(chunks).toString('latin1'),
    err: () => err,
  }
}
```

`/Users/yuai/Projects/.worktrees/agenttool-collab-bridge/packages/collab-bridge/src/nuance/fetch-gate.ts`:

```ts
// The gate's third form, `git-upload-pack '<path>'` (spec §7.4; K48–K52; R15; T12–T14; P44). The Air's mirror fetch is
// the only client. Every check runs before anything is executed, each refusal is a definite pkt-line ERR, and the only
// program ever run is the git INSTALLED recorded, after its sha256 is checked, in an env built from seven keys. Leaving
// GIT_PROTOCOL out of that env is the control that matters: it forces protocol v0, where hideRefs=refs/ advertises only
// HEAD and upload-pack refuses every other want (`not our ref`); a v2 want can name any object (K49).
import { lstatSync, readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { isAbsolute, join, resolve } from 'node:path'
import { longestFolderMatch, safeRealpath, tccProtected, type Allowlist } from '../allowlist.ts'
import { gitAcceptable, sha256File } from './git-resolve.ts'
import type { InstalledInfo, Share } from './installed.ts'

/** The six `-c` pairs of §7.4, in order: refs hidden, no unadvertised wants of any kind, no filters. */
export const UPLOAD_PACK_CONFIG: readonly string[] = [
  '-c', 'uploadpack.hideRefs=refs/',
  '-c', 'uploadpack.allowTipSHA1InWant=false',
  '-c', 'uploadpack.allowReachableSHA1InWant=false',
  '-c', 'uploadpack.allowAnySHA1InWant=false',
  '-c', 'uploadpack.allowFilter=false',
  '-c', 'uploadpack.allowRefInWant=false',
]

/** `--strict` needs the absolute gitdir, so a work-tree path never serves (K51); `--timeout` ends an idle client. */
export function uploadPackArgv(gitdir: string): string[] {
  return [...UPLOAD_PACK_CONFIG, 'upload-pack', '--strict', '--timeout=120', gitdir]
}

/** Exactly the seven keys of §7.4. Built, never inherited (P14), and never GIT_PROTOCOL. */
export function gitEnv(home: string): Record<string, string> {
  return {
    PATH: '/usr/bin:/bin',
    HOME: home,
    LC_ALL: 'C',
    GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: '1',
    GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: '/dev/null',
    GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH: '1',
    GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0',
  }
}

export interface FetchGateCtx { home: string; installed: InstalledInfo; shares: Share[]; allowlist: Allowlist | null; uid: number; realpath?: (p: string) => string | null }
export type FetchRefusal = 'path_form' | 'not_realpath' | 'tcc_protected' | 'not_shared' | 'not_edit_folder' | 'git_link' | 'outside_edit_folder' | 'foreign_owner' | 'alternates'
export type FetchCheck = { ok: true; gitdir: string; worktree: string } | { ok: false; code: FetchRefusal }

const refuse = (code: FetchRefusal): FetchCheck => ({ ok: false, code })

/** `//`, `/./`, `/../`, a trailing `/`, or a final `/.` or `/..`: one spelling per directory, or nothing. */
function badForm(p: string): boolean {
  return !p.startsWith('/') || p.includes('//') || p.includes('/./') || p.includes('/../')
    || p.endsWith('/') || p.endsWith('/.') || p.endsWith('/..')
}

/** A small file's text, or null when it is not a regular file (a symlink included) or cannot be read. */
function smallRegularFile(p: string, max = 4096): string | null {
  try {
    const st = lstatSync(p)
    if (!st.isFile() || st.size > max) return null
    return readFileSync(p, 'utf8')
  } catch {
    return null
  }
}

/** Where `<worktree>/.git` leads: the dir itself, or the target of a `gitdir: <path>` file; null for a symlink or anything else. */
function dotGitTarget(worktree: string, realpath: (p: string) => string | null): string | null {
  const dotGit = join(worktree, '.git')
  let st
  try { st = lstatSync(dotGit) } catch { return null }
  if (st.isSymbolicLink()) return null
  if (st.isDirectory()) return realpath(dotGit)
  if (!st.isFile()) return null
  const m = /^gitdir: (.+?)\r?\n?$/.exec(smallRegularFile(dotGit) ?? '')
  if (!m) return null
  return realpath(isAbsolute(m[1]!) ? m[1]! : resolve(worktree, m[1]!))
}

/** The repository's common dir: `<gitdir>/commondir` resolved (a linked work tree), else the gitdir itself; null when unreadable. */
function commonDirOf(gitdir: string, realpath: (p: string) => string | null): string | null {
  const file = join(gitdir, 'commondir')
  try { lstatSync(file) } catch { return gitdir }
  const text = smallRegularFile(file)
  if (text === null) return null
  const rel = text.trim()
  if (rel === '') return null
  return realpath(isAbsolute(rel) ? rel : resolve(gitdir, rel))
}

const isEditIn = (p: string, al: Allowlist, home: string, realpath: (p: string) => string | null) =>
  longestFolderMatch(p, al, home, realpath)?.access === 'edit'

function ownedDir(p: string, uid: number): boolean {
  try {
    const st = statSync(p)
    return st.isDirectory() && st.uid === uid
  } catch {
    return false
  }
}

/** Whether anything, even a dangling symlink, sits at this path. */
function present(p: string): boolean {
  try { lstatSync(p); return true } catch { return false }
}

/**
 * §7.4's checks, in order, before anything runs. `path` is what the gate's grammar captured between the quotes.
 * Same-uid symlink races between these checks and git's own open are an accepted residual risk while the Air is the only
 * client (§7.4).
 */
export function checkUploadPackPath(path: string, ctx: FetchGateCtx): FetchCheck {
  const realpath = ctx.realpath ?? safeRealpath
  if (badForm(path)) return refuse('path_form')
  if (realpath(path) !== path) return refuse('not_realpath')
  if (tccProtected(path, ctx.home, realpath)) return refuse('tcc_protected')
  const share = ctx.shares.find((s) => s.gitdir === path)
  if (!share) return refuse('not_shared')
  const worktree = share.realpath
  // The work tree is checked too: a gitdir file can put the repository's files in a TCC folder while its gitdir is not.
  if (tccProtected(worktree, ctx.home, realpath)) return refuse('tcc_protected')
  if (!ctx.allowlist || realpath(worktree) !== worktree || !isEditIn(worktree, ctx.allowlist, ctx.home, realpath)) return refuse('not_edit_folder')
  if (dotGitTarget(worktree, realpath) !== path) return refuse('git_link')
  const common = commonDirOf(path, realpath)
  if (!common) return refuse('outside_edit_folder')
  for (const dir of new Set([path, common])) {
    if (!isEditIn(dir, ctx.allowlist, ctx.home, realpath)) return refuse('outside_edit_folder')
  }
  for (const dir of new Set([path, common])) {
    if (!ownedDir(dir, ctx.uid)) return refuse('foreign_owner')
  }
  if (present(join(common, 'objects', 'info', 'alternates'))) return refuse('alternates')
  return { ok: true, gitdir: path, worktree }
}

/** One pkt-line `ERR <message>`, which git shows as `fatal: remote error: <message>`. */
export function pktLineErr(message: string): Uint8Array {
  return Buffer.from(`${(4 + 4 + message.length + 1).toString(16).padStart(4, '0')}ERR ${message}\n`, 'utf8')
}

export interface FetchGateIo {
  stdin: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>
  stdout: { write(b: Uint8Array): void }      // may return a promise, which is awaited before the next chunk
  stderr: { write(s: string): void }
}

/**
 * The upload-pack form, end to end. A refusal writes one pkt-line ERR and one stderr line and exits 64; otherwise the
 * recorded git runs with stdin and stdout piped byte for byte, and its exit code is the gate's. `bytes` counts what git
 * wrote to stdout (0 for a refusal), for the gate's content-free ledger line (Task 24).
 */
export async function runFetchGate(path: string, ctx: FetchGateCtx, io: FetchGateIo): Promise<{ exit: number; outcome: string; bytes: number }> {
  const refused = async (code: string) => {
    await io.stdout.write(pktLineErr(code))
    io.stderr.write(`collab-bridge gate: upload-pack refused: ${code}\n`)
    return { exit: 64, outcome: code, bytes: 0 }
  }
  const check = checkUploadPackPath(path, ctx)
  if (!check.ok) return refused(check.code)
  let sha: string | null
  try { sha = sha256File(ctx.installed.git.path) } catch { sha = null }
  // A Software Update or `brew upgrade` lands here by design: the install check must be re-run (§7.4).
  if (sha !== ctx.installed.git.sha256) return refused('git_changed')
  if (!gitAcceptable(ctx.installed.git)) return refused('git_unsafe')

  const proc = Bun.spawn([ctx.installed.git.path, ...uploadPackArgv(check.gitdir)], {
    cwd: '/', env: gitEnv(ctx.home), stdin: 'pipe', stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'pipe',
  })
  let done = false
  const exited = proc.exited.then((code) => { done = true; return code })
  const reader = io.stdin.getReader()
  const pumpIn = (async () => {
    try {
      for (;;) {
        const r = await Promise.race([reader.read(), exited.then(() => null)])
        if (r === null || r.done) break
        proc.stdin.write(r.value)
        await proc.stdin.flush()
      }
    } catch {
      // git went away while the client was still talking: its exit code says what happened.
    } finally {
      try { proc.stdin.end() } catch { /* already closed */ }
      if (done) reader.cancel().catch(() => {})
    }
  })()
  const pumpErr = (async () => {
    const dec = new TextDecoder()
    for await (const chunk of proc.stderr) io.stderr.write(dec.decode(chunk, { stream: true }))
  })()
  let bytes = 0
  for await (const chunk of proc.stdout) {
    bytes += chunk.byteLength
    await io.stdout.write(chunk)
  }
  const code = await exited
  await Promise.all([pumpIn, pumpErr])
  return { exit: code, outcome: code === 0 ? 'served' : 'git_failed', bytes }
}
```

```ts
export type GateCommand = { form: 'hello' } | { form: 'relay'; nonce: string } | { form: 'upload-pack'; path: string }
export const GATE_FORMS: { hello: RegExp; relay: RegExp; uploadPack: RegExp }   // /^hello$/, /^relay 1 ([0-9a-f]{32})$/, /^git-upload-pack '(\/[^'!\\\x00-\x1f\x7f]{1,1024})'$/
export function parseGateCommand(raw: string | undefined): GateCommand | null
export function uploadPackShaped(raw: string | undefined): boolean               // starts with 'git-upload-pack '

  shares: Share[]; git: ResolvedGit; summon: { key_sha256: string; dropin_stat: string };
  summon_now: { key_sha256: string; dropin_stat: string | null }; claude_version: string | null; zshenv_clean: boolean; clock: string }
export function zshenvClean(zsh: string, home: string): boolean                  // `zsh -c 'exit 0' </dev/null` with env {HOME, PATH:'/usr/bin:/bin'} prints 0 bytes
```

  Added by this task:
```ts
export const MAX_UPLOAD_PACK_PATH_BYTES = 1024
//   parseGateCommand also requires Buffer.byteLength(path) <= 1024: GATE_FORMS.uploadPack's {1,1024} counts characters after
//   the slash, so alone it admits a 1025-byte path and multibyte paths over 1024 bytes (§5.2: "the 1024-byte form")
```

Notes for the implementer:
- `GATE_FORMS` carries no regex flags: without `m`, a JavaScript `$` matches only at the end of the string (never before a trailing newline), and without `g` a regex keeps no `lastIndex` between calls. The test pins both.
- `describeCommand` is Summon's, verbatim (`packages/summon/src/gatekeeper.ts:32-36` at `b3ef7c95`; plan-facts `summon.md:1207-1211`).
- `zshenvClean` is stricter than "prints 0 bytes on stdout": stderr output and a non-zero exit also make it false. Anything on stdout comes before the relay's preamble (§5.4); anything on stderr muddies the one stderr line the hub reads from a refused gate (§5.4, `needs Yu: config`); a non-zero exit stops the forced command. It runs in the home with stdin `/dev/null` and env `{HOME, PATH}`, as sshd starts `$SHELL -c` (K37). Task 55's install check uses the same function.
- `buildHello` answers an error and nothing else when INSTALLED, `shares.json`, the seat public key or `authorized_keys` cannot be read, so pin-device never records a device from a partial answer. A missing Summon drop-in is reported as `summon_now.dropin_stat: null`, not as an error. `summon_now` is computed at each call (P22); `claude_version` is INSTALLED's (P23): the gate runs no harness.
- The tests build their Nuance home with an explicit env so `nuancePaths` puts the Summon drop-in inside that temp home, never at the suite's shared drop-in path.
- The tests' INSTALLED is Task 21's `testInstalled` with three overrides: the fixed Apple `RECORDED_GIT`, and the two Summon baselines computed from this home's `authorized_keys` and drop-in. The hello assertions spell out `testInstalled`'s fixed values (`abcdef01`, `20261013120000`, `20270111`, `2.1.296 (Claude Code)`).

```ts
interface Installed { home: string; paths: NuancePaths; installed: InstalledInfo; seatPublic: string; share: string }

/** A Nuance home as `install write` leaves it: INSTALLED with the Summon baselines, shares.json, the seat key, authorized_keys. */
function installedHome(): Installed {
  const home = temp('cb-hello-')
  const paths = nuancePaths(home, {
    ...process.env, HOME: home, COLLAB_BRIDGE_HOME_OVERRIDE: home,
    COLLAB_BRIDGE_SUMMON_DROPIN: join(home, 'etc', 'ssh', 'sshd_config.d', '010-summon.conf'),
  })
  mkdirSync(dirname(paths.authorizedKeys), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
  writeFileSync(paths.authorizedKeys, `${SUMMON_LINE}\n${COLLAB_LINE}\n`, { mode: 0o600 })
  mkdirSync(dirname(paths.summonDropin), { recursive: true })
  writeFileSync(paths.summonDropin, 'PasswordAuthentication no\n', { mode: 0o600 })
  const seatPublic = writeSeatKeyIfAbsent(paths).publicHex
  const share = join(home, 'Projects', 'collab-trial')
  mkdirSync(share, { recursive: true })
  writeShares(paths, [{ realpath: share, gitdir: join(share, '.git') }])
  const installed = testInstalled({
    git: RECORDED_GIT, summon_key_sha256: summonKeySha256(readFileSync(paths.authorizedKeys, 'utf8')),
    summon_dropin_stat: dropinStat(paths.summonDropin)!,
  })
  mkdirSync(paths.share, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
  writeFileSync(paths.installed, renderInstalled(installed), { mode: 0o600 })
  return { home, paths, installed, seatPublic, share }
}
```

```ts
// The forced command's closed grammar and its `hello` answer (spec §5.2; R2; T20; P22, P23). The grammar is three
// regexes and nothing else: any other SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND (scp, sftp, a shell line, extra spaces) is refused by the
// gate entry (Task 24) with exit 64, and an upload-pack-shaped one also gets a pkt-line ERR git can show.
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import type { NuancePaths } from '../paths.ts'
import type { ResolvedGit } from './git-resolve.ts'
import { dropinStat, readInstalled, readShares, summonKeySha256, type Share } from './installed.ts'
import { readSeatPublicHex } from './seatkey.ts'

export type GateCommand = { form: 'hello' } | { form: 'relay'; nonce: string } | { form: 'upload-pack'; path: string }

/** The whole grammar (§5.2). No flags: `$` is the end of the command, and a regex keeps no state between calls. */
export const GATE_FORMS: { hello: RegExp; relay: RegExp; uploadPack: RegExp } = {
  hello: /^hello$/,
  relay: /^relay 1 ([0-9a-f]{32})$/,
  uploadPack: /^git-upload-pack '(\/[^'!\\\x00-\x1f\x7f]{1,1024})'$/,
}

/** The quoted path is the gitdir, which must fit the 1024-byte form (§5.2's cost line); the regex counts characters. */
export const MAX_UPLOAD_PACK_PATH_BYTES = 1024

export function parseGateCommand(raw: string | undefined): GateCommand | null {
  if (raw === undefined) return null
  if (GATE_FORMS.hello.test(raw)) return { form: 'hello' }
  const relay = GATE_FORMS.relay.exec(raw)
  if (relay) return { form: 'relay', nonce: relay[1]! }
  const pack = GATE_FORMS.uploadPack.exec(raw)
  if (pack && Buffer.byteLength(pack[1]!, 'utf8') <= MAX_UPLOAD_PACK_PATH_BYTES) return { form: 'upload-pack', path: pack[1]! }
  return null
}

/** A refusal git will read: git sends `git-upload-pack '<path>'`, so a refused one of these gets a pkt-line ERR (§5.2). */
export function uploadPackShaped(raw: string | undefined): boolean {
  return raw !== undefined && raw.startsWith('git-upload-pack ')
}

/**
 * What the ledger may say about a refused command (Summon's describeCommand, verbatim). The ledger is hash-chained and
 * cannot be redacted later, and a client can put anything in SSH_ORIGINAL_COMMAND, including a prompt, so this is
 * content-free: the byte length, and the first token only when it looks like a program name.
 */
export function describeCommand(raw: string | undefined): string {
  if (raw === undefined) return 'unset'
  const first = raw.split(/\s/, 1)[0]!
  return `len ${Buffer.byteLength(raw, 'utf8')}, first token ${/^[a-z][a-z-]{0,15}$/.test(first) ? `"${first}"` : 'not shown'}`
}

export interface Hello { v: 1; device: string; build: string; prepared: string; expiry: string; user: string; seat_public: string;
  shares: Share[]; git: ResolvedGit; summon: { key_sha256: string; dropin_stat: string };
  summon_now: { key_sha256: string; dropin_stat: string | null }; claude_version: string | null; zshenv_clean: boolean; clock: string }

/**
 * Whether sshd's `$SHELL -c` start prints nothing (K37, R26): `zsh -c 'exit 0' </dev/null` in the home, as sshd starts it,
 * with only HOME and PATH. Anything on stdout would come before the relay's preamble; anything on stderr would muddy the
 * one line the hub reads from a refused gate; a non-zero exit would stop the forced command itself. All three are unclean.
 */
export function zshenvClean(zsh: string, home: string): boolean {
  const r = spawnSync(zsh, ['-c', 'exit 0'], {
    cwd: home, env: { HOME: home, PATH: '/usr/bin:/bin' }, stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'], timeout: 5_000,
  })
  return r.status === 0 && (r.stdout?.length ?? 0) === 0 && (r.stderr?.length ?? 0) === 0
}

/**
 * `hello`'s one JSON object, or an error and nothing else: a partial hello could pin a device on missing facts (§10.2
 * step 2). The Summon baselines come twice, as INSTALLED recorded them and as they are now (P22), so the live test
 * compares them without a Yu step; Claude's version is the one the installer recorded (P23), since the gate runs no harness.
 */
export function buildHello(o: { paths: NuancePaths; user: string; now: () => Date; zsh: string }): Hello | { error: string } {
  const installed = readInstalled(o.paths)
  if (!installed) return { error: 'INSTALLED is missing or unreadable' }
  const shares = readShares(o.paths)
  if (!shares) return { error: 'shares.json is missing or unreadable' }
  const seat = readSeatPublicHex(o.paths)
  if (!seat) return { error: 'the seat public key is missing or unreadable' }
  let keys: string
  try { keys = readFileSync(o.paths.authorizedKeys, 'utf8') } catch { return { error: 'authorized_keys is unreadable' } }
  return {
    v: 1,
    device: installed.device,
    build: installed.build,
    prepared: installed.prepared,
    expiry: installed.expiry,
    user: o.user,
    seat_public: seat,
    shares,
    git: installed.git,
    summon: { key_sha256: installed.summon_key_sha256, dropin_stat: installed.summon_dropin_stat },
    summon_now: { key_sha256: summonKeySha256(keys), dropin_stat: dropinStat(o.paths.summonDropin) },
    claude_version: installed.claude_version,
    zshenv_clean: zshenvClean(o.zsh, o.paths.home),
    clock: o.now().toISOString(),
  }
}
```

```ts
// src/nuance/unix.ts — the unix-socket plumbing the relay, the link client (Task 29), the tap server (Task 31) and the fake link share
export interface RawSock { write(b: Uint8Array): number; end(): void }
export class Outbox { constructor(sock: RawSock, o?: { onDead?(): void }); push(b: Uint8Array): void; drain(): void; endWhenFlushed(): void; clear(): void }
//   push writes at once while nothing waits and queues the rest of a partial write, in order, for drain(); a write of -1
//   drops the queue, calls onDead once and writes nothing more; endWhenFlushed ends the socket once the queue is empty (P18);
//   clear drops what waits without ending the socket
export function listenPrivate<T>(path: string, socket: SocketHandler<T>, o: { replace: boolean }): { server: UnixSocketListener<T>; ino: bigint | null }
//   unlink, bind under umask 0177 (restored, a throw included), chmod 0600; replace: true binds `<path>.<pid>`, reads its inode
//   and renames it over `path` (ino set); replace: false binds `path` itself (ino null); a failure after the bind stops the
//   listener and throws; path-length checks stay with the callers (P16)
// src/nuance/relay.ts
export interface RelayTimers { setInterval(fn: () => void, ms: number): unknown; clearInterval(h: unknown): void }
export interface RelayDeps { paths: NuancePaths; nonce: string; stdin: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>; write(bytes: Uint8Array): void;
  mono(): number; ledger(f: LedgerFields): void; timers?: RelayTimers; staleMs?: number; exitMs?: number; inodeCheckMs?: number }
export interface RelayStatusFile { pid: number; started_mono: number; last_ping_mono: number | null; streams: number }
export function readRelayStatus(paths: NuancePaths): RelayStatusFile | null
export async function runRelay(deps: RelayDeps): Promise<number>
//   listens first and only then writes the preamble (the start order below); dirs run/ 0700; binds run/hub.sock.<pid> under umask 0177, chmod 0600, renames over run/hub.sock and
//   records its inode; each local connection → mux.open() stream (ids from 1); local frames are stream 0 on the socket and are
//   re-numbered to the connection's stream toward the hub and back; PING from the hub → PONG back and a copy to every local connection;
//   last PING older than staleMs → a new local connection gets DATA refused{hub_away} then CLOSE; no PING for exitMs → exit 0;
//   every inodeCheckMs: hub.sock's inode differs → ledger `relay_replaced`, DATA {t:'relay_replaced'} on stream 0, exit 0;
//   a local frame over 2 MiB closes that connection (CLOSE to the hub); a hub frame over 4 MiB closes that stream; stdin EOF → exit 0;
//   on exit unlink hub.sock only while its inode is still ours; writes run/relay.json on every PING; never parses MCP
```
  Added by this task (each the smallest workable change; reported as interface deviations):
  - `RelayDeps.stderr?: { write(s: string): void }` and `export const RELAY_START_REFUSED = 64`: a relay that cannot listen says why on one stderr line and exits like a refused gate command, so the dialer's "exit 64 before the preamble" rule (§5.4) reports `needs Yu: config`.
  - Start order: the relay binds first and prints its preamble only once it is listening (the skeleton listed the preamble first). A relay that cannot listen writes nothing to stdout, so it never announces a link that can carry no pipe; "the preamble before any frame" still holds.
  - `run/relay.json` is written at start as well as on every PING, and removed on exit only while it still names this relay (pid and `started_mono`), so `collab-bridge status` (Task 24) sees a relay from its first moment and never a dead one's file.

Notes for the implementer:
- Verified on this Air (Bun 1.3.13, scratch runs): a listening unix socket keeps accepting after `renameSync` moves its file; `server.stop(true)` unlinks only the name it bound, which the rename already moved, so it can never remove a newer relay's `hub.sock`; `Bun.listen` under `process.umask(0o177)` creates the socket 0600 (air-env §6.7); listening on an existing path fails `EADDRINUSE` and a SIGKILLed listener leaves its file (F8), which is why the relay never listens on `hub.sock` itself.
- Bun's `socket.write` returns the bytes the kernel took right now (8192 of a 4 MiB write here) and drops nothing only if the caller keeps the rest: `Outbox` (in `unix.ts`, so Tasks 29 and 31 and the fake link reuse it rather than copy it) queues the remainder in order and flushes it on `drain`. A write to a closed socket returns -1, which marks the outbox dead. `listenPrivate` is the one place a unix socket is bound; `tests/unix.test.ts` uses its own `staleSocket()` (the SIGKILL spawn `relay.test.ts` also uses) because `tests/fake-link.ts` comes only in Task 29.
- Until the first PING arrives, the relay's own start counts as the last PING, for both the 20 s refusal and the 45 s exit: the hub has just dialled, and its first PING may come only after 15 s.
- Ledger lines (through `deps.ledger`, which the gate points at `appendLedger(paths.ledger, NUANCE_LEDGER_KEYS, …)` in Task 24): `{event:'relay', outcome:'start'}`, `{event:'relay', outcome:'exit', code:<reason>, ms}` with reason `stdin_eof`, `no_ping`, `relay_replaced`, `hub_malformed` or `stdin_error`, or, instead of both, `{event:'relay', outcome:'refused', code:'socket_path_too_long' | 'bind_failed'}`. Nothing from a frame ever reaches it.
- The relay drops a hub DATA or CLOSE for a stream it already closed, opens no stream for the hub, ignores OPEN, PING and PONG from a pipe, and closes a pipe connection that sends a frame on any stream but 0. A FrameTooLarge or FrameMalformed carries the good frames of the same push (Task 14); they are delivered before the connection or stream is closed.
- The tests drive the relay in process with an injected monotonic clock and hand-fired interval timers (`handTimers`), so nothing waits 5, 20 or 45 real seconds; sockets live under `shortSockRoot()` (K46).
- `scaled`, `appendLedger`, `NUANCE_LEDGER_KEYS` and `monoNowMs` reach the relay through `RelayDeps`, not as imports: Task 24's gate passes `scaled(TIMING.staleMs | relayExitMs | inodeCheckMs, env)`, an `appendLedger` closure and `monoNowMs`, so this module reads no environment and the tests inject everything.

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test'
import { existsSync, lstatSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import type { LedgerFields } from '../src/ledger.ts'
import { encodeFrame, FRAME_HEADER_BYTES, FRAME_TYPE, FrameDecoder, PreambleScanner, preambleOf, type Frame, type FrameType } from '../src/link/frame.ts'
import { decodeJson, MAX_HUB_TO_PIPE, MAX_PIPE_TO_HUB } from '../src/link/messages.ts'
import { readRelayStatus, RELAY_START_REFUSED, runRelay, type RelayTimers } from '../src/nuance/relay.ts'
import { nuancePaths, type NuancePaths } from '../src/paths.ts'
import { cleanupTmps, modeOf, shortSockRoot, temp } from './helpers.ts'

const NONCE = '0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef'
const { OPEN, DATA, CLOSE, PING, PONG } = FRAME_TYPE
const enc = new TextEncoder()
const dec = new TextDecoder()

/** A temp Nuance home whose sockets sit under a short root (K46: $TMPDIR alone is 49 characters). */
function nuance(sockRoot: string = shortSockRoot()): NuancePaths {
  const home = temp('cb-relay-')
  return nuancePaths(home, { HOME: home, COLLAB_BRIDGE_HOME_OVERRIDE: home, COLLAB_BRIDGE_SOCK_ROOT: sockRoot, COLLAB_BRIDGE_SUMMON_DROPIN: join(home, 'dropin') })
}

/** Interval timers the test fires by hand, so no test waits 5, 20 or 45 real seconds. */
function handTimers(): RelayTimers & { fire(): void; count(): number } {
  const live = new Map<number, () => void>()
  let n = 0
  return {
    setInterval(fn) { live.set(++n, fn); return n },
    clearInterval(h) { live.delete(h as number) },
    fire() { for (const fn of [...live.values()]) fn() },
    count: () => live.size,
  }
}

/** The 9-byte header of a frame that declares `len` payload bytes, for the size limits. */
function header(len: number, type: FrameType, stream: number): Uint8Array {
  const h = new Uint8Array(FRAME_HEADER_BYTES)
  const v = new DataView(h.buffer)
  v.setUint32(0, len)
  v.setUint8(4, type)
  v.setUint32(5, stream)
  return h
}

/** The hub's end of the ssh channel: what the relay writes (decoded after its preamble), and frames to send it. */
function hubEnd() {
  let ctl!: ReadableStreamDefaultController<Uint8Array>
  const stdin = new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({ start(c) { ctl = c } })
  const scanner = new PreambleScanner(NONCE)
  const decoder = new FrameDecoder(MAX_PIPE_TO_HUB)
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = []
  const frames: Frame[] = []
  let found = false
  return {
    stdin, chunks, frames,
    write(bytes: Uint8Array) {
      chunks.push(bytes.slice())
      let rest = bytes
      if (!found) {
        const s = scanner.push(bytes)
        if (s.state !== 'found') return
        found = true
        rest = s.rest
      }
      frames.push(...decoder.push(rest))
    },
    send(type: FrameType, stream: number, payload?: Uint8Array) { ctl.enqueue(encodeFrame(type, stream, payload)) },
    raw(bytes: Uint8Array) { ctl.enqueue(bytes) },
    end() { try { ctl.close() } catch { /* already closed or cancelled */ } },
    preambleSeen: () => found,
    of: (type: FrameType, stream?: number) => frames.filter((f) => f.type === type && (stream === undefined || f.stream === stream)),
  }
}

/** A pipe's end of a local connection to run/hub.sock: frames in, frames out, and whether the relay closed it. */
function localClient(path: string) {
  const decoder = new FrameDecoder(MAX_HUB_TO_PIPE)
  const frames: Frame[] = []
  let closed = false
  let sock: { write(b: Uint8Array): number; end(): void } | null = null
  const ready = Bun.connect({ unix: path, socket: {
    data(_s, d) { frames.push(...decoder.push(d)) },
    close() { closed = true },
    error() { closed = true },
  } }).then((s) => { sock = s })
  return {
    ready, frames,
    isClosed: () => closed,
    send(type: FrameType, payload?: Uint8Array) { sock!.write(encodeFrame(type, 0, payload)) },
    raw(bytes: Uint8Array) { sock!.write(bytes) },
    end() { sock?.end() },
    messages: () => frames.filter((f) => f.type === DATA).map((f) => decodeJson(f.payload)),
  }
}

async function until<T>(f: () => T | null | undefined | false, ms = 3000): Promise<T> {
  const end = Date.now() + ms
  for (;;) {
    const v = f()
    if (v) return v
    if (Date.now() > end) throw new Error('until: timed out')
    await Bun.sleep(5)
  }
}

const running: Array<{ hub: ReturnType<typeof hubEnd>; done: Promise<number> }> = []

async function startRelay(o: { paths?: NuancePaths; clock?: { t: number } } = {}) {
  const paths = o.paths ?? nuance()
  const clock = o.clock ?? { t: 1_000_000 }
  const hub = hubEnd()
  const timers = handTimers()
  const ledger: LedgerFields[] = []
  let settled = false
  const done = runRelay({ paths, nonce: NONCE, stdin: hub.stdin, write: (b) => hub.write(b), mono: () => clock.t,
    ledger: (f) => { ledger.push(f) }, timers, staleMs: 20_000, exitMs: 45_000, inodeCheckMs: 5_000 })
  done.then(() => { settled = true })
  running.push({ hub, done })
  await until(() => hub.preambleSeen())
  return { paths, clock, hub, timers, ledger, done, settled: () => settled }
}

afterEach(async () => {
  for (const r of running.splice(0)) { r.hub.end(); await r.done }
  cleanupTmps()
})

describe('relay', () => {
  test('writes the preamble before any frame', async () => {
    const r = await startRelay()
    expect(dec.decode(r.hub.chunks[0])).toBe(preambleOf(NONCE))
    const c = localClient(r.paths.hubSock)
    await c.ready
    await until(() => r.hub.of(OPEN).length === 1)
    expect(r.hub.frames.map((f) => [f.type, f.stream])).toEqual([[OPEN, 1]])
  })

  test('binds a fresh name, renames it into place, 0600 in a 0700 dir', async () => {
    const paths = nuance()
    mkdirSync(paths.run, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
    writeFileSync(`${paths.hubSock}.${process.pid}`, 'left by an earlier relay that had this pid')
    const r = await startRelay({ paths })
    expect(lstatSync(paths.hubSock).isSocket()).toBe(true)
    expect(modeOf(paths.hubSock)).toBe(0o600)
    expect(modeOf(paths.run)).toBe(0o700)
    expect(readdirSync(paths.run).filter((n) => n.startsWith('hub.sock.'))).toEqual([])
    expect(readRelayStatus(paths)).toEqual({ pid: process.pid, started_mono: 1_000_000, last_ping_mono: null, streams: 0 })
    expect(modeOf(paths.relayStatus)).toBe(0o600)
    expect(r.ledger).toEqual([{ event: 'relay', outcome: 'start' }])
  })

  test('each local connection is a new stream id, never reused', async () => {
    const r = await startRelay()
    for (let i = 1; i <= 3; i++) {
```

```ts
/** A RawSock that takes at most `take` bytes a write (8192 is what this Air's kernel takes), or -1 once it is dead. */
function fakeSock(o: { take?: number } = {}) {
  const got: Uint8Array[] = []
  let ends = 0
  let attempts = 0
  let dead = false
  const sock: RawSock = {
    write(b) {
      attempts++
      if (dead) return -1
      const n = Math.min(o.take ?? 8192, b.byteLength)
      got.push(b.slice(0, n))
      return n
    },
    end() { ends++ },
  }
  return { sock, bytes: () => Buffer.concat(got), ends: () => ends, attempts: () => attempts, kill: () => { dead = true } }
}

describe('Outbox', () => {
  test('a 4 MiB push arrives whole and in order across partial writes', () => {
    const f = fakeSock()
    const out = new Outbox(f.sock)
    const big = randomBytes(4 * 1024 * 1024)
    const tail = new TextEncoder().encode('and then this')
    out.push(big)
    out.push(tail) // queued behind the rest of big, not written past it
    expect(f.bytes().byteLength).toBe(8192)
    const total = big.byteLength + tail.byteLength
    for (let i = 0; i < 1000 && f.bytes().byteLength < total; i++) out.drain()
    expect(Buffer.compare(f.bytes(), Buffer.concat([big, tail]))).toBe(0)
    expect(f.ends()).toBe(0)
  })

  test('a write of -1 drops the queue and calls onDead once', () => {
    const f = fakeSock()
    let dead = 0
    const out = new Outbox(f.sock, { onDead: () => { dead++ } })
    out.push(new Uint8Array(20_000)) // 8192 out, the rest waits
    f.kill()
    out.drain()
    expect(dead).toBe(1)
    const tries = f.attempts()
    out.push(new Uint8Array(10))
    out.drain()
    expect(f.attempts()).toBe(tries) // nothing is written after it
    expect(dead).toBe(1)
    expect(f.bytes().byteLength).toBe(8192)
  })

  test('endWhenFlushed ends the socket only after the queue is empty', () => {
    const f = fakeSock()
    const out = new Outbox(f.sock)
    out.push(new Uint8Array(20_000)) // 8192 now, 11808 wait
    out.endWhenFlushed()
    expect(f.ends()).toBe(0)
    out.drain() // 8192 more, 3616 wait
    expect(f.ends()).toBe(0)
    out.drain()
    expect(f.bytes().byteLength).toBe(20_000)
    expect(f.ends()).toBe(1)
    const g = fakeSock()
    new Outbox(g.sock).endWhenFlushed()
    expect(g.ends()).toBe(1) // nothing waits: it ends at once
  })

  test('clear drops what waits and leaves the socket open', () => {
    const f = fakeSock()
    const out = new Outbox(f.sock)
    out.push(new Uint8Array(20_000))
    out.clear()
    out.drain()
    expect(f.bytes().byteLength).toBe(8192)
    expect(f.ends()).toBe(0)
    out.push(new Uint8Array(5)) // still usable
    expect(f.bytes().byteLength).toBe(8197)
  })
})
```

```ts
// Unix-socket plumbing the Nuance side shares: the relay (C3), the pipe's link client and its tap socket (C4), and the
// tests' fake link. Two things: a listener that is 0600 from its first moment (P17), and an outbox that keeps what
// Bun's socket.write did not take. Bun writes what the kernel accepts right now (8 KiB at a time on this Air for a unix
// socket), returns that count and buffers nothing, so the rest of every partial write waits here, in order, for `drain`.
import type { SocketHandler, UnixSocketListener } from 'bun'
import { chmodSync, lstatSync, renameSync, unlinkSync } from 'node:fs'

/** The two calls of a Bun socket the outbox makes. */
export interface RawSock { write(b: Uint8Array): number; end(): void }

/**
 * Bytes for one socket, in order. A push goes straight to the socket while nothing waits, and a partial write keeps the
 * rest for `drain`. A write that returns -1 (the socket is closed) drops the queue and calls onDead, once; nothing is
 * written after it.
 */
export class Outbox {
  private queue: Uint8Array[] = []
  private ending = false
  private dead = false
  constructor(private readonly sock: RawSock, private readonly o: { onDead?(): void } = {}) {}

  push(b: Uint8Array): void {
    if (this.dead) return
    if (this.queue.length > 0) this.queue.push(b)
    else this.send(b)
  }

  /** Bun's drain callback: the kernel takes bytes again. */
  drain(): void {
    while (this.queue.length > 0) if (!this.send(this.queue.shift()!)) return
    if (this.ending) this.sock.end()
  }

  /** P18: the side that ends an exchange writes its CLOSE frame first; the socket ends once everything is out. */
  endWhenFlushed(): void {
    if (this.queue.length === 0) this.sock.end()
    else this.ending = true
  }

  /** Drops what waits, without ending the socket. */
  clear(): void {
    this.queue = []
  }

  private send(b: Uint8Array): boolean {
    const n = this.sock.write(b)
    if (n < 0) {
      this.queue = []
      this.dead = true
      this.o.onDead?.()
      return false
    }
    if (n < b.byteLength) { this.queue.unshift(b.subarray(n)); return false }
    return true
  }
}

/**
 * Bun.listen on a unix socket that is 0600 from its first moment: bound under umask 0177 (restored afterwards, a throw
 * included), then chmodded 0600. A socket file outlives a SIGKILLed listener and listening on a path that exists fails
 * with EADDRINUSE (F8), so the name is unlinked before the bind.
 * - replace: true binds `<path>.<pid>`, a name only this process uses, reads its inode, then renames it over `path`. A
 *   stale or older socket at `path` is replaced in one step, and Bun's stop() later unlinks only the name it bound,
 *   which the rename already moved, so it never removes a newer listener's socket (P17). `ino` lets the caller check
 *   later whether `path` is still its own.
 * - replace: false unlinks `path` and binds it directly; `ino` is null.
 * Path-length checks stay with the callers, each with its own refusal code (P16). A failure after the bind stops the
 * listener (which unlinks the name it bound) and throws.
 */
export function listenPrivate<T>(path: string, socket: SocketHandler<T>, o: { replace: boolean }): { server: UnixSocketListener<T>; ino: bigint | null } {
  const bind = o.replace ? `${path}.${process.pid}` : path
  try { unlinkSync(bind) } catch { /* nothing there: the usual case */ }
  const mask = process.umask(0o177)
  let server: UnixSocketListener<T>
  try {
    server = Bun.listen<T>({ unix: bind, socket })
  } finally {
    process.umask(mask)
  }
  try {
    chmodSync(bind, 0o600)
    if (!o.replace) return { server, ino: null }
    const ino = lstatSync(bind, { bigint: true }).ino
    renameSync(bind, path)
    return { server, ino }
  } catch (e) {
    server.stop(true)
    throw e
  }
}
```

```ts
// The Nuance relay (C3, spec §5.3). The gate execs it for `relay 1 <nonce>`, so its stdin and stdout are the one ssh
// channel to the Air's hub. It listens on run/hub.sock for this Mac's pipes, gives each local connection its own stream
// on the link (ids from 1, never reused), copies every hub PING to every pipe so each knows how fresh the link is, and
// moves frames both ways. It never parses MCP: the frame size limits of §6.6 are the only thing it checks.
import { chmodSync, lstatSync, mkdirSync, readFileSync, unlinkSync } from 'node:fs'
import type { LedgerFields } from '../ledger.ts'
import { encodeFrame, FRAME_TYPE, FrameDecoder, FrameMalformed, FrameTooLarge, preambleOf, type Frame } from '../link/frame.ts'
import { Mux } from '../link/mux.ts'
import { encodeMessage, MAX_HUB_TO_PIPE, MAX_PIPE_TO_HUB, type RefusedMsg, type RelayReplacedMsg } from '../link/messages.ts'
import { writeFileDurable } from '../native.ts'
import { MAX_SOCKET_PATH_BYTES, socketPathOk, type NuancePaths } from '../paths.ts'
import { TIMING } from '../timing.ts'
import { listenPrivate, Outbox } from './unix.ts'

export interface RelayTimers { setInterval(fn: () => void, ms: number): unknown; clearInterval(h: unknown): void }
export interface RelayDeps { paths: NuancePaths; nonce: string; stdin: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>; write(bytes: Uint8Array): void;
  mono(): number; ledger(f: LedgerFields): void; timers?: RelayTimers; staleMs?: number; exitMs?: number; inodeCheckMs?: number;
  stderr?: { write(s: string): void } }
export interface RelayStatusFile { pid: number; started_mono: number; last_ping_mono: number | null; streams: number }

/** A relay that cannot listen exits like a refused gate command, before its preamble, so the dialer says needs Yu: config (§5.4). */
export const RELAY_START_REFUSED = 64

const realTimers: RelayTimers = {
  setInterval: (fn, ms) => setInterval(fn, ms),
  clearInterval: (h) => clearInterval(h as ReturnType<typeof setInterval>),
}

const HUB_AWAY: RefusedMsg = { t: 'refused', code: 'hub_away' }
const REPLACED: RelayReplacedMsg = { t: 'relay_replaced' }

const isMono = (v: unknown): v is number => typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v) && v >= 0

/** run/relay.json, written at start and on every PING; `collab-bridge status` reads it (its readings are CLOCK_MONOTONIC, system-wide). */
export function readRelayStatus(paths: NuancePaths): RelayStatusFile | null {
  let o: unknown
  try { o = JSON.parse(readFileSync(paths.relayStatus, 'utf8')) } catch { return null }
  if (typeof o !== 'object' || o === null || Array.isArray(o)) return null
  const { pid, started_mono, last_ping_mono, streams } = o as Record<string, unknown>
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(pid) || (pid as number) < 2 || !isMono(started_mono)) return null
  if (last_ping_mono !== null && !isMono(last_ping_mono)) return null
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(streams) || (streams as number) < 0) return null
  return { pid: pid as number, started_mono, last_ping_mono, streams: streams as number }
}

function inodeOf(path: string): bigint | null {
  try { return lstatSync(path, { bigint: true }).ino } catch { return null }
}

interface Conn { id: number; out: Outbox; decoder: FrameDecoder }

export async function runRelay(deps: RelayDeps): Promise<number> {
  const { paths } = deps
  const staleMs = deps.staleMs ?? TIMING.staleMs
  const exitMs = deps.exitMs ?? TIMING.relayExitMs
  const inodeCheckMs = deps.inodeCheckMs ?? TIMING.inodeCheckMs
  const timers = deps.timers ?? realTimers
  const started = deps.mono()
  const note = (f: LedgerFields) => { try { deps.ledger(f) } catch { /* the relay runs without its ledger */ } }
  const say = (line: string) => { try { deps.stderr?.write(`collab-bridge relay: ${line}\n`) } catch { /* nothing more to do */ } }
  const refuse = (code: string, line: string): number => {
    note({ event: 'relay', outcome: 'refused', code })
    say(line)
    return RELAY_START_REFUSED
  }

  // listenPrivate binds a name only this process uses, then renames it over hub.sock: listening on a path that exists
  // fails with EADDRINUSE, and a socket file outlives SIGKILL (F8), so a stale hub.sock never stops a new relay (Review
  // Focus 5, P17). The name it binds is checked here, so a long path refuses with this relay's own code (P16).
  const fresh = `${paths.hubSock}.${process.pid}`
  if (!socketPathOk(fresh)) return refuse('socket_path_too_long', `${fresh} is longer than ${MAX_SOCKET_PATH_BYTES} bytes (K46)`)

  const conns = new Map<number, Conn>()
  let lastPing: number | null = null
  let finished = false
  let resolveDone!: (code: number) => void
  const done = new Promise<number>((r) => { resolveDone = r })
  const mux = new Mux({ write: (b) => deps.write(b), maxInbound: MAX_HUB_TO_PIPE })
  const lastHeard = () => lastPing ?? started   // until the first PING, the hub has just dialled: count from the start

  const closeConn = (c: Conn, o: { hub: boolean; local: boolean }) => {
    if (conns.get(c.id) !== c) return
    conns.delete(c.id)
    if (o.hub) mux.close(c.id)
    if (o.local) c.out.push(encodeFrame(FRAME_TYPE.CLOSE, 0))
    c.out.endWhenFlushed()
  }

  /** A pipe speaks on stream 0 only; the relay renumbers its frames to the connection's stream toward the hub. */
  const fromPipe = (c: Conn, f: Frame) => {
    if (conns.get(c.id) !== c) return
    if (f.stream !== 0) return closeConn(c, { hub: true, local: true })
    if (f.type === FRAME_TYPE.DATA) mux.data(c.id, f.payload)
    else if (f.type === FRAME_TYPE.CLOSE) closeConn(c, { hub: true, local: false })
    // OPEN, PING and PONG from a pipe mean nothing here.
  }

  const fromHub = (f: Frame) => {
    if (f.type === FRAME_TYPE.PING) {
      lastPing = deps.mono()
      mux.pong()
      const copy = encodeFrame(FRAME_TYPE.PING, 0)
      for (const c of conns.values()) c.out.push(copy)
      writeStatus()
      return
    }
    const c = f.stream === 0 ? undefined : conns.get(f.stream)
    if (!c) return   // a stream that is already closed, or the hub's stream 0 (it opens no streams and sends no PONG)
    if (f.type === FRAME_TYPE.DATA) c.out.push(encodeFrame(FRAME_TYPE.DATA, 0, f.payload))
    else if (f.type === FRAME_TYPE.CLOSE) closeConn(c, { hub: false, local: true })
  }

  const writeStatus = () => {
    const s: RelayStatusFile = { pid: process.pid, started_mono: started, last_ping_mono: lastPing, streams: conns.size }
    try { writeFileDurable(paths.relayStatus, JSON.stringify(s) + '\n', 0o600) } catch { /* status only */ }
  }

  let server: { stop(closeActiveConnections?: boolean): void }
  let ours: bigint | null
  try {
    mkdirSync(paths.run, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
    chmodSync(paths.run, 0o700)   // a mode passed to mkdir applies only to a new dir, and the umask cuts it
    const l = listenPrivate<Conn | null>(paths.hubSock, {
      open(sock) {
        const c: Conn = { id: 0, out: new Outbox(sock), decoder: new FrameDecoder(MAX_PIPE_TO_HUB) }
        sock.data = c
        if (finished) { sock.end(); return }
        if (deps.mono() - lastHeard() > staleMs) {
          // §5.3: no new call goes into a stale link. The pipe answers its agent hub_away, a definite "not sent".
          c.out.push(encodeFrame(FRAME_TYPE.DATA, 0, encodeMessage(HUB_AWAY)))
          c.out.push(encodeFrame(FRAME_TYPE.CLOSE, 0))
          c.out.endWhenFlushed()
          return
        }
        c.id = mux.open()
        conns.set(c.id, c)
      },
      data(sock, chunk) {
        const c = sock.data
        if (!c || conns.get(c.id) !== c) return
        let frames: Frame[]
        try {
          frames = c.decoder.push(chunk)
        } catch (e) {
          // Over 2 MiB, or not a frame at all: forward what came before it, then close this connection only (§6.6).
          if (!(e instanceof FrameTooLarge) && !(e instanceof FrameMalformed)) throw e
          for (const f of e.frames) fromPipe(c, f)
          return closeConn(c, { hub: true, local: true })
        }
        for (const f of frames) fromPipe(c, f)
      },
      drain(sock) { sock.data?.out.drain() },
      close(sock) { if (sock.data) closeConn(sock.data, { hub: true, local: false }) },
      error(sock) { if (sock.data) closeConn(sock.data, { hub: true, local: false }) },
    }, { replace: true })
    server = l.server
    ours = l.ino
  } catch (e) {
    return refuse('bind_failed', `cannot listen on ${paths.hubSock}: ${e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)}`)
  }

  deps.write(new TextEncoder().encode(preambleOf(deps.nonce)))
  note({ event: 'relay', outcome: 'start' })
  writeStatus()
  const reader = deps.stdin.getReader()

  const finish = (reason: string, code: number) => {
    if (finished) return
    finished = true
    timers.clearInterval(liveness)
    timers.clearInterval(inodeCheck)
    for (const c of conns.values()) { c.out.push(encodeFrame(FRAME_TYPE.CLOSE, 0)); c.out.endWhenFlushed() }
    conns.clear()
    server.stop(true)   // unlinks only the name it bound, which the rename already moved
    if (ours !== null && inodeOf(paths.hubSock) === ours) { try { unlinkSync(paths.hubSock) } catch { /* gone */ } }
    const s = readRelayStatus(paths)
    if (s && s.pid === process.pid && s.started_mono === started) { try { unlinkSync(paths.relayStatus) } catch { /* gone */ } }
    note({ event: 'relay', outcome: 'exit', code: reason, ms: Math.max(0, Math.round(deps.mono() - started)) })
    reader.cancel().catch(() => { /* already closed */ })
    resolveDone(code)
  }

  const liveness = timers.setInterval(() => {
    if (!finished && deps.mono() - lastHeard() > exitMs) finish('no_ping', 0)
  }, Math.max(1, Math.min(1000, Math.floor(exitMs / 45))))

  const inodeCheck = timers.setInterval(() => {
    if (finished || inodeOf(paths.hubSock) === ours) return
    // A newer relay put its own socket in place (§5.3): tell this link's hub, which counts these for relay_contested (T5).
    mux.data(0, encodeMessage(REPLACED))
    finish('relay_replaced', 0)
  }, inodeCheckMs)

  void (async () => {
    try {
      for (;;) {
        const { done: eof, value } = await reader.read()
        if (finished) return
        if (eof) return finish('stdin_eof', 0)
        if (!value || value.byteLength === 0) continue
        let frames: Frame[]
        try {
          frames = mux.feed(value)
        } catch (e) {
          if (e instanceof FrameTooLarge) {
            // Over 4 MiB from the hub: the decoder skips that payload; close that one stream (§6.6).
            for (const f of e.frames) fromHub(f)
            const c = conns.get(e.stream)
            if (c) closeConn(c, { hub: true, local: true })
            continue
          }
          if (e instanceof FrameMalformed) {
            for (const f of e.frames) fromHub(f)
            return finish('hub_malformed', 1)
          }
          throw e
        }
        for (const f of frames) fromHub(f)
      }
    } catch {
      finish('stdin_error', 0)
    }
  })()

  return done
}
```

Notes for the implementer:
- Exit codes of the gate: 0 answered (hello, a clean relay end); 64 refused (`GATE_REFUSED_EXIT`: not one of the three forms, an unset command, hello without a complete install, an upload-pack form without INSTALLED, a relay that cannot listen); an upload-pack form that reaches git exits with git's code (Task 21); 1 a relay whose hub sent a malformed frame. `main.ts` adds 2 for usage and 70 for an unexpected throw.
- stdout: measured on this Air, `process.stdout.write(<8 MiB>); process.exit(0)` delivered 65536 bytes, and an empty write's callback fires at once; waiting for the last non-empty write's callback delivered all of it. So `main.ts` keeps the promise of the last write's callback and waits for it (at most 2 s) before `process.exit`: hello's line and the relay's last frames (its `relay_replaced` note to the hub) depend on it.
- hello's user is `passwdOfSelf().name` (getpwuid, Task 13), never `$USER` (F3). `buildHello` gets `systemBin('zsh', env)`: `/bin/zsh` in production, the suite's knob under the override.

```ts
// The installed "Nuance" home that the gate, fetch, mirror, pipe and install tests start from. This file is a fixture and
// is never named *.test.ts (Summon ruling R1). It provides INSTALLED, shares.json naming one share, and the Summon
// allowlist that grants it, plus the recorded git and a repo with a hidden branch. Later tasks import these helpers
// instead of building the INSTALLED literal, the allowlist YAML and the recorded git again in each test file.
import { mkdirSync, realpathSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { dirname, isAbsolute, join } from 'node:path'
import type { AllowlistFolder } from '../src/allowlist.ts'
import { hasLazyFetchGuard, parseGitVersion, sha256File, type ResolvedGit } from '../src/nuance/git-resolve.ts'
import { renderInstalled, writeShares, type InstalledInfo } from '../src/nuance/installed.ts'
import { writeSeatKeyIfAbsent } from '../src/nuance/seatkey.ts'
import { nuancePaths, type NuancePaths } from '../src/paths.ts'
import { temp, testEnv } from './helpers.ts'

/** The Air's Homebrew git: a symlink into the Cellar, which is what the suite's git knob points at too. */
const HOMEBREW_GIT = '/opt/homebrew/bin/git'
/** Fixture git runs with no system or global config and no prompts. */
const FIXTURE_GIT_ENV = { PATH: '/usr/bin:/bin', GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: '1', GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: '/dev/null', GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0', LC_ALL: 'C' }

let recorded: ResolvedGit | null = null

/**
 * The Air's git standing in for "Nuance's recorded git": the Cellar realpath of /opt/homebrew/bin/git, with its version,
 * sha256 and guard, recorded the way `install check` records a Terminal git (Task 20). It is computed once per test file.
 */
export function recordedGit(): ResolvedGit {
  if (recorded) return recorded
  const path = realpathSync(HOMEBREW_GIT)
  const v = parseGitVersion(Bun.spawnSync([path, '--version'], { env: FIXTURE_GIT_ENV }).stdout.toString())
  if (!v) throw new Error(`recordedGit: ${path} --version printed no git version line`)
  recorded = { path, version: v.version, sha256: sha256File(path), guard: hasLazyFetchGuard(path), apple: v.apple }
  return recorded
}

/** An INSTALLED record: fixed fixture values with `o` laid over them. The git is `o.git` when given, else recordedGit(), so the real git is read only when no git is passed. */
export function testInstalled(o: Partial<InstalledInfo> = {}): InstalledInfo {
  return {
    device: 'nuance', build: 'abcdef01', prepared: '20261013120000', expiry: '20270111', binary_sha256: 'a'.repeat(64),
    tools_seed: 'b'.repeat(64), summon_key_sha256: 'c'.repeat(64), summon_dropin_stat: '1 2 3 0 600',
    claude_version: '2.1.296 (Claude Code)', installed_at: '2026-10-13T12:00:00.000Z',
    ...o,
    git: o.git ?? recordedGit(),
  }
}

/** A Summon allowlist for device nuance in Summon's grammar (Task 17's parser reads it), granting these folders. */
export function allowlistYaml(folders: AllowlistFolder[]): string {
  return [
    'version: 1', 'device: nuance', 'peers: [air]',
    'runtimes:', '  - id: claude', '    models:', '      - model: sonnet',
    'folders:', ...folders.flatMap((f) => [`  - path: ${f.path}`, `    access: ${f.access}`]),
    'limits:', '  max_concurrent: 1', '  starts_per_hour: 6', '  job_timeout_max: 30m', '',
  ].join('\n')
}

/** Yu's Y1 grant: ~/Projects is review-only and ~/Projects/collab-trial is edit (spec §10.1). */
const TRIAL_FOLDERS: AllowlistFolder[] = [{ path: '~/Projects', access: 'review' }, { path: '~/Projects/collab-trial', access: 'edit' }]

export interface InstalledNuanceHome { home: string; env: Record<string, string>; paths: NuancePaths; share: string; installed: InstalledInfo }

/**
 * A temp "Nuance" home with the files `install write` leaves for the fetch gate:
 * - INSTALLED: testInstalled() with `installed` and then `git` laid over it.
 * - shares.json: one entry for `<home>/<share>` and its `.git`.
 * - the Summon allowlist: `folders`, or TRIAL_FOLDERS when none are given.
 * `share` is a path relative to the home. The caller creates the repo there.
 * `env` is testEnv(home) and `paths` is built from that env, so the Summon drop-in and the socket root are inside temp
 * dirs. `env` is also what a fake ssh should hand the gate.
 */
export function installedNuanceHome(o: { share: string; folders?: AllowlistFolder[]; git?: ResolvedGit; installed?: Partial<InstalledInfo> }): InstalledNuanceHome {
  if (isAbsolute(o.share)) throw new Error(`installedNuanceHome: share is relative to the home, not ${o.share}`)
  const home = temp('cb-nuance-')
  const env = testEnv(home)
  const paths = nuancePaths(home, env)
  const share = join(home, o.share)
  const installed = testInstalled({ ...o.installed, ...(o.git ? { git: o.git } : {}) })
  mkdirSync(dirname(paths.installed), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
  writeFileSync(paths.installed, renderInstalled(installed), { mode: 0o600 })
  writeShares(paths, [{ realpath: share, gitdir: join(share, '.git') }])
  mkdirSync(dirname(paths.summonAllowlist), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
  writeFileSync(paths.summonAllowlist, allowlistYaml(o.folders ?? TRIAL_FOLDERS))
  return { home, env, paths, share, installed }
}

/** Runs git with no system or global config and HOME=home. It throws, with git's stderr, on a non-zero exit, and returns stdout trimmed. */
export function fixtureGit(args: string[], home: string): string {
  const r = Bun.spawnSync([HOMEBREW_GIT, ...args], { env: { ...FIXTURE_GIT_ENV, HOME: home }, stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'pipe' })
  if (r.exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(`git ${args.join(' ')}: ${r.stderr.toString()}`)
  return r.stdout.toString().trim()
}

function commit(repo: string, home: string, file: string, text: string, message: string): string {
  mkdirSync(join(repo, file, '..'), { recursive: true })
  writeFileSync(join(repo, file), text)
  fixtureGit(['-C', repo, 'add', file], home)
  fixtureGit(['-C', repo, '-c', 'user.name=t', '-c', 'user.email=t@t.invalid', 'commit', '-q', '-m', message], home)
  return fixtureGit(['-C', repo, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'], home)
}

/**
 * A repo at `dir` with one commit on main and one commit only on refs/heads/secret, checked out at main. K49 needs this:
 * the gate advertises only HEAD, so `secret` is a commit that a client may want but must never get.
 */
export function secretBranchRepo(dir: string, home: string): { head: string; secret: string } {
  mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true })
  fixtureGit(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', dir], home)
  const head = commit(dir, home, 'README.md', 'trial\n', 'one')
  fixtureGit(['-C', dir, 'checkout', '-q', '-b', 'secret'], home)
  const secret = commit(dir, home, 'secret.txt', 'hidden\n', 'secret')
  fixtureGit(['-C', dir, 'checkout', '-q', 'main'], home)
  return { head, secret }
}

/**
 * What `install write` leaves for hello (Task 56 makes the real one): INSTALLED (testInstalled with a fixed recorded git
 * the gate never runs for hello), the seat key, shares.json naming ~/Projects/collab-trial, an authorized_keys with a
 * ` summon-air` line and the Summon drop-in. Returns the seat public key as hello prints it. Added by Task 24; Task 58
 * uses it for the compiled gate.
 */
export function installForHello(paths: NuancePaths): string {
  mkdirSync(dirname(paths.installed), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
  writeFileSync(paths.installed, renderInstalled(testInstalled({
    build: '0a1b2c3d', summon_key_sha256: 'd'.repeat(64), summon_dropin_stat: '1 2 3 4 600',
    git: { path: '/opt/homebrew/bin/git', version: '2.52.0', sha256: 'c'.repeat(64), guard: true, apple: false },
  })), { mode: 0o600 })
  const { publicHex } = writeSeatKeyIfAbsent(paths)
  const share = join(paths.home, 'Projects', 'collab-trial')
  writeShares(paths, [{ realpath: share, gitdir: join(share, '.git') }])
  mkdirSync(dirname(paths.authorizedKeys), { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
  writeFileSync(paths.authorizedKeys, 'restrict,command="/x/summon-gatekeeper" ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIA summon-air\n')
  mkdirSync(dirname(paths.summonDropin), { recursive: true })
  writeFileSync(paths.summonDropin, 'PasswordAuthentication no\n')
  return publicHex
}
```

```ts
/** The Air's git as the fetching client (Task 21's recordedGit: the Cellar realpath of /opt/homebrew/bin/git). */
const GIT = recordedGit().path
/** Fixture git runs with no system or global config and no prompts (as Task 21's fixtureGit). */
const GIT_ENV = { PATH: '/usr/bin:/bin', GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM: '1', GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL: '/dev/null', GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT: '0', LC_ALL: 'C' }
const UNADVERTISED = /not our ref|Server does not allow request for unadvertised object/
/** pkt-line framing for a raw upload-pack conversation. */
const pkt = (s: string) => `${(4 + Buffer.byteLength(s)).toString(16).padStart(4, '0')}${s}`

/** An installed Nuance home (Task 21) whose share holds a repo with a hidden branch, behind the fake ssh and the real gate entry. */
function uploadWorld() {
  const h = installedNuanceHome({ share: join('Projects', 'collab-trial') })
  const { head, secret } = secretBranchRepo(h.share, h.home)
  const fake = makeFakeSsh({ nuanceHome: h.home, target: gateFromSource(), env: h.env })
  return { h, fake, gitdir: join(h.share, '.git'), head, secret }
}

/** The Air side: `git fetch collab-nuance:<path> <refspec>` into a fresh repo through the fake ssh, as the hub's mirror sync does. */
function fetchThrough(fake: FakeSsh, remotePath: string, refspec: string, protocol: 0 | 2) {
  const air = temp('cb-air-')
  git(['init', '-q', '-b', 'main', air], air)
  const r = Bun.spawnSync([GIT, '-C', air, '-c', `protocol.version=${protocol}`, 'fetch', '--no-tags', '--no-write-fetch-head',
    `collab-nuance:${remotePath}`, refspec], {
    cwd: '/', env: { ...GIT_ENV, HOME: air, GIT_SSH_COMMAND: `'${fake.bin}'` }, stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'pipe', timeout: 30_000,
  })
  return { code: r.exitCode, stderr: r.stderr.toString(), air }
}

/** One raw upload-pack conversation through an ssh: what git would send, and every byte that came back. */
function rawUploadPack(bin: string, command: string, request: string, env: Record<string, string> = {}) {
  const r = Bun.spawnSync([bin, 'collab-nuance', command], { stdin: Buffer.from(request), stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'pipe', env: { PATH: '/usr/bin:/bin', ...env } })
  return { code: r.exitCode, out: r.stdout.toString('latin1') }
}

describe('upload-pack through the fake ssh and the real gate entry (§12.1 Git transfer)', () => {
  test('a v0 fetch through the gate gets HEAD', () => {
    const w = uploadWorld()
    const r = fetchThrough(w.fake, w.gitdir, '+HEAD:refs/collab/nuance/macair/0000000000000000/incoming', 0)
    expect([r.code, r.stderr]).toEqual([0, expect.any(String)])
    expect(git(['-C', r.air, 'rev-parse', 'refs/collab/nuance/macair/0000000000000000/incoming'], r.air)).toBe(w.head)
    // The fake ssh got git's own form of the command (K48), and the gate ledgered it as served.
    expect(w.fake.calls().at(-1)!.at(-1)).toBe(`git-upload-pack '${w.gitdir}'`)
    expect(gateLines(w.h.paths).map((e) => [e.form, e.outcome])).toEqual([['upload-pack', 'served']])
  }, 30_000)

  test('a git client asking for a hidden commit gets nothing, and the raw want is refused by upload-pack (K49)', () => {
    const w = uploadWorld()
    const r = fetchThrough(w.fake, w.gitdir, w.secret, 0)
    expect(r.code).not.toBe(0)
    expect(r.stderr).toMatch(UNADVERTISED)
    expect(Bun.spawnSync([GIT, '-C', r.air, 'cat-file', '-e', w.secret], { cwd: '/', env: { ...GIT_ENV, HOME: r.air } }).exitCode).not.toBe(0)
    // The client check above is git's own; this raw want shows the gate's upload-pack refuses it too.
    const raw = rawUploadPack(w.fake.bin, `git-upload-pack '${w.gitdir}'`, pkt(`want ${w.secret} multi_ack\n`) + '0000' + pkt('done\n'))
    expect(raw.out).toContain(' HEAD\0')                       // only HEAD is advertised (hideRefs=refs/)
    expect(raw.out).not.toMatch(/[0-9a-f]{40} refs\//)         // and no ref under refs/
    expect(raw.out).toContain(`ERR upload-pack: not our ref ${w.secret}`)
    expect(raw.code).toBe(128)                                  // the gate exits with git's code
  }, 30_000)

  test('an sshd that forwards GIT_PROTOCOL=version=2 changes nothing: the gate scrubs it and upload-pack speaks v0', () => {
    const w = uploadWorld()
    w.fake.setPassGitProtocol(true)
    // Control: the same kind of fake ssh in front of a bare upload-pack hands it GIT_PROTOCOL, and it answers in v2.
    const bare = makeFakeSsh({ nuanceHome: w.h.home, target: [GIT, 'upload-pack', '--strict', w.gitdir], env: w.h.env })
    bare.setPassGitProtocol(true)
    expect(rawUploadPack(bare.bin, 'git-upload-pack', '0000', { GIT_PROTOCOL: 'version=2' }).out.startsWith('000eversion 2\n')).toBe(true)
    // Through the gate the same request gets the v0 advertisement: upload-pack never saw GIT_PROTOCOL.
    const raw = rawUploadPack(w.fake.bin, `git-upload-pack '${w.gitdir}'`, '0000', { GIT_PROTOCOL: 'version=2' })
    expect(raw.out.startsWith('000eversion 2')).toBe(false)
    expect(raw.out).toContain(' HEAD\0')
    // A v2-asking client still cannot fetch the hidden commit, and still fetches HEAD.
    const hidden = fetchThrough(w.fake, w.gitdir, w.secret, 2)
    expect(hidden.code).not.toBe(0)
    expect(hidden.stderr).toMatch(UNADVERTISED)
    expect(fetchThrough(w.fake, w.gitdir, '+HEAD:refs/collab/t/incoming', 2).code).toBe(0)
  }, 30_000)

  test('the work-tree path is refused: shares.json lists only the gitdir', async () => {
    const w = uploadWorld()
    const r = fetchThrough(w.fake, w.h.share, '+HEAD:refs/collab/t/incoming', 0)
    expect(r.code).toBe(128)
    expect(r.stderr).toContain('remote error: not_shared')
    // git exits on the ERR line without waiting for its ssh, so the gate's ledger line may land a moment later.
    const end = Date.now() + 5_000
    while (gateLines(w.h.paths).length === 0 && Date.now() < end) await Bun.sleep(20)
    expect(gateLines(w.h.paths).map((e) => [e.form, e.outcome])).toEqual([['upload-pack', 'not_shared']])
  }, 30_000)
})
```

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test'
import { existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { pipeRecordName, readPipeRecords, writePipeRecord, type PipeRecord } from '../src/nuance/pipe-record.ts'
import type { RelayStatusFile } from '../src/nuance/relay.ts'
import { nuanceStatus, renderNuanceStatus } from '../src/nuance/status.ts'
import { nuancePaths, type NuancePaths } from '../src/paths.ts'
import { cleanupTmps, modeOf, PKG, shortSockRoot, temp, testEnv } from './helpers.ts'

afterEach(cleanupTmps)

function nuance(): NuancePaths {
  const home = temp('cb-status-')
  return nuancePaths(home, { HOME: home, COLLAB_BRIDGE_HOME_OVERRIDE: home, COLLAB_BRIDGE_SOCK_ROOT: shortSockRoot(), COLLAB_BRIDGE_SUMMON_DROPIN: join(home, 'dropin') })
}

function writeRelayJson(paths: NuancePaths, s: RelayStatusFile): void {
  mkdirSync(paths.run, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
  writeFileSync(paths.relayStatus, JSON.stringify(s) + '\n')
}

/** A pid that has exited and been reaped, so kill(pid, 0) answers ESRCH. */
function deadPid(): number {
  return Bun.spawnSync(['/usr/bin/true']).pid
}

const rec = (host: number, pipe: number, o: Partial<PipeRecord> = {}): PipeRecord => ({
  v: 1, host_pid: host, host_lstart: 'Wed Oct 7 16:22:59 2026', pipe_pid: pipe, lineage: `lin_${'0'.repeat(32)}`, state: 'ready', refused: null, ...o,
})

const runMain = (args: string[], home: string) =>
  Bun.spawnSync([process.execPath, '--no-env-file', '--config=/dev/null', `${PKG}/src/nuance/main.ts`, ...args], { env: testEnv(home), cwd: '/' })

describe('collab-bridge status', () => {
  test('none, up and stale from relay.json', () => {
    const paths = nuance()
    const none = nuanceStatus(paths, () => 50_000)
    expect(none).toEqual({ relay: 'none', stale_since_mono: null, last_ping_age_s: null, pipes: 0, refused: [] })
    expect(renderNuanceStatus(none, 50_000)).toEqual(['relay: none', 'last PING: none', 'pipes attached: 0'])

    writeRelayJson(paths, { pid: process.pid, started_mono: 1_000, last_ping_mono: 30_000, streams: 1 })
    const up = nuanceStatus(paths, () => 35_000)
    expect(up).toEqual({ relay: 'up', stale_since_mono: null, last_ping_age_s: 5, pipes: 0, refused: [] })
    expect(renderNuanceStatus(up, 35_000)).toEqual(['relay: up', 'last PING: 5 s ago', 'pipes attached: 0'])
    expect(nuanceStatus(paths, () => 50_000).relay).toBe('up')   // exactly 20 s is not yet stale (§5.3: more than 20 s)

    const stale = nuanceStatus(paths, () => 80_000)
    expect(stale).toEqual({ relay: 'stale', stale_since_mono: 50_000, last_ping_age_s: 50, pipes: 0, refused: [] })
    expect(renderNuanceStatus(stale, 80_000)).toEqual(['relay: stale since 30s', 'last PING: 50 s ago', 'pipes attached: 0'])

    writeRelayJson(paths, { pid: process.pid, started_mono: 1_000, last_ping_mono: null, streams: 0 })
    expect(nuanceStatus(paths, () => 6_000)).toEqual({ relay: 'up', stale_since_mono: null, last_ping_age_s: null, pipes: 0, refused: [] })
    expect(nuanceStatus(paths, () => 21_001)).toMatchObject({ relay: 'stale', stale_since_mono: 21_000 })

    writeRelayJson(paths, { pid: deadPid(), started_mono: 1_000, last_ping_mono: 30_000, streams: 1 })
    expect(nuanceStatus(paths, () => 35_000).relay).toBe('none')
  })

  test('counts ready pipes and lists refused codes', () => {
    const paths = nuance()
    writePipeRecord(paths, rec(4100, process.pid))
    writePipeRecord(paths, rec(4101, process.pid))
    writePipeRecord(paths, rec(4102, process.pid, { state: 'connecting', refused: 'seat_proof_failed' }))
    writePipeRecord(paths, rec(4103, process.pid, { state: 'stopped', lineage: null, refused: 'seat_session_ended' }))
    writePipeRecord(paths, rec(4104, process.pid, { state: 'detached', refused: 'seat_proof_failed' }))
    writePipeRecord(paths, rec(4105, deadPid(), { refused: 'lineage_cap' }))
    const s = nuanceStatus(paths, () => 1)
    expect(s.pipes).toBe(2)
    expect(s.refused).toEqual(['seat_proof_failed', 'seat_session_ended'])
    expect(renderNuanceStatus(s, 1)).toEqual(['relay: none', 'last PING: none', 'pipes attached: 2', 'refused: seat_proof_failed, seat_session_ended'])
  })

  test('collab-bridge status prints its three lines and exits 0', () => {
    const home = temp('cb-status-main-')
    const p = runMain(['status'], home)
    expect(p.stderr.toString()).toBe('')
    expect(p.exitCode).toBe(0)
    expect(p.stdout.toString()).toBe('relay: none\nlast PING: none\npipes attached: 0\n')
  })

  test('an unknown verb exits 2 with the usage line', () => {
    const home = temp('cb-status-main-')
    const p = runMain(['bogus'], home)
    expect(p.exitCode).toBe(2)
    expect(p.stdout.toString()).toBe('')
    expect(p.stderr.toString()).toStartWith('usage: collab-bridge ')
    expect(p.stderr.toString().split('\n')).toHaveLength(2)
    expect(runMain(['status', 'extra'], home).exitCode).toBe(2)
  })
})

describe('pipe records', () => {
  test('a pipe record round-trips and is 0600', () => {
    const paths = nuance()
    const r = rec(4100, process.pid)
```

```ts
// The `pipes/<host_pid>-<pipe_pid>.json` record (spec §8 item 1): a pipe writes it beside its tap socket (Task 31), the
// tap reads it to find its own pipe (Task 32), and `collab-bridge status` counts it. It holds no secret: two pids, the
// host's start time, the lineage id (not a secret, §6.1), the link state and the latest refusal code.
import { chmodSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { LINEAGE_RE } from '../link/messages.ts'
import { writeFileDurable } from '../native.ts'
import type { NuancePaths } from '../paths.ts'
import { pidAlive } from '../proc.ts'

export interface PipeRecord { v: 1; host_pid: number; host_lstart: string; pipe_pid: number; lineage: string | null; state: string; refused: string | null }

const NAME_RE = /^([1-9][0-9]{0,9})-([1-9][0-9]{0,9})\.json$/
const LSTART_RE = /^[\x20-\x7e]{1,64}$/
const WORD_RE = /^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$/   // a link state or a refusal code
const isPid = (v: unknown): v is number => Number.isSafeInteger(v) && (v as number) > 1

export function pipeRecordName(hostPid: number, pipePid: number): string {
  return `${hostPid}-${pipePid}`
}

/** Null unless every field is present and well-formed; keys this build does not know are dropped. */
export function parsePipeRecord(text: string): PipeRecord | null {
  let o: unknown
  try { o = JSON.parse(text) } catch { return null }
  if (typeof o !== 'object' || o === null || Array.isArray(o)) return null
  const r = o as Record<string, unknown>
  if (r.v !== 1 || !isPid(r.host_pid) || !isPid(r.pipe_pid)) return null
  if (typeof r.host_lstart !== 'string' || !LSTART_RE.test(r.host_lstart)) return null
  if (r.lineage !== null && (typeof r.lineage !== 'string' || !LINEAGE_RE.test(r.lineage))) return null
  if (typeof r.state !== 'string' || !WORD_RE.test(r.state)) return null
  if (r.refused !== null && (typeof r.refused !== 'string' || !WORD_RE.test(r.refused))) return null
  return { v: 1, host_pid: r.host_pid, host_lstart: r.host_lstart, pipe_pid: r.pipe_pid,
    lineage: r.lineage as string | null, state: r.state, refused: r.refused as string | null }
}

/** Replaces the record whole (temp file, F_FULLFSYNC, rename), 0600 in the 0700 pipes dir; a malformed record is never written. */
export function writePipeRecord(paths: NuancePaths, r: PipeRecord): void {
  const text = JSON.stringify({ v: 1, host_pid: r.host_pid, host_lstart: r.host_lstart, pipe_pid: r.pipe_pid, lineage: r.lineage, state: r.state, refused: r.refused })
  if (!parsePipeRecord(text)) throw new Error(`pipe record ${pipeRecordName(r.host_pid, r.pipe_pid)} is malformed`)
  mkdirSync(paths.pipes, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
  chmodSync(paths.pipes, 0o700)
  writeFileDurable(paths.pipeJson(r.host_pid, r.pipe_pid), text + '\n', 0o600)
}

/**
 * Every record whose file name matches its own host_pid and pipe_pid and whose pipe is alive (P61: kill(pid, 0), because
 * a SIGKILLed pipe's files outlive it, F8). Dead records are skipped, never deleted here: a starting pipe removes its own
 * host's (Task 31). Sorted by host pid, then pipe pid.
 */
export function readPipeRecords(paths: NuancePaths, alive: (pid: number) => boolean = pidAlive): PipeRecord[] {
  let names: string[]
  try { names = readdirSync(paths.pipes) } catch { return [] }
  const out: PipeRecord[] = []
  for (const name of names) {
    const m = NAME_RE.exec(name)
    if (!m) continue
    let text: string
    try { text = readFileSync(join(paths.pipes, name), 'utf8') } catch { continue }
    const r = parsePipeRecord(text)
    if (!r || r.host_pid !== Number(m[1]) || r.pipe_pid !== Number(m[2]) || !alive(r.pipe_pid)) continue
    out.push(r)
  }
  return out.sort((a, b) => a.host_pid - b.host_pid || a.pipe_pid - b.pipe_pid)
}
```

```ts
// `collab-bridge status` on Nuance (C14): whether the relay is up, stale since when, or not there; how old its last PING
// is; how many pipes are attached, and any refusal a pipe holds (P29). Read-only: it connects to nothing, so it answers
// with the hub away and cannot disturb a live link. Ages compare CLOCK_MONOTONIC readings, which are system-wide (F13).
import { monoNowMs } from '../native.ts'
import type { NuancePaths } from '../paths.ts'
import { pidAlive } from '../proc.ts'
import { TIMING } from '../timing.ts'
import { readPipeRecords } from './pipe-record.ts'
import { readRelayStatus } from './relay.ts'

export interface NuanceStatus { relay: 'up' | 'stale' | 'none'; stale_since_mono: number | null; last_ping_age_s: number | null; pipes: number; refused: string[] }

export function nuanceStatus(paths: NuancePaths, mono: () => number, o: { staleMs?: number; alive?: (pid: number) => boolean } = {}): NuanceStatus {
  const staleMs = o.staleMs ?? TIMING.staleMs
  const alive = o.alive ?? pidAlive
  const records = readPipeRecords(paths, alive)
  const pipes = records.filter((r) => r.state === 'ready').length
  const refused = [...new Set(records.flatMap((r) => (r.refused === null ? [] : [r.refused])))].sort()
  const now = mono()
  const relay = readRelayStatus(paths)
  if (!relay || !alive(relay.pid)) return { relay: 'none', stale_since_mono: null, last_ping_age_s: null, pipes, refused }
  const lastPingAge = relay.last_ping_mono === null ? null : Math.max(0, Math.round((now - relay.last_ping_mono) / 1000))
  const heard = relay.last_ping_mono ?? relay.started_mono   // the relay's own rule: until the first PING, its start counts (§5.3)
  if (now - heard <= staleMs) return { relay: 'up', stale_since_mono: null, last_ping_age_s: lastPingAge, pipes, refused }
  return { relay: 'stale', stale_since_mono: heard + staleMs, last_ping_age_s: lastPingAge, pipes, refused }
}

export function renderNuanceStatus(s: NuanceStatus, nowMono: number = monoNowMs()): string[] {
  const relay = s.relay === 'stale' && s.stale_since_mono !== null
    ? `relay: stale since ${Math.max(0, Math.round((nowMono - s.stale_since_mono) / 1000))}s`
    : `relay: ${s.relay}`
  const out = [relay, s.last_ping_age_s === null ? 'last PING: none' : `last PING: ${s.last_ping_age_s} s ago`, `pipes attached: ${s.pipes}`]
  if (s.refused.length > 0) out.push(`refused: ${s.refused.join(', ')}`)
  return out
}
```
