```ts
// src/air/mirror.ts
export interface MirrorSpec { device: string; user: string; mirrorId: string; mirrorPath: string; airClone: string; remoteGitdir: string; caps: TreeCaps }
export interface MirrorDeps { git: GitRunner; sshBin: string; sshConfig: string; alias: string; freeBytes(path: string): number;
  fetchedToday(mirrorId: string): number; ledger(f: LedgerFields): void; wireCapBytes?: number; dailyBudgetBytes?: number;
  minFreeBytes?: number; fetchTimeoutMs?: number; checkoutTimeoutMs?: number }
export const WIRE_CAP_BYTES = 134_217_728, DAILY_BUDGET_BYTES = 1_073_741_824, MIN_FREE_BYTES = 5_368_709_120, FETCH_HEADROOM_BYTES = 134_217_728
export function mirrorIdOf(remoteRealpath: string): string      // sha256 hex [:16]
export function mirrorRefs(spec: MirrorSpec): { incoming: string; synced: string; task(taskId: string): string }
export function ulimitBlocks(bytes: number): number              // Math.floor(bytes / 1024) (P11)
export function fetchArgv(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: Pick<MirrorDeps, 'sshBin' | 'sshConfig' | 'alias' | 'git'>, wireCapBytes: number): string[]
//   ['/bin/sh', '-c', `ulimit -f ${ulimitBlocks(cap)}; exec "$@"`, 'sh', 'env', '-u', 'GIT_SSH', `GIT_SSH_COMMAND=${ssh} -F '${config}'`,
//    git, '-C', airClone, '-c', 'protocol.version=0', '-c', 'transfer.fsckObjects=true', '-c', 'fetch.fsckObjects=true',
//    '-c', 'transfer.unpackLimit=1', ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'fetch', '--no-tags', '--no-recurse-submodules', '--no-prune',
//    '--no-write-fetch-head', `${alias}:${remoteGitdir}`, `+HEAD:${incoming}`]
export class MirrorLock { run<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> }   // FIFO async mutex (P25)
export type SyncResult = { ok: true; oid: string; changed?: number } | { ok: false; code: AgentCode; message: string }
export function syncMirror(spec: MirrorSpec, o: { declaredHead: string; atComplete?: { base: string; scopes: readonly string[] } }, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<SyncResult>   // steps 1–9
export function createMirror(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<SyncResult>   // steps 2–4 and 6, repo_mismatch, worktree add --detach, lock, synced
//   before `worktree add`, mkdirSync(…, {recursive: true, mode: 0o700}) and chmodSync 0700 for collab-shared/, mirrors/,
//   mirrors/<device>/ and mirrors/<device>/<user>/: git would make them 0755, and Collab tightens the journal's parent only when
//   it created it (KN `src/store.ts:402-407`), so §4.3's 0700 would otherwise never hold
export function mirrorWorkspaceId(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: Pick<MirrorDeps, 'git'>): Promise<string | null>
//   Collab's K11 rule for this mirror's repository: realpath of `git -C <mirror> rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`
//   → `ws_` + sha256(`local-git:` + sha256(commonDir)).slice(0, 24) (KN `src/repository.ts:101-104`, `src/store.ts:1394-1401`;
//   the shared journal has one workspace per key, §6.3); null when git fails (P55)
export function liveMirrorDeps(o: { paths: AirPaths; git: GitRunner; ssh: string; alias: string }): MirrorDeps
//   freeBytes = statfsSync(path).bavail * bsize (air-env F17); fetchedToday = fetchedTodayFromLedger(paths.ledger, id, new Date());
//   ledger = appendLedger(paths.ledger, AIR_LEDGER_KEYS, …); sshConfig = paths.sshConfig
export function syncedOid(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<string | null>
export function mirrorHead(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<string | null>
export function writeTaskRef(spec: MirrorSpec, taskId: string, head: string, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<'ok' | 'mirror_tampered'>   // only when head === mirror HEAD; create-only
export function fetchedTodayFromLedger(ledgerPath: string, mirrorId: string, now: Date): number    // P31
//   each fetch appends {event:'fetch', device, user, code: mirrorId, bytes: <new .pack bytes>, outcome, ms}
```
- Also produced (this task's additions and the behaviour the comments above leave open; no signature changes):
  - `export function taskRefOk(id: string): boolean` — whether git can hold the id as one ref component. Collab task ids are `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*`, and git refuses `:`, `..` and a trailing `.` or `.lock` in a ref name. `mirrorRefs(spec).task(id)` throws for an id that fails it, and `mirrorRefs` throws when the device, user or mirror id would fail it.
  - `writeTaskRef` answers `mirror_tampered` when `head` is not a full oid or not the mirror's HEAD, and when the ref already holds another commit (the ref is left as it is). The same value again answers `ok` and writes nothing. For a task id that fails `taskRefOk`, it writes no ref and answers `ok`: the mirror is fine, and the reviewer reads the task's `result_checkpoint.head_sha` instead, which §7.7 names as the fallback when the ref is missing. Task 45 needs no special case.
  - `syncMirror` refuses a `declaredHead` that is not a full oid with `remote_head_moved` before fetching. A spec whose refs cannot be named is `mirror_tampered`, and a fetch command that cannot be built safely (`fetchArgv` throws on an ssh path with shell characters, a config path holding `'`, a bad alias, or a remote gitdir the gate's grammar would refuse) is `fetch_failed`. Neither function ever throws to its caller.
  - `createMirror` on a mirror path that already exists never deletes or re-adds it (`worktree_identity_changed`, K11). A healthy mirror (a real directory, a worktree of this clone, detached, clean, HEAD equal to `…/synced`) is kept, locked if it was not, and answered `{ok: true, oid: <synced>}` with no fetch, so a re-pin (re-pairing renews the key expiry, §5.1) is idempotent. Anything else is `mirror_tampered` for Ai.
  - `mirrorHead` answers null unless the mirror path is a real directory (never a symlink) that git sees as its own work-tree root, in the Air clone's repository. A plain directory would otherwise let git walk up to a parent repository and report that one's HEAD.

Notes for the implementer:
- **The fetch runs the real gate.** The fake ssh (Task 11) execs `gateFromSource()`, which is Task 24's gate entry: it runs Task 21's fetch gate and the real `git upload-pack` against the temp Nuance home. The world's Nuance home is Task 21's `installedNuanceHome({ share: 'Projects/collab-trial' })`: INSTALLED, with the Air's own git as "Nuance's recorded git" (`recordedGit()`, its Cellar realpath, as `install check` would record it), `shares.json`, and a Summon allowlist where `~/Projects` is review and `~/Projects/collab-trial` is edit; the test then makes the repo in the share. The fake's env is the home's `env` (`testEnv(home)`), so the gate reads its knobs under the override.
- **What the wire cap leaves behind** (measured on this Air with git 2.52 and `ulimit -f 1024`): the fetch fails with `fatal: fetch-pack: invalid index-pack output`, exit 128, and leaves `objects/pack/tmp_pack_XXXXXX` (mode 0444, cut at exactly the cap). So `syncMirror` removes the new `tmp_*` files of a failed fetch itself. Their bytes still go into the ledger line, so repeated over-cap fetches use up the day's budget. In-process, fetches into one Air clone are serialised (two devices sharing one repo in Phase 2 would otherwise count or remove each other's temporary packs). The per-mirror `MirrorLock` stays the caller's: Task 45 holds it from the sync until the forwarded call returns (§7.3, P25).
- **`includeIf "gitdir:<clone>/.git/worktrees/"` matches a linked worktree's own gitdir and not the clone's** (measured: `git config --show-scope --get-regexp` from the mirror shows `global filter.x.smudge cat`; from the clone, exit 1). So `createMirror` checks the clone's view (§7.3 step 2), adds the worktree with `--no-checkout`, checks the config again as the mirror sees it, and only then checks out. A refused new worktree is removed with `git worktree remove --force`: nothing can have bound to it, because it has no `…/synced` yet, and `.git/worktrees/<mirror_id>` goes with it, so a later attempt reuses the same name. The outcome is the spec's `worktree add --detach` at the fetched commit.
- **The filter check carries no `-c`.** `git -c core.fsmonitor=false config --show-scope --get-regexp '^core\.fsmonitor$'` prints `command core.fsmonitor false` (measured), so `MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS` on that one command would refuse every sync. Every other mirror and clone command carries them.
- `update-ref <ref> <new> ''` creates the ref only when it is absent (otherwise exit 128, `reference already exists`). `…/synced` and the tasks refs are created that way; a sync moves `…/synced` with the old value as compare-and-swap (§7.3 step 9).
- The tamper check counts ignored and untracked files (`status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all --ignored`), because `checkout -f` would clobber them without a word (T16). It also requires a detached HEAD (`symbolic-ref -q HEAD` exits 1), so a branch checked out in a mirror is caught.
- The workspace-id test starts real Collab sessions through `collabHarness` on `airPaths(<temp Air home>).sharedJournal`, a temp journal, never a real one. It also shows that an Air session in the clone lands in the same workspace as the mirror (§7.1: no explicit repository_key, one `local-git:` key).

`/Users/yuai/Projects/.worktrees/agenttool-collab-bridge/packages/collab-bridge/tests/mirror.test.ts`:

```ts
import { afterEach, describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test'
import { randomBytes } from 'node:crypto'
import { chmodSync, existsSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, readFileSync, realpathSync, rmSync, statfsSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
import { DEFAULT_CAPS, type TreeCaps } from '../src/air/diff-check.ts'
import { airGit, type GitRunner } from '../src/air/git.ts'
import {
  createMirror, DAILY_BUDGET_BYTES, FETCH_HEADROOM_BYTES, fetchArgv, fetchedTodayFromLedger, liveMirrorDeps, MIN_FREE_BYTES,
  MirrorLock, mirrorHead, mirrorIdOf, mirrorRefs, mirrorWorkspaceId, syncedOid, syncMirror, taskRefOk, ulimitBlocks, WIRE_CAP_BYTES,
  writeTaskRef, type MirrorDeps, type MirrorSpec,
} from '../src/air/mirror.ts'
import { AIR_LEDGER_KEYS, appendLedger, readLedger } from '../src/ledger.ts'
import { airPaths, type AirPaths } from '../src/paths.ts'
import { gateFromSource, makeFakeSsh, type FakeSsh } from './fake-ssh.ts'
import { cleanupTmps, commitFiles, makeRepo, modeOf, REAL_GIT, repoGit, temp } from './helpers.ts'
import { collabHarness } from './mcp-harness.ts'
import { installedNuanceHome } from './nuance-home.ts'

afterEach(cleanupTmps)

const T = 30_000 // every test here spawns git, the fake ssh and the source gate

interface World {
  air: string; paths: AirPaths; airClone: string; base: string
  nuance: string; share: string; fake: FakeSsh; spec: MirrorSpec; deps: MirrorDeps
}

/**
 * An Air home with the trial clone, and a "Nuance" home whose ~/Projects/collab-trial is an edit share holding a clone
 * of it (or, with related: false, a repo with no shared history), INSTALLED, shares.json and the Summon allowlist. The
 * Air side fetches through the fake ssh into the real gate from source, which runs the real `git upload-pack`.
 */
function world(o: { related?: boolean; caps?: Partial<TreeCaps>; deps?: Partial<MirrorDeps> } = {}): World {
  const air = temp('cb-mirror-air-')
  const paths = airPaths(air)
  const airClone = join(air, 'Projects', 'collab-trial')
  const base = makeRepo(airClone)
  // Task 21's installed Nuance home: INSTALLED with the Air's git as Nuance's recorded git (recordedGit, its Cellar
  // realpath, as `install check` records it), shares.json naming the share, and ~/Projects review, ~/Projects/collab-trial edit.
  const h = installedNuanceHome({ share: join('Projects', 'collab-trial') })
  const nuance = h.home
  const share = h.share
  if (o.related === false) {
    makeRepo(share, { 'README.md': 'another repo\n' })
  } else {
    mkdirSync(join(nuance, 'Projects'), { recursive: true })
    repoGit(join(nuance, 'Projects'), ['clone', '-q', airClone, 'collab-trial'])
  }
  const fake = makeFakeSsh({ nuanceHome: nuance, target: gateFromSource(), env: h.env })
  const mirrorId = mirrorIdOf(share)
  const spec: MirrorSpec = {
    device: 'nuance', user: 'macair', mirrorId, mirrorPath: paths.mirrorDir('nuance', 'macair', mirrorId), airClone,
    remoteGitdir: join(share, '.git'), caps: { ...DEFAULT_CAPS, ...o.caps },
  }
  const deps: MirrorDeps = {
    git: airGit({ git: REAL_GIT, home: air }), sshBin: fake.bin, sshConfig: paths.sshConfig, alias: 'collab-nuance',
    freeBytes: () => 1e15, fetchedToday: () => 0, ledger: (f) => { appendLedger(paths.ledger, AIR_LEDGER_KEYS, f) }, ...o.deps,
  }
  return { air, paths, airClone, base, nuance, share, fake, spec, deps }
}

async function created(o: Parameters<typeof world>[0] = {}): Promise<World> {
  const w = world(o)
  const r = await createMirror(w.spec, w.deps)
  if (!r.ok) throw new Error(`createMirror: ${r.code}: ${r.message}`)
  return w
}

const collabRefs = (w: World) => repoGit(w.airClone, ['for-each-ref', '--format=%(refname) %(objectname)', 'refs/collab'])
const packTemps = (w: World) => readdirSync(join(w.airClone, '.git', 'objects', 'pack')).filter((n) => n.startsWith('tmp_'))
const fetchLines = (w: World) => readLedger(w.paths.ledger).filter((e) => e.event === 'fetch')

describe('createMirror', () => {
  test('createMirror makes a locked linked worktree at the fetched commit, with incoming and synced refs and no refs/heads', async () => {
    const w = world()
    const heads = repoGit(w.airClone, ['for-each-ref', '--format=%(refname)', 'refs/heads'])
    expect(await createMirror(w.spec, w.deps)).toEqual({ ok: true, oid: w.base })
    const refs = mirrorRefs(w.spec)
    expect(refs.incoming).toBe(`refs/collab/nuance/macair/${w.spec.mirrorId}/incoming`)
    expect(refs.synced).toBe(`refs/collab/nuance/macair/${w.spec.mirrorId}/synced`)
    expect(refs.task('t-notes-1')).toBe(`refs/collab/nuance/macair/${w.spec.mirrorId}/tasks/t-notes-1`)
    expect(repoGit(w.airClone, ['worktree', 'list', '--porcelain'])).toContain(
      `worktree ${w.spec.mirrorPath}\nHEAD ${w.base}\ndetached\nlocked collab-bridge mirror`)
    expect(collabRefs(w)).toBe(`${refs.incoming} ${w.base}\n${refs.synced} ${w.base}`)
    expect(repoGit(w.airClone, ['for-each-ref', '--format=%(refname)', 'refs/heads'])).toBe(heads)
    expect(await mirrorHead(w.spec, w.deps)).toBe(w.base)
    expect(await syncedOid(w.spec, w.deps)).toBe(w.base)
    expect(readFileSync(join(w.spec.mirrorPath, 'README.md'), 'utf8')).toBe('collab trial\n')
    expect(w.fake.calls().map((c) => c.at(-1))).toEqual([`git-upload-pack '${w.share}/.git'`])
    // A second createMirror (a re-pin) finds a healthy mirror and changes nothing.
    expect(await createMirror(w.spec, w.deps)).toEqual({ ok: true, oid: w.base })
    expect(w.fake.calls().length).toBe(1)
  }, T)

  test('after createMirror, collab-shared and every mirrors level are 0700', async () => {
    const w = world()
    mkdirSync(w.paths.sharedDir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o755 })
    chmodSync(w.paths.sharedDir, 0o755) // as if an Air session's Collab had made it first
    await createMirror(w.spec, w.deps)
    const levels = [w.paths.sharedDir, w.paths.mirrorsRoot, join(w.paths.mirrorsRoot, 'nuance'), join(w.paths.mirrorsRoot, 'nuance', 'macair'), w.spec.mirrorPath]
    for (const dir of levels) expect([dir, modeOf(dir)]).toEqual([dir, 0o700])
  }, T)

  test('the derived workspace id equals the one a real Collab session rooted at the mirror reports', async () => {
    const w = await created()
    const start = async (root: string) => {
      const h = collabHarness({ journal: w.paths.sharedJournal, home: w.air })
      try {
        await h.initialize()
        return await h.callTool('collab_session_start', { root_path: root, actor: 'mirror-test' })
      } finally {
        await h.close()
      }
    }

    expect(remote.isError).toBeUndefined()
    expect(await mirrorWorkspaceId(w.spec, w.deps)).toBe(remote.structuredContent.workspace.id)
    // An Air session in the clone itself lands in the same workspace: mirrors share the clone's local-git key (§7.1).
    const local = await start(w.airClone)

    expect(await mirrorWorkspaceId({ ...w.spec, mirrorPath: join(w.air, 'no-such-mirror') }, w.deps)).toBeNull()
  }, T)

  test('liveMirrorDeps reads free space and today\'s fetch total', async () => {
    const air = temp('cb-mirror-air-')
    const paths = airPaths(air)
    const deps = liveMirrorDeps({ paths, git: airGit({ git: REAL_GIT, home: air }), ssh: '/usr/bin/ssh', alias: 'collab-nuance' })
    expect([deps.sshBin, deps.sshConfig, deps.alias, deps.git.path]).toEqual(['/usr/bin/ssh', paths.sshConfig, 'collab-nuance', REAL_GIT])
    const s = statfsSync(air)
    expect(Math.abs(deps.freeBytes(air) - Number(s.bavail) * Number(s.bsize))).toBeLessThan(256 * 1024 * 1024)
    deps.ledger({ event: 'fetch', device: 'nuance', user: 'macair', code: 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa', bytes: 100, outcome: 'ok', ms: 5 })
    deps.ledger({ event: 'fetch', device: 'nuance', user: 'macair', code: 'aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa', bytes: 23, outcome: 'failed', ms: 5 })
    deps.ledger({ event: 'fetch', device: 'nuance', user: 'macair', code: 'bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb', bytes: 7, outcome: 'ok', ms: 5 })
    expect(deps.fetchedToday('aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa')).toBe(123)
    expect(deps.fetchedToday('bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb')).toBe(7)

  test('a Nuance repo with no shared history is repo_mismatch and leaves no worktree', async () => {

    expect(r.ok === false && r.code).toBe('repo_mismatch')

    writeFileSync(join(w.air, '.gitconfig'), `[includeIf "gitdir:${w.airClone}/.git/worktrees/"]\n\tpath = ${inc}\n`)
    const r = await createMirror(w.spec, w.deps)

    expect(await syncedOid(w.spec, w.deps)).toBeNull()

describe('syncMirror', () => {
  test('a sync moves synced only after the checkout', async () => {
    const w = await created()
    const c2 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'a\n' }, 'a note')
    const calls: string[][] = []
    const real = w.deps.git
    const recording: GitRunner = {
      path: real.path,
      run: (a, o) => { calls.push(a); return real.run(a, o) },
      records: (a, o) => { calls.push(a); return real.records(a, o) },
    }
    expect(await syncMirror(w.spec, { declaredHead: c2 }, { ...w.deps, git: recording })).toEqual({ ok: true, oid: c2 })
    const checkout = calls.findIndex((a) => a.includes('checkout') && a.includes(c2))
    const update = calls.findIndex((a) => a.includes('update-ref') && a.includes(mirrorRefs(w.spec).synced))
    expect(checkout).toBeGreaterThan(-1)
    expect(update).toBeGreaterThan(checkout)
    expect(await mirrorHead(w.spec, w.deps)).toBe(c2)
    expect(await syncedOid(w.spec, w.deps)).toBe(c2)
    expect(readFileSync(join(w.spec.mirrorPath, 'notes', 'a.md'), 'utf8')).toBe('a\n')
    const last = fetchLines(w).at(-1)!
    expect([last.device, last.user, last.code, last.outcome]).toEqual(['nuance', 'macair', w.spec.mirrorId, 'ok'])
    expect(last.bytes as number).toBeGreaterThan(0)
  }, T)

    expect(await code()).toBe('mirror_tampered')
    repoGit(w.spec.mirrorPath, ['switch', '-q', '--detach', w.base])
    expect(w.fake.calls().length).toBe(1) // no refused sync ever fetched
    expect(await code()).toBe('ok')
  }, T)

  test('a filter in a temp global config is mirror_filters_present', async () => {
    const w = await created()
    const c2 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'a\n' }, 'a note')
    for (const conf of ['[filter "lfs"]\n\tclean = git-lfs clean -- %f\n', '[diff "pdf"]\n\ttextconv = cat\n', '[core]\n\tfsmonitor = true\n']) {

      expect([conf, r.ok === false && r.code]).toEqual([conf, 'mirror_filters_present'])
    }

    rmSync(join(w.air, '.gitconfig'))
    expect(await syncMirror(w.spec, { declaredHead: c2 }, w.deps)).toEqual({ ok: true, oid: c2 })
  }, T)

  test('a filter reached only through an includeIf is mirror_filters_present', async () => {
    const w = await created()
    const c2 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'a\n' }, 'a note')
    const inc = join(w.air, 'filters.conf')
    writeFileSync(inc, '[filter "x"]\n\tsmudge = cat\n')
    writeFileSync(join(w.air, '.gitconfig'), `[includeIf "gitdir:${w.airClone}/.git/worktrees/"]\n\tpath = ${inc}\n`)
    // The clone's own view is clean: the include matches only the mirror's gitdir, which the check reads from.
    expect((await w.deps.git.run(['-C', w.airClone, 'config', '--show-scope', '--get-regexp', '^filter\\.'])).code).toBe(1)
    const r = await syncMirror(w.spec, { declaredHead: c2 }, w.deps)
    expect(r.ok === false && r.code).toBe('mirror_filters_present')
    expect(await mirrorHead(w.spec, w.deps)).toBe(w.base)
  }, T)

  test('low disk before the fetch and before the checkout is mirror_low_disk', async () => {
    const w = await created()
    const c2 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'a'.repeat(100) }, 'a note')
    const before = await syncMirror(w.spec, { declaredHead: c2 }, { ...w.deps, freeBytes: () => MIN_FREE_BYTES + FETCH_HEADROOM_BYTES - 1 })
    expect(before.ok === false && before.code).toBe('mirror_low_disk')
    expect(w.fake.calls().length).toBe(1) // refused before fetching
    // Enough for the fetch, then less than the tree needs: README (13) + notes/a.md (100) = 113 bytes over the floor.
    const frees = [MIN_FREE_BYTES + FETCH_HEADROOM_BYTES, MIN_FREE_BYTES + 112]
    const after = await syncMirror(w.spec, { declaredHead: c2 }, { ...w.deps, freeBytes: () => frees.shift() ?? 0 })
    expect(after.ok === false && after.code).toBe('mirror_low_disk')
    expect(w.fake.calls().length).toBe(2)
    expect(await mirrorHead(w.spec, w.deps)).toBe(w.base)
    expect(await syncedOid(w.spec, w.deps)).toBe(w.base)
    expect(existsSync(join(w.spec.mirrorPath, 'notes', 'a.md'))).toBe(false)
  }, T)

  test('a mirror past its daily budget is rate_limited', async () => {
    const w = await created()
    const c2 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'a\n' }, 'a note')
    const r = await syncMirror(w.spec, { declaredHead: c2 }, { ...w.deps, fetchedToday: () => DAILY_BUDGET_BYTES })
    expect(r.ok === false && r.code).toBe('rate_limited')
    expect(w.fake.calls().length).toBe(1)
    expect(await syncMirror(w.spec, { declaredHead: c2 }, { ...w.deps, fetchedToday: () => DAILY_BUDGET_BYTES - 1 })).toEqual({ ok: true, oid: c2 })
  }, T)

  test('a pack over the wire cap is fetch_failed and leaves no temp pack', async () => {
    const w = await created()
    const c2 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/noise.txt': randomBytes(1536 * 1024).toString('base64') }, 'a 2 MiB note')
    const r = await syncMirror(w.spec, { declaredHead: c2 }, { ...w.deps, wireCapBytes: 1024 * 1024 })
    expect(r.ok === false && [r.code, r.message]).toEqual(['fetch_failed', 'the fetched pack passed the 1 MiB limit for one sync'])
    expect(packTemps(w)).toEqual([])
    expect(await mirrorHead(w.spec, w.deps)).toBe(w.base)
    expect(collabRefs(w)).toBe(`${mirrorRefs(w.spec).incoming} ${w.base}\n${mirrorRefs(w.spec).synced} ${w.base}`)
    const last = fetchLines(w).at(-1)!
    expect(last.outcome).toBe('failed')
    expect(last.bytes as number).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1024 * 1024) // the cut pack counts against the day's budget

  test('the production cap is ulimit -f 131072', () => {

describe('MirrorLock', () => {
  test('runs one at a time, in order, and a failure frees it', async () => {
    const lock = new MirrorLock()
    const order: string[] = []
    const a = lock.run(async () => { order.push('a start'); await Bun.sleep(30); order.push('a end'); return 1 })
    const b = lock.run(async () => { order.push('b'); throw new Error('b failed') })
    const c = lock.run(async () => { order.push('c'); return 3 })
    expect(await a).toBe(1)
    await expect(b).rejects.toThrow('b failed')
    expect(await c).toBe(3)
    expect(order).toEqual(['a start', 'a end', 'b', 'c'])
  })
})
```

`/Users/yuai/Projects/.worktrees/agenttool-collab-bridge/packages/collab-bridge/src/air/mirror.ts`:

```ts
// Per-device mirrors on the Air (C11, spec §7.1, §7.3): one locked linked worktree of the Air clone per (device, user,
// Nuance repo), moved only by a read-only v0 fetch from the Nuance gate and a checkout of exactly the commit the pipe
// declared. Every step refuses rather than repairs (R12), except that a failed checkout restores the mirror first; an
// ambiguous failure is refused once and never retried. Nothing here takes the per-mirror lock: the caller holds it for
// the whole flow, from the sync until the forwarded call returns (Task 45, P25). No harness and no bun ever has its cwd in
// a mirror (R27): git runs with `-C` from cwd '/'.
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { chmodSync, lstatSync, mkdirSync, readdirSync, realpathSync, rmSync, statfsSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { basename, dirname, join } from 'node:path'
import type { AgentCode } from '../failure.ts'
import { AIR_LEDGER_KEYS, appendLedger, readLedger, type LedgerFields } from '../ledger.ts'
import type { AirPaths } from '../paths.ts'
import { TIMING } from '../timing.ts'
import { ancestorCheck, checkDiff, checkTree, type TreeCaps } from './diff-check.ts'
import { MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, OID_RE, type GitResult, type GitRunner } from './git.ts'

export interface MirrorSpec { device: string; user: string; mirrorId: string; mirrorPath: string; airClone: string; remoteGitdir: string; caps: TreeCaps }
export interface MirrorDeps {
  git: GitRunner; sshBin: string; sshConfig: string; alias: string; freeBytes(path: string): number
  fetchedToday(mirrorId: string): number; ledger(f: LedgerFields): void; wireCapBytes?: number; dailyBudgetBytes?: number
  minFreeBytes?: number; fetchTimeoutMs?: number; checkoutTimeoutMs?: number
}

/** §6.6: 128 MiB of pack per sync, 1 GiB of packs per mirror per day, 5 GiB free beyond the fetch (128 MiB) or the checkout. */
export const WIRE_CAP_BYTES = 134_217_728, DAILY_BUDGET_BYTES = 1_073_741_824, MIN_FREE_BYTES = 5_368_709_120, FETCH_HEADROOM_BYTES = 134_217_728

export type SyncResult = { ok: true; oid: string; changed?: number } | { ok: false; code: AgentCode; message: string }

const sha256 = (s: string) => createHash('sha256').update(s).digest('hex')
const text = (r: GitResult) => new TextDecoder().decode(r.stdout).trim()
const refuse = (code: AgentCode, message: string): SyncResult => ({ ok: false, code, message })

/** `mirror_id = sha256(remote realpath)[:16]` (§7.1). */
export function mirrorIdOf(remoteRealpath: string): string {
  return sha256(remoteRealpath).slice(0, 16)
}

/**
 * True when git can hold the id as one ref component. Collab task ids are `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*`; git refuses
 * `:`, `..`, and a trailing `.` or `.lock` in a ref name (git-check-ref-format(1)).
 */
export function taskRefOk(id: string): boolean {
  return /^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$/.test(id) && !id.includes('..') && !id.endsWith('.') && !id.endsWith('.lock')
}

/** The mirror's refs, never under refs/heads (§7.1). Throws for a device, user, mirror id or task id git cannot hold. */
export function mirrorRefs(spec: MirrorSpec): { incoming: string; synced: string; task(taskId: string): string } {
  for (const part of [spec.device, spec.user, spec.mirrorId]) {
    if (!taskRefOk(part)) throw new Error(`mirrorRefs: ${JSON.stringify(part)} cannot be part of a ref name`)
  }
  const root = `refs/collab/${spec.device}/${spec.user}/${spec.mirrorId}`
  return {
    incoming: `${root}/incoming`,
    synced: `${root}/synced`,
    task(taskId: string) {
      if (!taskRefOk(taskId)) throw new Error(`mirrorRefs: task id ${JSON.stringify(taskId)} cannot be a ref name`)
      return `${root}/tasks/${taskId}`
    },
  }
}

/** `ulimit -f` counts 1024-byte blocks in the Air's /bin/sh (P11, F1): 128 MiB is 131072, never §7.3's 262144. */
export function ulimitBlocks(bytes: number): number {
  return Math.floor(bytes / 1024)
}

/** The fetch of §7.3 step 4, split where the Air's git starts: the size-capped shell and env words, then git's own args. */
function fetchParts(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: Pick<MirrorDeps, 'sshBin' | 'sshConfig' | 'alias' | 'git'>, wireCapBytes: number): { prefix: string[]; args: string[] } {
  if (!deps.sshBin.startsWith('/') || /[\s'"\\$`]/.test(deps.sshBin)) throw new Error('fetchArgv: the ssh path must be absolute with no shell characters')
  if (!deps.sshConfig.startsWith('/') || /['\\\n]/.test(deps.sshConfig)) throw new Error('fetchArgv: the ssh config path cannot be single-quoted')
  if (!/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$/.test(deps.alias)) throw new Error('fetchArgv: bad ssh Host alias')
  // The gate's own grammar (§5.2): an absolute path of at most 1024 bytes with no ', !, \ or control character.
  if (!/^\/[^'!\\\x00-\x1f\x7f]{1,1023}$/.test(spec.remoteGitdir) || Buffer.byteLength(spec.remoteGitdir) > 1024) {
    throw new Error('fetchArgv: the remote gitdir cannot pass the gate')
  }
  if (!Number.isSafeInteger(wireCapBytes) || wireCapBytes < 1024) throw new Error('fetchArgv: bad wire cap')
  return {
    prefix: ['/bin/sh', '-c', `ulimit -f ${ulimitBlocks(wireCapBytes)}; exec "$@"`, 'sh',
      'env', '-u', 'GIT_SSH', `GIT_SSH_COMMAND=${deps.sshBin} -F '${deps.sshConfig}'`],
    args: ['-C', spec.airClone, '-c', 'protocol.version=0', '-c', 'transfer.fsckObjects=true', '-c', 'fetch.fsckObjects=true',
      '-c', 'transfer.unpackLimit=1', ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'fetch', '--no-tags', '--no-recurse-submodules', '--no-prune',
      '--no-write-fetch-head', `${deps.alias}:${spec.remoteGitdir}`, `+HEAD:${mirrorRefs(spec).incoming}`],
  }
}

/**
 * The exact argv of §7.3 step 4: `-c fetch.fsckObjects=true` outranks any config that would turn fsck off, and
 * `transfer.unpackLimit=1` keeps the download as one pack file, which the file-size limit bounds. GIT_PROTOCOL is never
 * set, so the fetch is v0 end to end (K49).
 */
export function fetchArgv(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: Pick<MirrorDeps, 'sshBin' | 'sshConfig' | 'alias' | 'git'>, wireCapBytes: number): string[] {
  const { prefix, args } = fetchParts(spec, deps, wireCapBytes)
  return [...prefix, deps.git.path, ...args]
}

/** A FIFO async mutex, one per mirror, inside the one hub process (`hub.lock` keeps it to one hub, P25). */
export class MirrorLock {
  private tail: Promise<unknown> = Promise.resolve()
  run<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
    const result = this.tail.then(() => fn())
    this.tail = result.then(() => undefined, () => undefined) // a failure frees the lock for the next caller
    return result
  }
}

async function commitAt(deps: MirrorDeps, cwd: string, rev: string): Promise<string | null> {
  const r = await deps.git.run(['-C', cwd, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'rev-parse', '--verify', '--quiet', `${rev}^{commit}`])
  const oid = text(r)
  return r.code === 0 && OID_RE.test(oid) ? oid : null
}

async function commonDirOf(deps: Pick<MirrorDeps, 'git'>, cwd: string): Promise<string | null> {
  const r = await deps.git.run(['-C', cwd, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'rev-parse', '--path-format=absolute', '--git-common-dir'])
  if (r.code !== 0) return null
  try { return realpathSync(text(r)) } catch { return null }
}

/** The last synced oid (`…/synced`), or null when the ref is missing or unreadable. */
export function syncedOid(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<string | null> {
  return commitAt(deps, spec.airClone, mirrorRefs(spec).synced)
}

/**
 * The mirror's own HEAD commit, or null. The mirror must be a real directory (never a symlink) that git sees as its
 * own work-tree root, in the Air clone's repository: a plain directory would otherwise let git walk up to some parent
 * repository and report that one's HEAD.
 */
export async function mirrorHead(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<string | null> {
  let real: string
  try {
    const st = lstatSync(spec.mirrorPath)
    if (!st.isDirectory() || st.isSymbolicLink()) return null
    real = realpathSync(spec.mirrorPath)
  } catch { return null }
  const r = await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.mirrorPath, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'rev-parse', '--path-format=absolute',
    '--show-toplevel', '--git-common-dir', 'HEAD^{commit}'])
  if (r.code !== 0) return null
  const [top, common, oid] = text(r).split('\n')
  if (top !== real || !oid || !OID_RE.test(oid)) return null
  const clone = await commonDirOf(deps, spec.airClone)
  let commonReal: string
  try { commonReal = realpathSync(common ?? '') } catch { return null }
  return clone !== null && commonReal === clone ? oid : null
}

/** §7.3 step 1: null when the mirror is clean, detached, and at `…/synced`; else why not. */
async function tamperReason(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<string | null> {
  const head = await mirrorHead(spec, deps)
  if (head === null) return 'the mirror has no readable HEAD of its own in the Air clone'
  const synced = await syncedOid(spec, deps)
  if (synced === null) return 'the mirror has no synced ref'
  if (head !== synced) return "the mirror's HEAD is not its last synced commit"
  const sym = await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.mirrorPath, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'symbolic-ref', '-q', 'HEAD'])
  if (sym.code !== 1) return 'the mirror is not on a detached HEAD'
  // Ignored and untracked files count: a forced checkout would clobber them without a word (T16).
  const st = await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.mirrorPath, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'status', '--porcelain=v1', '--untracked-files=all', '--ignored'])
  if (st.code !== 0) return 'git status failed in the mirror'
  if (st.stdout.byteLength > 0) return 'the mirror has local changes or extra files'
  return null
}

/**
 * §7.3 step 2, as seen from `cwd`: every scope (system, global, includes, the repo, the worktree), never `--local` or
 * `--file`, and never with `-c` (a command-line `core.fsmonitor=false` would itself match). Exit 1 with no output is clean.
 */
async function filterReason(cwd: string, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<string | null> {
  const r = await deps.git.run(['-C', cwd, 'config', '--show-scope', '--get-regexp', '^filter\\.|^diff\\..*\\.textconv$|^core\\.fsmonitor$'])
  if (r.code === 1 && r.stdout.byteLength === 0 && !r.timedOut) return null
  if (r.code === 0) return 'a git filter, textconv or fsmonitor is configured where the mirror would see it'
  return 'the git config check failed'
}

/** §7.3 step 3. */
function diskAndBudget(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: MirrorDeps): SyncResult | null {
  const minFree = deps.minFreeBytes ?? MIN_FREE_BYTES
  let free: number
  try { free = deps.freeBytes(spec.airClone) } catch { return refuse('mirror_low_disk', 'the Air could not read its free disk space') }
  if (!(free >= minFree + FETCH_HEADROOM_BYTES)) return refuse('mirror_low_disk', 'the Air has less than 5 GiB plus the 128 MiB fetch allowance free')
  let today: number
  try { today = deps.fetchedToday(spec.mirrorId) } catch { return refuse('rate_limited', "the Air could not read today's fetch total for this mirror") }
  if (!(today < (deps.dailyBudgetBytes ?? DAILY_BUDGET_BYTES))) return refuse('rate_limited', 'this mirror has fetched its 1 GiB of packs for today')
  return null
}

function listPackDir(dir: string): string[] {
  try { return readdirSync(dir) } catch { return [] }
}

function sizeOf(path: string): number {
  try { return statSync(path).size } catch { return 0 }
}

/**
 * Two mirrors of one Air clone (two devices sharing a repo, Phase 2) fetch into one object store, so their fetches are
 * serialised: neither ever counts or removes the other's temporary pack.
 */
const cloneFetchLocks = new Map<string, MirrorLock>()

/**
 * §7.3 step 4: fetch the remote HEAD into `…/incoming`, then ledger the new pack bytes (P31: the day's budget is summed
 * from these lines). A fetch git leaves half done, whether it hit the file-size limit (SIGXFSZ leaves `tmp_pack_*`
 * behind, measured on this Air) or the timeout, has its new temporary files removed; their bytes still count.
 */
async function fetchIncoming(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<SyncResult | null> {
  let lock = cloneFetchLocks.get(spec.airClone)
  if (lock === undefined) cloneFetchLocks.set(spec.airClone, (lock = new MirrorLock()))
  return lock.run(() => fetchIncomingNow(spec, deps))
}

async function fetchIncomingNow(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<SyncResult | null> {
  const wireCap = deps.wireCapBytes ?? WIRE_CAP_BYTES
  let parts: { prefix: string[]; args: string[] }
  try { parts = fetchParts(spec, deps, wireCap) } catch { return refuse('fetch_failed', 'the fetch command could not be built safely from the device file') }
  const packs = await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.airClone, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'rev-parse', '--path-format=absolute', '--git-path', 'objects/pack'])
  if (packs.code !== 0) return refuse('fetch_failed', 'the Air clone has no object store git could name')
  const packDir = text(packs)
  const before = new Set(listPackDir(packDir))
  const { prefix, args } = parts
  const t0 = performance.now()
  const r = await deps.git.run(args, { prefix, timeoutMs: deps.fetchTimeoutMs ?? TIMING.fetchMs })
  const fresh = listPackDir(packDir).filter((n) => !before.has(n))
  let bytes = 0
  let capped = false
  for (const n of fresh) {
    if (!n.endsWith('.pack') && !n.startsWith('tmp_pack_')) continue
    const size = sizeOf(join(packDir, n))
    bytes += size
    if (n.startsWith('tmp_pack_') && size >= wireCap) capped = true
  }
  const ok = r.code === 0
  if (!ok) for (const n of fresh) if (n.startsWith('tmp_')) rmSync(join(packDir, n), { force: true })
  try {
    deps.ledger({ event: 'fetch', device: spec.device, user: spec.user, code: spec.mirrorId, bytes,
      outcome: ok ? 'ok' : r.timedOut ? 'timeout' : 'failed', ms: Math.max(0, Math.round(performance.now() - t0)) })
  } catch {
    return refuse('rate_limited', "the fetch could not be written to the hub ledger, so today's budget cannot be kept")
  }
  if (ok) return null
  if (r.timedOut) return refuse('fetch_failed', 'the fetch from the device took longer than 60 s and was stopped')
  if (capped) return refuse('fetch_failed', `the fetched pack passed the ${Math.round(wireCap / 1_048_576)} MiB limit for one sync`)
  return refuse('fetch_failed', 'the fetch from the device failed')
}

/** §7.3 step 6, then the free-space floor for the checkout. */
async function treeAndDisk(spec: MirrorSpec, oid: string, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<SyncResult | null> {
  const t = await checkTree(deps.git, spec.airClone, oid, spec.caps)
  if (!t.ok) {
    const where = t.path === undefined ? '' : ` (${t.path})`
    return refuse(t.code, t.code === 'remote_too_large'
      ? `the fetched tree is over this share's size caps${where}`
      : t.code === 'remote_non_regular_path' ? `the fetched tree holds a gitlink${where}` : 'the fetched tree could not be read')
  }
  let free: number
  try { free = deps.freeBytes(spec.airClone) } catch { return refuse('mirror_low_disk', 'the Air could not read its free disk space') }
  if (!(free >= (deps.minFreeBytes ?? MIN_FREE_BYTES) + t.totalBytes)) return refuse('mirror_low_disk', 'the Air has less than 5 GiB plus the tree free')
  return null
}

const DIFF_MESSAGES: Record<string, string> = {
  remote_non_regular_path: 'the commit changes a symlink, a gitlink or another non-regular path',
  remote_out_of_scope: "the commit changes a path outside the task's path scopes",
  remote_control_path: 'the commit changes a control file such as .claude, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, package.json or bunfig.toml',
  remote_too_large: "the commit changes more paths than this share's cap",
  fetch_failed: 'the commit could not be compared with its base',
}

/** §7.3 step 7: the task's base must be an ancestor, and every changed path regular, in scope and not a control path. */
async function heldToTask(spec: MirrorSpec, oid: string, at: { base: string; scopes: readonly string[] }, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<{ changed: number } | SyncResult> {
  const anc = await ancestorCheck(deps.git, spec.airClone, at.base, oid)
  if (anc === 'remote_base_not_ancestor') return refuse(anc, "the task's base is not an ancestor of the commit")
  if (anc !== 'ok') return refuse('fetch_failed', "the commit could not be checked against the task's base")
  const d = await checkDiff(deps.git, spec.airClone, at.base, oid, at.scopes, spec.caps)
  if (!d.ok) return refuse(d.code, `${DIFF_MESSAGES[d.code]}${d.path === undefined ? '' : ` (${d.path})`}`)
  return { changed: d.changed }
}

/** Steps 1–9 of §7.3. The caller holds this mirror's lock. */
export async function syncMirror(spec: MirrorSpec, o: { declaredHead: string; atComplete?: { base: string; scopes: readonly string[] } }, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<SyncResult> {
  let refs: ReturnType<typeof mirrorRefs>
  try { refs = mirrorRefs(spec) } catch { return refuse('mirror_tampered', 'the mirror spec cannot name its refs; Ai looks at the device file') }
  if (!OID_RE.test(o.declaredHead)) return refuse('remote_head_moved', 'the declared head is not a commit id')
  const why = await tamperReason(spec, deps) // 1
  if (why !== null) return refuse('mirror_tampered', `${why}; Ai looks at it on the Air`)
  const synced = (await syncedOid(spec, deps))!
  const filters = await filterReason(spec.mirrorPath, deps) // 2
  if (filters !== null) return refuse('mirror_filters_present', filters)
  const room = diskAndBudget(spec, deps) // 3
  if (room !== null) return room
  const fetched = await fetchIncoming(spec, deps) // 4
  if (fetched !== null) return fetched
  const oid = await commitAt(deps, spec.airClone, refs.incoming)
  if (oid === null) return refuse('fetch_failed', 'the fetch left no readable commit')
  if (oid !== o.declaredHead) return refuse('remote_head_moved', "the device's HEAD is not the head the pipe declared") // 5
  const tree = await treeAndDisk(spec, oid, deps) // 6
  if (tree !== null) return tree
  let changed: number | undefined
  if (o.atComplete) { // 7
    const held = await heldToTask(spec, oid, o.atComplete, deps)
    if ('ok' in held) return held
    changed = held.changed
  }
  const co = await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.mirrorPath, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'checkout', '--detach', '-f', '--no-recurse-submodules', oid],
    { timeoutMs: deps.checkoutTimeoutMs ?? TIMING.checkoutMs }) // 8
  if (co.code !== 0) {
    const back = await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.mirrorPath, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'checkout', '--detach', '-f', '--no-recurse-submodules', synced],
      { timeoutMs: deps.checkoutTimeoutMs ?? TIMING.checkoutMs })
    const clean = back.code === 0 ? await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.mirrorPath, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'clean', '-ffdxq']) : back
    if (back.code === 0 && clean.code === 0) return refuse('checkout_failed', 'the checkout of the fetched commit failed; the mirror was restored')
    return refuse('mirror_tampered', 'the checkout failed and the mirror could not be restored; Ai repairs it on the Air')
  }
  // 9: compare and swap. A crash between 8 and 9 shows as mirror_tampered at the next sync (HEAD is not synced).
  const moved = await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.airClone, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'update-ref', refs.synced, oid, synced])
  if (moved.code !== 0) return refuse('mirror_tampered', 'the synced ref moved during the sync; Ai looks at it on the Air')
  return changed === undefined ? { ok: true, oid } : { ok: true, oid, changed }
}

/** The four levels above the mirror (collab-shared/, mirrors/, mirrors/<device>/, mirrors/<device>/<user>/), or null. */
function mirrorLevels(spec: MirrorSpec): string[] | null {
  const user = dirname(spec.mirrorPath)
  const device = dirname(user)
  const mirrors = dirname(device)
  const shared = dirname(mirrors)
  if (basename(spec.mirrorPath) !== spec.mirrorId || basename(user) !== spec.user || basename(device) !== spec.device || basename(mirrors) !== 'mirrors') return null
  return [shared, mirrors, device, user]
}

async function removeNewWorktree(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<void> {
  // Only a worktree this call added and nothing has bound to (it has no synced ref yet), so its name can be reused.
  await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.airClone, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'worktree', 'remove', '--force', spec.mirrorPath])
}

async function ensureLocked(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<boolean> {
  const list = await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.airClone, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'worktree', 'list', '--porcelain'])
  if (list.code !== 0) return false
  const block = new TextDecoder().decode(list.stdout).split('\n\n').find((b) => b.split('\n')[0] === `worktree ${realpathSync(spec.mirrorPath)}`)
  if (block === undefined) return false
  if (block.split('\n').some((l) => l === 'locked' || l.startsWith('locked '))) return true
  const lock = await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.airClone, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'worktree', 'lock', '--reason', 'collab-bridge mirror', spec.mirrorPath])
  return lock.code === 0
}

/**
 * The first sync, at pin-device, before any session can bind (§7.1, K17): steps 2–4 and 6 of §7.3, then
 * `repo_mismatch` unless the fetched commit shares history with the clone, then the linked worktree (added without a
 * checkout, its own config view checked for filters, since an includeIf can match only a worktree's gitdir, then checked
 * out), locked against prune, and `…/synced` created. A mirror that already exists is never deleted and re-added (that
 * would give `worktree_identity_changed`, K11): a healthy one is kept as it is, anything else is mirror_tampered.
 */
export async function createMirror(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<SyncResult> {
  let refs: ReturnType<typeof mirrorRefs>
  try { refs = mirrorRefs(spec) } catch { return refuse('mirror_tampered', 'the mirror spec cannot name its refs; Ai looks at the device file') }
  const levels = mirrorLevels(spec)
  if (levels === null) return refuse('mirror_tampered', 'the mirror path is not <collab-shared>/mirrors/<device>/<user>/<mirror_id>')
  let exists = true
  try { lstatSync(spec.mirrorPath) } catch { exists = false }
  if (exists) {
    const why = await tamperReason(spec, deps)
    if (why !== null) return refuse('mirror_tampered', `an existing mirror path is not a healthy mirror: ${why}`)
    if (!(await ensureLocked(spec, deps))) return refuse('mirror_tampered', 'the existing mirror could not be locked against prune')
    return { ok: true, oid: (await syncedOid(spec, deps))! }
  }
  // Git would make these 0755, and Collab tightens the journal's parent only when it created it (KN src/store.ts:402-407).
  for (const dir of levels) {
    mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 })
    chmodSync(dir, 0o700)
  }
  const filters = await filterReason(spec.airClone, deps) // 2
  if (filters !== null) return refuse('mirror_filters_present', filters)
  const room = diskAndBudget(spec, deps) // 3
  if (room !== null) return room
  const fetched = await fetchIncoming(spec, deps) // 4
  if (fetched !== null) return fetched
  const oid = await commitAt(deps, spec.airClone, refs.incoming)
  if (oid === null) return refuse('fetch_failed', 'the fetch left no readable commit')
  const tree = await treeAndDisk(spec, oid, deps) // 6
  if (tree !== null) return tree
  const shared = await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.airClone, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'merge-base', oid, 'HEAD'])
  if (shared.code !== 0) {
    await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.airClone, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'update-ref', '-d', refs.incoming])
    return refuse('repo_mismatch', "the device's repository shares no history with the Air clone")
  }
  const checkoutMs = deps.checkoutTimeoutMs ?? TIMING.checkoutMs
  const added = await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.airClone, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'worktree', 'add', '--detach', '--no-checkout', spec.mirrorPath, oid], { timeoutMs: checkoutMs })
  if (added.code !== 0) return refuse('checkout_failed', 'git could not add the mirror worktree')
  const own = await filterReason(spec.mirrorPath, deps)
  if (own !== null) {
    await removeNewWorktree(spec, deps)
    return refuse('mirror_filters_present', own)
  }
  const co = await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.mirrorPath, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'checkout', '--detach', '-f', '--no-recurse-submodules', oid], { timeoutMs: checkoutMs })
  if (co.code !== 0) {
    await removeNewWorktree(spec, deps)
    return refuse('checkout_failed', 'the first checkout of the mirror failed; nothing was kept')
  }
  chmodSync(spec.mirrorPath, 0o700)
  const lock = await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.airClone, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'worktree', 'lock', '--reason', 'collab-bridge mirror', spec.mirrorPath])
  if (lock.code !== 0) {
    await removeNewWorktree(spec, deps)
    return refuse('mirror_tampered', 'git could not lock the new mirror; nothing was kept')
  }
  const made = await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.airClone, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'update-ref', refs.synced, oid, ''])
  if (made.code !== 0) return refuse('mirror_tampered', 'the synced ref already exists for a mirror that did not; Ai looks at it on the Air')
  return { ok: true, oid }
}

/**
 * Collab's K11 rule for this mirror's repository (KN `src/repository.ts:101-104`, `src/store.ts:1394-1401`):
 * `ws_` + sha256(`local-git:` + sha256(realpath of the git common dir))[:24]. The shared journal has one workspace per
 * key (§6.3), so this is the workspace the first remote session_start binds to (P55). Null when git fails.
 */
export async function mirrorWorkspaceId(spec: MirrorSpec, deps: Pick<MirrorDeps, 'git'>): Promise<string | null> {
  const common = await commonDirOf(deps, spec.mirrorPath)
  return common === null ? null : `ws_${sha256(`local-git:${sha256(common)}`).slice(0, 24)}`
}

/**
 * `…/tasks/<task_id>`, written once for a new completion and only when `head` is the mirror's HEAD (§7.2). The same
 * value again is a no-op; a different value is mirror_tampered and the ref stays. A task id git cannot hold as a ref
 * name (`taskRefOk`) writes nothing and answers 'ok': the mirror is fine, and the reviewer reads the task's result
 * checkpoint head instead (§7.7).
 */
export async function writeTaskRef(spec: MirrorSpec, taskId: string, head: string, deps: MirrorDeps): Promise<'ok' | 'mirror_tampered'> {
  if (!OID_RE.test(head)) return 'mirror_tampered'
  if ((await mirrorHead(spec, deps)) !== head) return 'mirror_tampered'
  if (!taskRefOk(taskId)) return 'ok'
  const ref = mirrorRefs(spec).task(taskId)
  const existing = await commitAt(deps, spec.airClone, ref)
  if (existing !== null) return existing === head ? 'ok' : 'mirror_tampered'
  const r = await deps.git.run(['-C', spec.airClone, ...MIRROR_GIT_FLAGS, 'update-ref', ref, head, ''])
  if (r.code === 0) return 'ok'
  return (await commitAt(deps, spec.airClone, ref)) === head ? 'ok' : 'mirror_tampered'
}

/** P31: the `bytes` of this mirror's `fetch` lines in the hub ledger since local midnight. */
export function fetchedTodayFromLedger(ledgerPath: string, mirrorId: string, now: Date): number {
  const midnight = new Date(now.getFullYear(), now.getMonth(), now.getDate()).getTime()
  let total = 0
  for (const e of readLedger(ledgerPath)) {
    if (e.event !== 'fetch' || e.code !== mirrorId || typeof e.bytes !== 'number') continue
    const at = Date.parse(e.ts)
    if (Number.isFinite(at) && at >= midnight) total += e.bytes
  }
  return total
}

/** The hub's deps: free space on the Air's Data volume (air-env F17), today's total from its ledger, its ssh config. */
export function liveMirrorDeps(o: { paths: AirPaths; git: GitRunner; ssh: string; alias: string }): MirrorDeps {
  return {
    git: o.git,
    sshBin: o.ssh,
    sshConfig: o.paths.sshConfig,
    alias: o.alias,
    freeBytes: (path) => {
      const s = statfsSync(path)
      return Number(s.bavail) * Number(s.bsize)
    },
    fetchedToday: (mirrorId) => fetchedTodayFromLedger(o.paths.ledger, mirrorId, new Date()),
    ledger: (f) => { appendLedger(o.paths.ledger, AIR_LEDGER_KEYS, f) },
  }
}
```

### Task 43: Task views and the one-task rule

**Kind:** [implementer] · **Group:** 14 · **Spec:** §7.2 "One edit task per mirror at a time (R36), derived, never stored", §12.2 One-task rule (request_changes then a reissue is not mirror_busy; a remote task_block frees the mirror; an Air-side accept and an Air-side recover-release free it; a reported-policy completion frees it; a pending review and a recovery_required claim keep it busy; a complete of the task claimed on the mirror does not refuse itself); K60; R36.

The hub never keeps its own idea of which task holds a mirror: before a sync for task X or a takeover of X it reads Collab's task projection through the lineage's own child and derives the answer (§7.2). This task makes the typed views of that projection and the rule itself. Facts it builds on, measured on this Air against the tracked Collab dist (0.5.0, `packages/collab/dist/agenttool-collab-mcp.js`) for this plan:

- `collab_task_get`, `collab_task_claim`, `collab_task_complete`, `collab_task_recover` and `collab_task_review` answer `structuredContent.task`; `collab_task_list` answers `structuredContent.tasks` and takes one optional `status`; an isError result carries `{error, message, …}` instead (KN `src/mcp.ts:594-620`, `:1224-1243`).
- A claim sets `claim_worktree_id` to the claiming session's worktree id. Complete nulls `claim_worktree_id`, `lease_id` and `lease_expires_at` and stores `result_checkpoint` with that worktree id; `review_status` is then `pending` for an `accepted`-policy edit task and `not_required` for a `reported` one. request_changes reopens the task as `open` with `changes_requested` and keeps `expected_base_sha` (K60).
- An expired session lease keeps `status: 'claimed'` and its `claim_worktree_id`; only `effective_status` reads `recovery_required` (KN `src/store.ts:5803-5813`), so `collab_task_list` with `status: 'claimed'` returns it.
- Collab's smallest lease is `ttl_seconds: 30` (KN `src/mcp.ts:38`) and expiry is computed on every read against the store's own wall clock, so no test can wait for one inside the 10 s test budget. The tests move a lease into the past with `/usr/bin/sqlite3` (3.43.2) on their temp journal, in one transaction that inserts and then deletes Collab's own `v2_write_guard` row: the triggers at KN `src/store.ts:925-947` refuse a v0.2 task update without it, and a guard row left behind would make the next open fail `database_write_guard_invalid` (`src/store.ts:1291-1297`). The event chain is not touched, and `collab_journal_verify` still answers `chain_valid: true` afterwards. Like Task 38's `tamperJournal`, it goes through the system `sqlite3`, so no test imports `bun:sqlite` (Global Constraints), and it is only ever given a temp journal.
- A linked worktree of the Air clone shares the clone's `local-git:` key (K11), so a session rooted at the mirror and one rooted at the clone land in one workspace, and an unbound child started later (as after a hub restart) reads the same projection.

```ts
// src/air/tasks.ts — field names from Collab's Task and RepoCheckpoint (packages/collab/src/protocol.ts:81-91, 253-296)
export interface CheckpointView { worktree_id: string; head_sha: string | null }
export interface TaskView { id: string; version: number; status: 'open' | 'claimed' | 'blocked' | 'completed'; effective_status: string;
  work_mode: 'coordination' | 'read_only' | 'edit'; completion_policy: 'reported' | 'accepted'; review_status: string;
  assignee_session_id: string | null; lease_id: string | null; lease_expires_at: string | null; expected_base_sha: string | null;
  base_checkpoint: CheckpointView | null; claim_worktree_id: string | null; result_checkpoint: CheckpointView | null; path_scopes: string[] }
export function taskFromResult(r: ToolResult): TaskView | null      // structuredContent.task
export function tasksFromResult(r: ToolResult): TaskView[] | null   // structuredContent.tasks
export function readTask(child: CollabChild, workspaceId: string, taskId: string): Promise<TaskView | null>
export function listTasks(child: CollabChild, workspaceId: string, status: 'claimed' | 'completed'): Promise<TaskView[] | null>
// src/air/busy.ts
export type Busy = { busy: false } | { busy: true; holder: string | null; reason: 'claimed' | 'pending_review' | 'read_failed' | 'mirror_unknown' }
export function mirrorBusy(child: CollabChild, workspaceId: string, mirrorWorktreeId: string | null, taskId: string): Promise<Busy>
//   another edit task (not taskId) claimed with claim_worktree_id === mirror (recovery_required included), or completed with
//   review_status 'pending' and result_checkpoint.worktree_id === mirror → busy with its id; a failed read → busy read_failed;
//   an unknown mirror worktree id → busy mirror_unknown
```

Notes for the implementer:
- A view keeps exactly the fifteen fields above, copies `path_scopes`, and reduces each checkpoint to `{worktree_id, head_sha}`; a value of the wrong type anywhere (a status outside Collab's four, a version below 1, a checkpoint without a string `worktree_id`) makes the whole result read as null. An isError result is null too. Every caller treats null as a failed read, never as "no task" or "nothing claimed".
- `mirrorBusy` decides `mirror_unknown` before any read (no remote session has bound to the mirror yet, so nothing can be matched), then reads the `claimed` page, then the `completed` page. Only `work_mode: 'edit'` tasks hold a mirror (§7.2 "another edit task"). It never caches: each call is at most two Collab reads, which is what makes refused claims, Air-side reviews and hub restarts need no bookkeeping.
- `readTask` and `listTasks` go through `child.call`, which never throws and answers `unknown` for a dead or stalled child (Task 37); anything but `outcome: 'ok'` is null.

```ts
// The one-task rule against real Collab (spec §7.2, §12.2 "One-task rule"): a remote session rooted at a linked
// worktree of the Air clone (the mirror, as createMirror leaves it) and an Air session in the clone itself, both on one
// temp shared journal. No fetch is needed: the rule reads only Collab's task projection.
import { afterEach, describe, expect, test } from 'bun:test'
import { mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { dirname, join } from 'node:path'
import { mirrorBusy } from '../src/air/busy.ts'
import { CollabChild } from '../src/air/children.ts'
import { listTasks, readTask, taskFromResult, tasksFromResult } from '../src/air/tasks.ts'
import type { ToolResult } from '../src/link/messages.ts'
import { cleanupTmps, COLLAB_DIST, makeRepo, repoGit, temp } from './helpers.ts'
import { collabHarness, type StdioHarness } from './mcp-harness.ts'

const running: Array<() => Promise<unknown>> = []
afterEach(async () => {
  for (const stop of running.splice(0).reverse()) await stop()
  cleanupTmps()
})

const T = 30_000 // each world starts two Collab children

async function startChild(journal: string, home: string): Promise<CollabChild> {
  const c = await CollabChild.start({ bun: process.execPath, dist: COLLAB_DIST, journal, home })
  if (!(c instanceof CollabChild)) throw new Error(`a Collab child did not start: ${c.lastErrLine}`)
  running.push(() => c.stop())
  return c
}

/** A Collab call that must succeed; returns its structuredContent. */
async function ok(child: CollabChild, name: string, args: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<any> {
  const o = await child.call(name, args)
  if (o.outcome === 'unknown') throw new Error(`${name}: no answer (${o.reason})`)
  if (o.outcome === 'error') throw new Error(`${name}: ${JSON.stringify(o.result.structuredContent)}`)
  return o.result.structuredContent
}

async function airOk(air: StdioHarness, name: string, args: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<any> {
  const r = await air.callTool(name, args)
  if (r.isError) throw new Error(`${name}: ${JSON.stringify(r.structuredContent)}`)
  return r.structuredContent
}

/**
 * Collab's minimum lease is 30 s and its store reads its own wall clock, so no test can wait for an expiry within its
 * 10 s budget. This moves one temp journal's lease into the past with the sqlite3 CLI, under the write guard Collab's
 * own v0.2 writes use (inserted and removed in the same transaction); the event chain is untouched.
 */
function expireLease(journal: string, taskId: string): void {
  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/.test(taskId)) throw new Error('expireLease: test task ids are plain words')
  const sql = "BEGIN IMMEDIATE; INSERT INTO v2_write_guard (nonce, enabled) VALUES ('collab-bridge-test', 1); " +
    `UPDATE tasks SET lease_expires_at = '2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z' WHERE id = '${taskId}'; ` +
    "DELETE FROM v2_write_guard WHERE nonce = 'collab-bridge-test'; COMMIT;"
  const r = Bun.spawnSync(['/usr/bin/sqlite3', '-cmd', '.timeout 5000', journal, sql], { env: { PATH: '/usr/bin:/bin' }, stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'pipe' })
  if (r.exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(`expireLease: ${r.stderr.toString()}`)
}

interface World { root: string; home: string; journal: string; base: string; ws: string; mirrorWt: string; remote: CollabChild; air: StdioHarness }

async function world(): Promise<World> {
  const root = temp('cb-busy-')
  const home = join(root, 'home')
  mkdirSync(home)
  const airClone = join(root, 'air', 'collab-trial')
  const base = makeRepo(airClone)
  // The mirror as createMirror leaves it (Task 42): a detached linked worktree of the Air clone at the shared base.
  const mirror = join(root, 'collab-shared', 'mirrors', 'nuance', 'macair', '0123456789abcdef')
  mkdirSync(dirname(mirror), { recursive: true })
  repoGit(airClone, ['worktree', 'add', '--detach', mirror, base])
  const journal = join(root, 'collab-shared', 'collab.sqlite')
  const remote = await startChild(journal, home)
  const started = await ok(remote, 'collab_session_start', { root_path: mirror, actor: 'nuance/macair · self-declared: busy test' })
  const air = collabHarness({ journal, home })
  running.push(() => air.close())
  await air.initialize()
  const airStart = await airOk(air, 'collab_session_start', { root_path: airClone, actor: 'air reviewer' })
  // A linked worktree shares the clone's local-git key, so both sessions land in one workspace (K11).
  expect(airStart.workspace.id).toBe(started.workspace.id)
  return { root, home, journal, base, ws: started.workspace.id, mirrorWt: started.worktree.id, remote, air }
}

let n = 0
const key = () => `busy-key-${++n}`

function createEdit(w: World, id: string, o: { policy?: 'accepted' | 'reported' } = {}): Promise<any> {
  return airOk(w.air, 'collab_task_create', { workspace_id: w.ws, idempotency_key: key(), task_id: id, title: `task ${id}`,
    work_mode: 'edit', completion_policy: o.policy ?? 'accepted', path_scopes: ['notes'], expected_base_sha: w.base }).then((r) => r.task)
}
const remoteClaim = (w: World, t: any) =>
  ok(w.remote, 'collab_task_claim', { workspace_id: w.ws, task_id: t.id, idempotency_key: key(), expected_version: t.version }).then((r) => r.task)
const remoteComplete = (w: World, t: any) =>
  ok(w.remote, 'collab_task_complete', { workspace_id: w.ws, task_id: t.id, lease_id: t.lease_id, idempotency_key: key(),
    expected_version: t.version, summary: 'done' }).then((r) => r.task)
const airReview = (w: World, t: any, outcome: 'accept' | 'request_changes') =>
  airOk(w.air, 'collab_task_review', { workspace_id: w.ws, task_id: t.id, idempotency_key: key(), expected_version: t.version,
    outcome, summary: outcome === 'accept' ? 'looks right' : 'please change' }).then((r) => r.task)

describe('task views', () => {
  const task = {
    id: 'A', workspace_id: 'ws_x', title: 'x', status: 'claimed', effective_status: 'recovery_required', work_mode: 'edit',
    completion_policy: 'accepted', review_status: 'not_required', assignee_session_id: 'session_1', lease_id: 'lease_1',
    lease_expires_at: '2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z', expected_base_sha: 'a'.repeat(40),
    base_checkpoint: { worktree_id: 'wt_1', head_sha: 'a'.repeat(40), index_sha256: 'b'.repeat(64), source: 'server_observed' },
    claim_worktree_id: 'wt_1', result_checkpoint: null, path_scopes: ['notes'], version: 3, assignee: 'nuance/macair · self-declared: x',
  }
  const result = (sc: Record<string, unknown>, isError = false): ToolResult => ({ content: [{ type: 'text', text: '{}' }], structuredContent: sc, ...(isError ? { isError } : {}) })

  test('taskFromResult keeps exactly the fields the hub decides on', () => {
    expect(taskFromResult(result({ task }))).toEqual({
      id: 'A', version: 3, status: 'claimed', effective_status: 'recovery_required', work_mode: 'edit', completion_policy: 'accepted',
      review_status: 'not_required', assignee_session_id: 'session_1', lease_id: 'lease_1', lease_expires_at: '2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z',
      expected_base_sha: 'a'.repeat(40), base_checkpoint: { worktree_id: 'wt_1', head_sha: 'a'.repeat(40) }, claim_worktree_id: 'wt_1',
      result_checkpoint: null, path_scopes: ['notes'],
    })
  })

  test('an isError result, a missing task or a malformed field reads as null', () => {
    expect(taskFromResult(result({ task }, true))).toBeNull()
    expect(taskFromResult(result({}))).toBeNull()
    expect(taskFromResult(result({ task: { ...task, status: 'done' } }))).toBeNull()
    expect(taskFromResult(result({ task: { ...task, version: 0 } }))).toBeNull()
    expect(taskFromResult(result({ task: { ...task, claim_worktree_id: 7 } }))).toBeNull()
    expect(taskFromResult(result({ task: { ...task, base_checkpoint: { head_sha: 'a'.repeat(40) } } }))).toBeNull()
    expect(taskFromResult(result({ task: { ...task, path_scopes: ['notes', 3] } }))).toBeNull()
  })

  test('one malformed entry makes a whole task page unreadable', () => {
    expect(tasksFromResult(result({ tasks: [task, task] }))?.length).toBe(2)
    expect(tasksFromResult(result({ tasks: [task, { ...task, work_mode: 'write' }] }))).toBeNull()
    expect(tasksFromResult(result({ tasks: 'none' }))).toBeNull()
  })
})

describe('the one-task rule', () => {
  test('a claimed edit task on the mirror keeps it busy', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const a = await remoteClaim(w, await createEdit(w, 'A'))
    expect(a.claim_worktree_id).toBe(w.mirrorWt)
    expect(await mirrorBusy(w.remote, w.ws, w.mirrorWt, 'B')).toEqual({ busy: true, holder: 'A', reason: 'claimed' })
  }, T)

  test('a pending review keeps it busy', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const a = await remoteComplete(w, await remoteClaim(w, await createEdit(w, 'A')))
    expect([a.status, a.review_status, a.claim_worktree_id]).toEqual(['completed', 'pending', null])
    expect(a.result_checkpoint.worktree_id).toBe(w.mirrorWt)
    expect(await mirrorBusy(w.remote, w.ws, w.mirrorWt, 'B')).toEqual({ busy: true, holder: 'A', reason: 'pending_review' })
  }, T)

  test('a recovery_required claim keeps it busy, also when read by a fresh child as after a hub restart', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    await remoteClaim(w, await createEdit(w, 'A'))
    expireLease(w.journal, 'A')
    expect((await readTask(w.remote, w.ws, 'A'))?.effective_status).toBe('recovery_required')
    expect(await mirrorBusy(w.remote, w.ws, w.mirrorWt, 'B')).toEqual({ busy: true, holder: 'A', reason: 'claimed' })
    const fresh = await startChild(w.journal, w.home) // unbound, as the hub's children are right after a restart
    expect(await mirrorBusy(fresh, w.ws, w.mirrorWt, 'B')).toEqual({ busy: true, holder: 'A', reason: 'claimed' })
  }, T)

  test('request_changes frees it and a reissue is not busy', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const a = await remoteComplete(w, await remoteClaim(w, await createEdit(w, 'A')))
    const back = await airReview(w, a, 'request_changes')
    expect([back.status, back.review_status]).toEqual(['open', 'changes_requested'])
    expect(await mirrorBusy(w.remote, w.ws, w.mirrorWt, 'A')).toEqual({ busy: false })
    await createEdit(w, 'A2') // the creator's reissue on a new base (§7.2); the old task holds nothing
    expect(await mirrorBusy(w.remote, w.ws, w.mirrorWt, 'A2')).toEqual({ busy: false })
  }, T)

  test('a remote block frees it', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const a = await remoteClaim(w, await createEdit(w, 'A'))
    await ok(w.remote, 'collab_task_block', { workspace_id: w.ws, task_id: 'A', lease_id: a.lease_id, idempotency_key: key(),
      expected_version: a.version, blocker: 'waiting for Yu' })
    expect(await mirrorBusy(w.remote, w.ws, w.mirrorWt, 'B')).toEqual({ busy: false })
  }, T)

  test('an Air-side accept frees it', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const a = await remoteComplete(w, await remoteClaim(w, await createEdit(w, 'A')))
    expect((await airReview(w, a, 'accept')).review_status).toBe('accepted')
    expect(await mirrorBusy(w.remote, w.ws, w.mirrorWt, 'B')).toEqual({ busy: false })
  }, T)

  test('an Air-side recover-release frees it', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    await remoteClaim(w, await createEdit(w, 'A'))
    expireLease(w.journal, 'A')
    const expired = await readTask(w.remote, w.ws, 'A')
    const released = await airOk(w.air, 'collab_task_recover', { workspace_id: w.ws, task_id: 'A', idempotency_key: key(),
      expected_version: expired!.version, action: 'release', recovery_note: 'the remote seat went quiet' })
    expect(released.task.status).toBe('open')
    expect(await mirrorBusy(w.remote, w.ws, w.mirrorWt, 'B')).toEqual({ busy: false })
  }, T)

  test('a reported-policy completion frees it', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const a = await remoteComplete(w, await remoteClaim(w, await createEdit(w, 'A', { policy: 'reported' })))
    expect([a.status, a.review_status]).toEqual(['completed', 'not_required'])
    expect(await mirrorBusy(w.remote, w.ws, w.mirrorWt, 'B')).toEqual({ busy: false })
  }, T)

  test('the task claimed on the mirror is not busy for itself', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    await remoteClaim(w, await createEdit(w, 'A'))
    expect(await mirrorBusy(w.remote, w.ws, w.mirrorWt, 'A')).toEqual({ busy: false })
    expect((await listTasks(w.remote, w.ws, 'claimed'))?.map((t) => t.id)).toEqual(['A'])
  }, T)

  test('a dead child is busy read_failed', async () => {
    const root = temp('cb-busy-dead-')
    const child = await startChild(join(root, 'collab.sqlite'), root)
    await child.stop()
    expect(await mirrorBusy(child, 'ws_none', 'wt_none', 'A')).toEqual({ busy: true, holder: null, reason: 'read_failed' })
    expect(await readTask(child, 'ws_none', 'A')).toBeNull()
  }, T)

  test('an unknown mirror id is busy mirror_unknown', async () => {
    const root = temp('cb-busy-unknown-')
    const child = await startChild(join(root, 'collab.sqlite'), root)
    await child.stop()
    // Decided before any read: even a dead child answers mirror_unknown, not read_failed.
    expect(await mirrorBusy(child, 'ws_none', null, 'A')).toEqual({ busy: true, holder: null, reason: 'mirror_unknown' })
  }, T)
})
```

```ts
// Collab's task projection as the hub reads it (C11, spec §7.2, K60). Before an edit flow the hub reads the task, or one
// status page of the bound workspace's tasks, through the lineage's own child: Collab's own state every time, never a
// copy the hub keeps. The field names are Collab's Task and RepoCheckpoint (packages/collab/src/protocol.ts:81-91,
// 253-296); a view keeps only what the hub decides on. A result without this exact shape reads as null, and every
// caller treats null as a failed read, never as "no task" or "nothing claimed" (fail closed).
import type { ToolResult } from '../link/messages.ts'
import type { CollabChild } from './children.ts'

export interface CheckpointView { worktree_id: string; head_sha: string | null }
export interface TaskView { id: string; version: number; status: 'open' | 'claimed' | 'blocked' | 'completed'; effective_status: string;
  work_mode: 'coordination' | 'read_only' | 'edit'; completion_policy: 'reported' | 'accepted'; review_status: string;
  assignee_session_id: string | null; lease_id: string | null; lease_expires_at: string | null; expected_base_sha: string | null;
  base_checkpoint: CheckpointView | null; claim_worktree_id: string | null; result_checkpoint: CheckpointView | null; path_scopes: string[] }

type Obj = Record<string, unknown>
const isObj = (v: unknown): v is Obj => typeof v === 'object' && v !== null && !Array.isArray(v)
const isStr = (v: unknown): v is string => typeof v === 'string'
const isStrOrNull = (v: unknown): v is string | null => v === null || typeof v === 'string'
const STATUSES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(['open', 'claimed', 'blocked', 'completed'])
const MODES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(['coordination', 'read_only', 'edit'])
const POLICIES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(['reported', 'accepted'])

/** A checkpoint view, null for "no checkpoint", or undefined when the value is malformed. */
function checkpointOf(v: unknown): CheckpointView | null | undefined {
  if (v === null) return null
  if (!isObj(v) || !isStr(v.worktree_id) || !isStrOrNull(v.head_sha)) return undefined
  return { worktree_id: v.worktree_id, head_sha: v.head_sha }
}

function parseTask(v: unknown): TaskView | null {
  if (!isObj(v)) return null
  const { id, version, status, effective_status, work_mode, completion_policy, review_status } = v
  if (!isStr(id) || !Number.isSafeInteger(version) || (version as number) < 1) return null
  if (!isStr(status) || !STATUSES.has(status) || !isStr(effective_status)) return null
  if (!isStr(work_mode) || !MODES.has(work_mode) || !isStr(completion_policy) || !POLICIES.has(completion_policy)) return null
  if (!isStr(review_status)) return null
  const { assignee_session_id, lease_id, lease_expires_at, expected_base_sha, claim_worktree_id, path_scopes } = v
  if (![assignee_session_id, lease_id, lease_expires_at, expected_base_sha, claim_worktree_id].every(isStrOrNull)) return null
  if (!Array.isArray(path_scopes) || !path_scopes.every(isStr)) return null
  const base = checkpointOf(v.base_checkpoint)
  const result = checkpointOf(v.result_checkpoint)
  if (base === undefined || result === undefined) return null
  return {
    id, version: version as number, status: status as TaskView['status'], effective_status,
    work_mode: work_mode as TaskView['work_mode'], completion_policy: completion_policy as TaskView['completion_policy'], review_status,
    assignee_session_id: assignee_session_id as string | null, lease_id: lease_id as string | null,
    lease_expires_at: lease_expires_at as string | null, expected_base_sha: expected_base_sha as string | null,
    base_checkpoint: base, claim_worktree_id: claim_worktree_id as string | null, result_checkpoint: result,
    path_scopes: [...path_scopes],
  }
}

/** structuredContent.task of a successful result (task_get, claim, complete, recover, review all answer this way). */
export function taskFromResult(r: ToolResult): TaskView | null {
  if (r.isError === true || !isObj(r.structuredContent)) return null
  return parseTask(r.structuredContent.task)
}

/** structuredContent.tasks of a successful task_list; one malformed entry makes the whole page unreadable. */
export function tasksFromResult(r: ToolResult): TaskView[] | null {
  if (r.isError === true || !isObj(r.structuredContent) || !Array.isArray(r.structuredContent.tasks)) return null
  const out: TaskView[] = []
  for (const t of r.structuredContent.tasks) {
    const view = parseTask(t)
    if (!view) return null
    out.push(view)
  }
  return out
}

/** One collab_task_get through `child`; anything but a readable task (an isError, an unknown outcome) is null. */
export async function readTask(child: CollabChild, workspaceId: string, taskId: string): Promise<TaskView | null> {
  const o = await child.call('collab_task_get', { workspace_id: workspaceId, task_id: taskId })
  return o.outcome === 'ok' ? taskFromResult(o.result) : null
}

/** One collab_task_list page for one status (Collab's list does not paginate, K60); null when it cannot be read. */
export async function listTasks(child: CollabChild, workspaceId: string, status: 'claimed' | 'completed'): Promise<TaskView[] | null> {
  const o = await child.call('collab_task_list', { workspace_id: workspaceId, status })
  return o.outcome === 'ok' ? tasksFromResult(o.result) : null
}
```

`/Users/yuai/Projects/.worktrees/agenttool-collab-bridge/packages/collab-bridge/src/air/busy.ts`:

```ts
// The one-task rule (R36, spec §7.2): one edit task per mirror at a time, derived from Collab's own task projection at
// every check and never stored. Without it a second task's sync would move the mirror under a pending review, which
// could then never pass (K16). Because it reads Collab every time, request_changes, block, release, Air-side reviews and
// recoveries, refused claims and hub restarts need no bookkeeping here. A read that fails is busy, never free.
import type { CollabChild } from './children.ts'
import { listTasks } from './tasks.ts'

export type Busy = { busy: false } | { busy: true; holder: string | null; reason: 'claimed' | 'pending_review' | 'read_failed' | 'mirror_unknown' }

/**
 * Whether another edit task (not `taskId`) holds the mirror whose Collab worktree id is `mirrorWorktreeId`: claimed on it
 * (recovery_required included, since an expired claim keeps status `claimed` and its claim_worktree_id, K12), or completed
 * there and still waiting for review (K60). An unknown worktree id (no remote session has bound to the mirror yet) is
 * busy too, because nothing can be matched against it.
 */
export async function mirrorBusy(child: CollabChild, workspaceId: string, mirrorWorktreeId: string | null, taskId: string): Promise<Busy> {
  if (mirrorWorktreeId === null) return { busy: true, holder: null, reason: 'mirror_unknown' }
  const claimed = await listTasks(child, workspaceId, 'claimed')
  if (claimed === null) return { busy: true, holder: null, reason: 'read_failed' }
  for (const t of claimed) {
    if (t.id !== taskId && t.work_mode === 'edit' && t.claim_worktree_id === mirrorWorktreeId) return { busy: true, holder: t.id, reason: 'claimed' }
  }
  const completed = await listTasks(child, workspaceId, 'completed')
  if (completed === null) return { busy: true, holder: null, reason: 'read_failed' }
  for (const t of completed) {
    if (t.id !== taskId && t.work_mode === 'edit' && t.review_status === 'pending' && t.result_checkpoint?.worktree_id === mirrorWorktreeId) {
      return { busy: true, holder: t.id, reason: 'pending_review' }
    }
  }
  return { busy: false }
}
```
