### Task 44: Sync-point plans

**Kind:** [implementer] · **Group:** 14 · **Spec:** §7.2 (when to sync for claim and complete; never before review or takeover; every other state forwards unchanged), §7.3 step 7 (base from expected_base_sha, else the claim's base checkpoint; remote_base_unknown), §7.5 (remote_uncommitted), §9.2 `remote_review_required` ("a remote claim or takeover of one"), §12.2 Policy "remote_review_required at claim and takeover"; R11, R13, R40.

A plan says what the hub does with one remote claim, complete or takeover once it has read the task: sync (and with which base and scopes), forward unchanged, or refuse with a definite "not sent". It is pure, so every branch is a one-line table test; Task 45 runs it under the mirror's lock. The rule that decides everything is §7.2's "only when Collab could newly apply the call": a replay of a call that already applied, a duplicate under a new key, an expired lease or a completed task is forwarded without a sync, so Collab returns its stored receipt (K61) or refuses, and the mirror never moves for it. For a claim, "could newly apply" is read wide (P67): a task held on another worktree, a blocked task and a legacy lease_expired claim can all be claimable by the time the forward reaches Collab, so they sync, and another session's claim on this very mirror is `mirror_busy` instead.

The one exception is R40, and it comes before the state: a reported-policy edit task is refused `remote_review_required` at claim and at complete whatever state the hub reads it in. The mirror lock serialises hub children, not Air sessions, so a task read as claimed or blocked can be open again by the time the forward reaches Collab (an Air session releases or unblocks it in between), and Collab's claim checks no completion policy. A legacy-path claim whose lease ran out (`status: 'claimed'`, `assignee_session_id: null`, `effective_status: 'lease_expired'`) needs no race at all: Collab's session claim reopens it and re-claims it for the caller in one write (KN `src/store.ts:2484-2493`). A remote seat that got a reported edit task either way could then complete it with `review_status: 'not_required'`, which satisfies dependents at once (K60). No remote claim of one can ever have applied through the hub, so there is no receipt a replay could be owed, and refusing at complete too closes the path even if a claim slipped through.

```ts
// src/air/sync-points.ts
export type Plan =
  | { kind: 'sync'; atComplete?: { base: string; scopes: string[] } }
  | { kind: 'forward' }
  | { kind: 'refuse'; code: AgentCode; message: string }
export function baseOf(task: TaskView): string | null                       // expected_base_sha ?? base_checkpoint?.head_sha ?? null
export function planClaim(task: TaskView, o: { sessionId: string; mirrorWorktreeId: string | null; declared: Declared | undefined }): Plan
//   non-edit → forward; completion_policy 'reported' → remote_review_required in every state (R40); completed → forward;
//   claimed or blocked by o.sessionId → forward (this seat's replay or duplicate); claimed on this mirror by another session →
//   mirror_busy; otherwise (open, held on another worktree, blocked, legacy lease_expired; P67): no declared → fetch_failed;
//   expected_base_sha set and declared head differs → expected_base_mismatch (no fetch); else sync
export function planComplete(task: TaskView, o: { sessionId: string; leaseId: unknown; nowMs: number; declared: Declared | undefined }): Plan
//   non-edit → forward; completion_policy 'reported' → remote_review_required in every state (R40); claimed by this session
//   with this lease: dirty → remote_uncommitted; < 150 s left → lease_too_short; no base → remote_base_unknown; else sync
//   atComplete {base, scopes}; any other state → forward
export function planTakeover(task: TaskView): Plan                          // edit + reported → remote_review_required; else forward (never sync)
export interface MirrorHandle { spec: MirrorSpec; lock: MirrorLock; worktreeId: string | null }
export class MirrorRegistry { get(device: string, user: string, mirrorId: string): MirrorHandle | undefined; set(h: MirrorHandle): void; all(): MirrorHandle[] }
//   set() replaces the handle for (device, user, mirrorId) and keeps its lock, so a recorded worktree id reaches every later call
```
- Also produced (this task's additions; the signatures above are unchanged):
  - `export const PLAN_MESSAGES` — the messages of the seven refusals (`reviewRequired`, `baseMismatch`, `uncommitted`, `leaseTooShort`, `baseUnknown`, `noDeclared`, `heldOnMirror`); Task 45 reuses `noDeclared`.
  - A plan that would sync without `declared` refuses `fetch_failed` with `PLAN_MESSAGES.noDeclared` (a definite not sent): the sync needs the declared head (§7.3 step 5) and the dirty flag (§7.5), and P48 already answers `fetch_failed` when the pipe cannot read its folder's git state. Branches that forward or refuse earlier never look at `declared`.

Notes for the implementer:
- `planClaim` order: not an edit task → forward; `reported` → `remote_review_required` (R40), in every state, before the status is looked at (see above: a race with an Air session, or a legacy lease_expired claim, would otherwise reach Collab with no R40 check); `completed` → forward (a reopened task reads `open`); `claimed` or `blocked` with `assignee_session_id === o.sessionId` → forward (this seat's own replay or duplicate: Collab answers, and the mirror stays where this task left it, so a later takeover still finds HEAD at the base); `claimed` with `claim_worktree_id === o.mirrorWorktreeId` (and that id known) → `mirror_busy` with `PLAN_MESSAGES.heldOnMirror` (another session's claim holds this mirror, `recovery_required` included, the same as `mirrorBusy` counts it); every other state takes the open path (P67): no `declared` → `fetch_failed`; `expected_base_sha` set and the declared head differs → `expected_base_mismatch`, decided before any fetch so the mirror never moves for a claim Collab would refuse (K15); otherwise `{kind: 'sync'}` with no `atComplete`. Collab stores `expected_base_sha` lower-cased (KN `src/store.ts:6266-6275`) and Task 15's `parseCall` accepts a declared head only as lower-case 40 or 64 hex, so the comparison is exact.
- `planComplete` order: not an edit task → forward; `reported` → `remote_review_required` (R40), in every state; not `claimed` by `o.sessionId` with `o.leaseId === task.lease_id` → forward; the lease already expired on the Air's wall clock (`Date.parse(lease_expires_at) <= nowMs`, K26) → forward, so Collab refuses it; no `declared` → `fetch_failed`; dirty → `remote_uncommitted`; less than `TIMING.leaseMinRemainingMs` (150000 ms) left → `lease_too_short`; no base → `remote_base_unknown`; otherwise sync with `atComplete: {base: baseOf(task), scopes: [...task.path_scopes]}`. Exactly 150 s left syncs.
- `MirrorRegistry` keys handles by `` `${device}/${user}/${mirrorId}` ``; `set` of an existing key keeps the old `lock` object, so flows already queued on it stay serialised with every later one (P25).

```ts
// When the hub syncs a mirror (R11, spec §7.2): before a remote claim or complete of an edit task, and only when Collab
// could newly apply the call. Every other state (a replay of a call that already applied, a duplicate under a new key,
// an expired lease, a task completed, reopened or held by someone else) is forwarded unchanged without a sync, so Collab
// returns its stored receipt (K61) or refuses, and a skipped sync never moves the mirror. Review and takeover are never
// synced: review compares the mirror with itself at the completed commit, and takeover needs HEAD == expected_base (K15).
// The one rule that comes before the state is R40: a reported-policy edit task is refused at claim and complete in every
// state. The lock does not serialise Air sessions, so a task read as claimed may be open by the forward, and a legacy
// lease_expired claim is reopened and claimed by Collab in one write; no remote claim of one ever applied, so no replay
// is owed a receipt.
// Pure: the caller reads the task first (Task 43) and runs the plan under the mirror's lock (Task 45).
import type { AgentCode } from '../failure.ts'
import type { Declared } from '../link/messages.ts'
import { TIMING } from '../timing.ts'
import type { MirrorLock, MirrorSpec } from './mirror.ts'
import type { TaskView } from './tasks.ts'

export type Plan =
  | { kind: 'sync'; atComplete?: { base: string; scopes: string[] } }
  | { kind: 'forward' }
  | { kind: 'refuse'; code: AgentCode; message: string }

const FORWARD: Plan = { kind: 'forward' }
const refuse = (code: AgentCode, message: string): Plan => ({ kind: 'refuse', code, message })

export const PLAN_MESSAGES = {
  reviewRequired: 'Remote seats cannot work on an edit task that skips review (completion_policy reported); ask its creator for completion_policy accepted.',
  baseMismatch: "This folder's HEAD is not the task's expected base; nothing was sent. Check out the base, or ask the creator to reissue the task.",
  uncommitted: 'This folder has uncommitted changes; nothing was sent. Commit your edits on this Mac, then complete.',
  leaseTooShort: 'Less than 150 s of lease is left; nothing was sent. Renew the lease, then complete.',
  baseUnknown: 'The task has no expected base and its claim recorded no base commit, so the hub cannot hold the commit to it; nothing was sent.',
  noDeclared: 'The call carried no git state from this folder, so the hub cannot check it; nothing was sent.',
  heldOnMirror: "Another session's claim of this task holds this folder's mirror; nothing was sent. Wait for it to be released or completed.",
} as const

/** The commit a completion is held to (§7.3 step 7): the task's expected base, else the head its claim recorded. */
export function baseOf(task: TaskView): string | null {
  return task.expected_base_sha ?? task.base_checkpoint?.head_sha ?? null
}

/** A remote claim (§7.2): a reported-policy edit task is refused in every state (R40, §9.2 "a remote claim or takeover of
 *  one"); a completed task and this seat's own claim are forwarded (Collab answers, a replay gets its receipt, and the
 *  mirror stays where this seat's task left it); another session's claim on this mirror is mirror_busy (R36); every
 *  other state syncs (P67), because the lock does not serialise Air sessions: a task read as claimed elsewhere or blocked
 *  can be open by the forward, and a legacy lease_expired claim is reopened and claimed by Collab in one write. */
export function planClaim(task: TaskView, o: { sessionId: string; mirrorWorktreeId: string | null; declared: Declared | undefined }): Plan {
  if (task.work_mode !== 'edit') return FORWARD
  if (task.completion_policy === 'reported') return refuse('remote_review_required', PLAN_MESSAGES.reviewRequired) // R40: in every state
  if (task.status === 'completed') return FORWARD // Collab answers; a reopened task reads open
  if (task.status !== 'open' && task.assignee_session_id === o.sessionId) return FORWARD // this seat's own: a replay or a duplicate
  // Another session's claim holds this mirror (recovery_required included), so a sync would move it under that task (R36).
  if (task.status === 'claimed' && o.mirrorWorktreeId !== null && task.claim_worktree_id === o.mirrorWorktreeId) {
    return refuse('mirror_busy', PLAN_MESSAGES.heldOnMirror)
  }
  if (!o.declared) return refuse('fetch_failed', PLAN_MESSAGES.noDeclared)
  // Refused without fetching, so the mirror never moves for a claim that would fail Collab's own base check (K15).
  if (task.expected_base_sha !== null && o.declared.head !== task.expected_base_sha) return refuse('expected_base_mismatch', PLAN_MESSAGES.baseMismatch)
  return { kind: 'sync' }
}

/** A remote complete (§7.2, §7.3 step 7, §7.5): sync only while this session's own lease could still complete it; a
 *  reported-policy edit task is refused in every state, so a claim that slipped past planClaim can never complete (R40). */
export function planComplete(task: TaskView, o: { sessionId: string; leaseId: unknown; nowMs: number; declared: Declared | undefined }): Plan {
  if (task.work_mode !== 'edit') return FORWARD
  if (task.completion_policy === 'reported') return refuse('remote_review_required', PLAN_MESSAGES.reviewRequired) // R40: in every state
  if (task.status !== 'claimed' || task.assignee_session_id !== o.sessionId || task.lease_id === null || o.leaseId !== task.lease_id) return FORWARD
  const expires = task.lease_expires_at === null ? Number.NaN : Date.parse(task.lease_expires_at)
  // Leases run on the Air's wall clock (K26), the same clock as nowMs. An expired lease is Collab's to refuse.
  if (!Number.isFinite(expires) || expires <= o.nowMs) return FORWARD
  if (!o.declared) return refuse('fetch_failed', PLAN_MESSAGES.noDeclared)
  if (o.declared.dirty) return refuse('remote_uncommitted', PLAN_MESSAGES.uncommitted)
  if (expires - o.nowMs < TIMING.leaseMinRemainingMs) return refuse('lease_too_short', PLAN_MESSAGES.leaseTooShort)
  const base = baseOf(task)
  if (base === null) return refuse('remote_base_unknown', PLAN_MESSAGES.baseUnknown)
  return { kind: 'sync', atComplete: { base, scopes: [...task.path_scopes] } }
}

/** A remote takeover (§7.2): never synced; a reported-policy edit task is refused (R40). */
export function planTakeover(task: TaskView): Plan {
  if (task.work_mode === 'edit' && task.completion_policy === 'reported') return refuse('remote_review_required', PLAN_MESSAGES.reviewRequired)
  return FORWARD
}

export interface MirrorHandle { spec: MirrorSpec; lock: MirrorLock; worktreeId: string | null }

/** The hub's mirrors by (device, user, mirror id). */
export class MirrorRegistry {
  private readonly handles = new Map<string, MirrorHandle>()

  private static key(device: string, user: string, mirrorId: string): string {
    return `${device}/${user}/${mirrorId}`
  }

  get(device: string, user: string, mirrorId: string): MirrorHandle | undefined {
    return this.handles.get(MirrorRegistry.key(device, user, mirrorId))
  }

  /** Replaces the handle for its (device, user, mirror id) but keeps the existing lock, so a worktree id recorded from the
   *  first session_start reaches every later call while flows already queued on the lock stay serialised with it. */
  set(h: MirrorHandle): void {
    const k = MirrorRegistry.key(h.spec.device, h.spec.user, h.spec.mirrorId)
    const old = this.handles.get(k)
    this.handles.set(k, old ? { ...h, lock: old.lock } : h)
  }

  all(): MirrorHandle[] {
    return [...this.handles.values()]
  }
}
```

### Task 45: Stamped edit flows

**Kind:** [implementer] · **Group:** 14 · **Spec:** §7.2 (the one-task rule runs only before a sync for X or a takeover of X; the tasks ref), §7.5 (HEAD equal to the base noted), §7.6 (stamps in the same write; rebuilt identically on a replay), §12.2 Git (a stable checkpoint across syncs; no sync before takeover or review), §12.2 Diff and size "a task with no expected base", §12.2 Replays (all seven lines), §12.2 One-task rule (request_changes then a re-claim fails expected_base_mismatch; a claim refused after its sync leaves the mirror free; `remote_head_moved` then a retry, and a failed checkout then a resync, both work); R11, R13, R14, R36, R38, R40.

`runEditFlow` is the one place a remote call can move or capture a mirror. It runs a whole remote claim, complete, takeover or artifact_attach under the mirror's lock (P25), held from the sync until the forwarded call returns, so only one hub child captures a mirror at a time and the capture runs outside Collab's write transaction (K15). Task 51's forwarder calls it for every `edit_flow` decision of the policy (Task 36) and turns a `refuse` into `bridgeFailure(code, message, call_ref, extra)`. Facts it builds on, measured on this Air against the tracked Collab dist and Tasks 37–42 for this plan:

- Collab answers a complete on an expired lease with `lease_expired`; a complete re-sent under a new key after the task completed with `version_conflict` (its CAS runs first, KN `src/store.ts:5794-5801`); a claim whose `expected_version` predates another session's claim with `version_conflict` too; and a claim over a scope another session holds with `path_scope_conflict` (K12). So the lost race of §12.2 ("a claim refused after its sync (task_claimed, …)") reaches Collab as `version_conflict`, never `task_claimed`: by the time the hub has read the task as open, any other claim has bumped its version. The test reproduces that race exactly and expects Collab's real code.
- A same-key replay with byte-identical arguments returns the stored response, the same object the first call returned (K24); a request that differs under that key would answer `idempotency_conflict`. The tests compare a replay's task with the first one's by `toEqual`.
- The session that held an expired lease may itself take the task over while the mirror is still at the base (the takeover recaptures the mirror and requires HEAD == expected_base, K15), so "a later takeover passes" runs on the same remote seat.
- `task.recovered` events carry the note as `payload.recovery_note`, and completion reports carry `limits`; `collab_events_since` and `collab_report_list` show both to the Air session.
- Task 42's `syncMirror` runs its checkout as `git -C <mirror> -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false checkout --detach -f --no-recurse-submodules <oid>` through `deps.git.run`, and restores with the same command naming the synced oid. The failed-checkout test wraps that `GitRunner` and fails exactly one checkout naming the fetched oid, so the restore and the resync run for real.
- Task 42's `mirrorHead` answers null when the mirror's `.git` file points nowhere (`gitdir: /nonexistent/…`), and `writeTaskRef` answers `mirror_tampered` when the ref already holds another commit.
- One world here is an Air clone, a Nuance clone made from it, a fetch through the fake ssh and the gate from source, and two Collab children: the file takes about 40 s on this Air; no single test waits more than 0.2 s on a timer.

```ts
// src/air/edit-flows.ts
export interface EditFlowCtx { flow: 'claim' | 'complete' | 'takeover' | 'attach'; name: string; args: Record<string, unknown>; declared: Declared | undefined;
  device: string; user: string; sessionId: string; workspaceId: string; child: CollabChild; mirror: MirrorHandle; mirrorDeps: MirrorDeps; nowMs: number;
  notAfterMono: number | null; mono: () => number }   // the forwarder's deadline on the hub's monotonic clock (Task 51); null: none
export type EditFlowOutcome = { kind: 'outcome'; outcome: CallOutcome } | { kind: 'refuse'; code: AgentCode; message: string; extra?: Record<string, unknown> }
export function runEditFlow(ctx: EditFlowCtx): Promise<EditFlowOutcome>
//   under ctx.mirror.lock for the whole flow: readTask (failure → refuse mirror_busy read_failed); plan first (planClaim,
//   planComplete or planTakeover); the busy check (mirrorBusy) runs only when the plan is `sync` or the flow is a takeover of an
//   edit task (§7.2: "before a sync for task X or a takeover of X"), so a replay or any other forwarded state reaches Collab and
//   gets its stored receipt (K61); sync when planned; complete: limits := completeLimitsStamp(oid = the fetched oid, or on a
//   replay/forward the result checkpoint's head, else the synced oid; headEqualsBase; seat limits) — the same bytes on a replay;
//   takeover: recovery_note := takeoverNoteStamp(synced oid, declared head, seat note); forward once through ctx.child.call;
//   a new successful completion writes the tasks ref from the returned task's result_checkpoint.head_sha (writeTaskRef answers
//   mirror_tampered when it differs from the mirror's HEAD; the flow still returns Collab's result and ledgers it, see below);
//   attach: forwarded under the lock; before each of the two forwards (attach, and the one child.call) a deadline that has
//   passed refuses hub_away FLOW_MESSAGES.late {reason: 'deadline_passed'} (also first thing under the lock and before a
//   sync), and a child that is no longer accepting() refuses hub_away FLOW_MESSAGES.childStopped: nothing is sent either way
```
- Also produced (this task's additions; the signatures above are unchanged):
  - `export const FLOW_MESSAGES` — the messages of `mirror_tampered`, `mirror_busy` (busy and read-failed), an unexpected sync fault, `late` (the call's deadline passed while it waited on the Air) and `childStopped` (the lineage's child was stopping when the call came to be forwarded).
  - `EditFlowCtx.notAfterMono` and `mono` (Task 51 passes the call's receipt time plus `timeout_ms` less `TIMING.callMinRemainingMs`, and its monotonic clock): the lock can be held for minutes by another lineage's capture, so the flow checks the deadline first thing under the lock, before a sync and before the forward, and refuses `hub_away` with `extra: {reason: 'deadline_passed'}`, which Task 51 ledgers as `deadline_passed`. A sync that ran before a late refusal leaves the mirror at the fetched commit with nothing forwarded, as Collab's own refusal would (§12.2).
  - Both forwards check `ctx.child.accepting()` in the same synchronous turn as `call` (Task 37): a child stopped while the call waited (a park, an end or a drain) answers `hub_away` with nothing sent, never `hub_outcome_unknown` (§9.3 item 3).
  - Before reading the task, claim, complete and takeover refuse `mirror_tampered` unless `mirrorHead` and `syncedOid` both answer and are equal: a mirror git cannot read, or one left off its synced commit (a crash between §7.3 steps 8 and 9), is never captured (K17), and Ai repairs it. artifact_attach skips both reads: it stores a uri and reads no file (K18), so it only waits for the lock.
  - `mirror_busy` refusals carry `extra: {holder_task_id, reason}` (the holder's task id, §9.2, and Task 43's reason); a failed task read carries `extra: {reason: 'read_failed'}`.
  - An edit takeover without `declared` refuses `fetch_failed` (`PLAN_MESSAGES.noDeclared`): its stamp names the declared head.
  - The seat's own `limits` and `recovery_note` pass through `normalizeText` (N2) before stamping. The policy (Task 36) has already applied N2 and N2 is idempotent, so this changes nothing on the hub's path and keeps a direct caller's bytes deterministic. A `limits` or `recovery_note` that is not a string is forwarded untouched, for Collab to refuse.
  - When the tasks ref cannot be written for a completion that applied, the flow still returns Collab's result (the call cannot be un-sent) and calls `mirrorDeps.ledger({event: 'tasks_ref', device, user, code: 'mirror_tampered' | 'missing', outcome: 'refused'})`; the reviewer then reads the result checkpoint's head (§7.7).
  - An exception thrown by `syncMirror` refuses `mirror_tampered` (nothing was forwarded, and the mirror's state is Ai's to check).

Notes for the implementer:
- The order inside the lock is the contract, and each step's test is named below: the mirror check; `readTask` through the lineage's own child; the plan; the busy check only for a sync plan or an edit takeover (planned first, so a same-key replay is forwarded even while another task holds the mirror); the sync; the stamp; one `child.call`; the tasks ref only for a new completion (`plan.kind === 'sync'` and outcome `ok`).
- The complete stamp's oid is the fetched oid for a new completion. For anything forwarded (a replay, a duplicate, an expired lease) it is the task's `result_checkpoint.head_sha`, else the synced oid, so a same-key replay rebuilds exactly the first request even after another task has moved the mirror (§7.6 "on a replay the hub takes the oid from the task's result checkpoint"). `headEqualsBase` compares that oid with `baseOf(task)`.
- Nothing here retries: a refused sync, a refused forward and an `unknown` outcome are each returned once (R18).

Tests it contains, by name, against the skeleton's list: every named test is here. The skeleton's `a claim refused by Collab after its sync (task_claimed; path_scope_conflict) leaves the mirror free for the next task` is named `… (a lost race to another claim; path_scope_conflict) …`, because Collab answers that race `version_conflict` (first fact above). Four more pin behaviour the code depends on: a claim and a takeover refused `mirror_busy` while another task awaits review, a completion whose tasks ref cannot be written, and artifact_attach waiting for the lock.

```ts
/** The git Nuance's INSTALLED records: the Air's own Homebrew git by its Cellar realpath, as `install check` would. */
function nuanceGit(): ResolvedGit {
  const path = realpathSync(REAL_GIT)
  const v = parseGitVersion(Bun.spawnSync([path, '--version'], { env: { PATH: '/usr/bin:/bin' } }).stdout.toString())!
  return { path, version: v.version, sha256: sha256File(path), guard: hasLazyFetchGuard(path), apple: v.apple }
}

const ALLOWLIST = ['version: 1', 'device: nuance', 'peers: [air]', 'runtimes:', '  - id: claude', '    models:', '      - model: sonnet',
  'folders:', '  - path: ~/Projects', '    access: review', '  - path: ~/Projects/collab-trial', '    access: edit',
  'limits:', '  max_concurrent: 1', '  starts_per_hour: 6', '  job_timeout_max: 30m', ''].join('\n')

/**
 * Collab's minimum lease is 30 s and its store reads its own wall clock, so no test can wait for an expiry within its
 * 10 s budget. This moves one temp journal's lease into the past with the sqlite3 CLI, under the write guard Collab's
 * own v0.2 writes use (inserted and removed in the same transaction); the event chain is untouched.
 */
function expireLease(journal: string, taskId: string): void {
  if (!/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$/.test(taskId)) throw new Error('expireLease: test task ids are plain words')
  const sql = "BEGIN IMMEDIATE; INSERT INTO v2_write_guard (nonce, enabled) VALUES ('collab-bridge-test', 1); " +
    `UPDATE tasks SET lease_expires_at = '2000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z' WHERE id = '${taskId}'; ` +
    "DELETE FROM v2_write_guard WHERE nonce = 'collab-bridge-test'; COMMIT;"
  const r = Bun.spawnSync(['/usr/bin/sqlite3', '-cmd', '.timeout 5000', journal, sql], { env: { PATH: '/usr/bin:/bin' }, stdout: 'pipe', stderr: 'pipe' })
  if (r.exitCode !== 0) throw new Error(`expireLease: ${r.stderr.toString()}`)
}

/** Faults a test can arm on the mirror's git runner: the next checkout of `checkoutOf` fails once. */
interface Faults { checkoutOf: string | null }

function faulty(g: GitRunner, faults: Faults): GitRunner {
  return {
    path: g.path,
    records: (args, o) => g.records(args, o),
    run: async (args, o) => {
      const target = faults.checkoutOf
      if (target !== null && args.includes('checkout') && args.some((a) => a.includes(target))) {
        faults.checkoutOf = null
        return { code: 1, stdout: new Uint8Array(), stderr: 'error: injected checkout failure\n', timedOut: false }
      }
      return g.run(args, o)
    },
  }
}

async function ok(child: CollabChild, name: string, args: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<any> {
  const o = await child.call(name, args)
  if (o.outcome === 'unknown') throw new Error(`${name}: no answer (${o.reason})`)
  if (o.outcome === 'error') throw new Error(`${name}: ${JSON.stringify(o.result.structuredContent)}`)
  return o.result.structuredContent
}

async function airOk(air: StdioHarness, name: string, args: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<any> {
  const r = await air.callTool(name, args)
  if (r.isError) throw new Error(`${name}: ${JSON.stringify(r.structuredContent)}`)
  return r.structuredContent
}

const tasksRef = (w: World, id: string): string | null => {

}

function createEdit(w: World, id: string, o: { base?: string | null; policy?: 'accepted' | 'reported'; scopes?: string[] } = {}): Promise<any> {

}

  o: { child?: CollabChild; nowMs?: number; notAfterMono?: number; mono?: () => number } = {}): EditFlowCtx {

    child: o.child ?? w.remote, mirror: w.handle, mirrorDeps: w.deps, nowMs: o.nowMs ?? Date.now(),
    notAfterMono: o.notAfterMono ?? null, mono: o.mono ?? (() => performance.now()) }
}

/** The task of a flow that reached Collab and succeeded. */
function taskOf(r: EditFlowOutcome): any {
  if (r.kind !== 'outcome') throw new Error(`refused: ${r.code} ${r.message}`)
  const o = r.outcome
  if (o.outcome === 'unknown') throw new Error(`no answer from Collab (${o.reason})`)
  if (o.outcome === 'error') throw new Error(`Collab: ${JSON.stringify(o.result.structuredContent)}`)
  return o.result.structuredContent!.task
}

/** Collab's own refusal code for a flow that reached Collab and was refused there. */
function collabError(r: EditFlowOutcome): string {
  if (r.kind !== 'outcome' || r.outcome.outcome !== 'error') throw new Error(`expected a Collab refusal, got ${JSON.stringify(r)}`)
  return String(r.outcome.result.structuredContent!.error)
}

async function claimed(w: World, id = 'T', o: { base?: string | null; scopes?: string[]; ttl?: number } = {}): Promise<any> {
  return taskOf(await claim(w, await createEdit(w, id, o), declaredOf(w), { ttl: o.ttl }))
}

async function completionLimits(w: World, t: any): Promise<string | null> {
  const reports = (await airOk(w.air, 'collab_report_list', { workspace_id: w.ws, task_id: t.id })).reports as any[]
  return reports.find((r) => r.id === t.completion_report_id)?.limits ?? null
}

const airReview = (w: World, t: any, outcome: 'accept' | 'request_changes') =>
  airOk(w.air, 'collab_task_review', { workspace_id: w.ws, task_id: t.id, idempotency_key: key(), expected_version: t.version,
    outcome, summary: outcome === 'accept' ? 'read the diff; it holds' : 'please change' }).then((r) => r.task)

/** A view of `child` that records every call, and can run something of its own just before one named call. */
function recording(child: CollabChild, before?: { name: string; run(): Promise<void> }) {
  const calls: Array<{ name: string; args: Record<string, unknown> }> = []
  let armed = before
  const proxy = new Proxy(child, {
    get(target, prop) {
      if (prop === 'call') {
        return async (name: string, args: Record<string, unknown>) => {
          calls.push({ name, args: structuredClone(args) })
          if (armed && armed.name === name) {
            const b = armed
            armed = undefined
            await b.run()
          }
          return target.call(name, args)
        }
      }
      const v = Reflect.get(target, prop, target)
      return typeof v === 'function' ? v.bind(target) : v
    },
  })
  return { child: proxy as CollabChild, calls }
}

const stampOf = (oid: string, o: { equalsBase?: boolean; seat?: string } = {}) =>
  `hub-observed: fetched ${oid} from nuance/macair via git-upload-pack v0; remote clean self-declared` +
  (o.equalsBase ? '; HEAD equals base' : '') + (o.seat ? `\nremote self-declared: ${o.seat}` : '')

describe('claim', () => {
  test('a claim syncs and passes its base check', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const before = fetches(w)
    const t = taskOf(await claim(w, await createEdit(w, 'T'), declaredOf(w)))
    expect([t.status, t.claim_worktree_id, t.base_checkpoint.head_sha]).toEqual(['claimed', w.handle.worktreeId, w.base])
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before + 1)
    expect(mirrorAt(w)).toBe(w.base)
  }, T)

  test('a claim whose declared head is not the expected base is refused before fetching', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const task = await createEdit(w, 'T')
    commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'early\n' }, 'work before the claim')
    const before = fetches(w)
    expect(await claim(w, task, declaredOf(w))).toMatchObject({ kind: 'refuse', code: 'expected_base_mismatch' })
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before)
    expect((await readTask(w.remote, w.ws, 'T'))?.status).toBe('open')
  }, T)

  test('a claim refused by Collab after its sync (a lost race to another claim; path_scope_conflict) leaves the mirror free for the next task', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    // path_scope_conflict: an Air session already holds notes/ in the same repository (K12).
    const held = await createEdit(w, 'HELD')
    await airOk(w.air, 'collab_task_claim', { workspace_id: w.ws, task_id: 'HELD', idempotency_key: key(), expected_version: held.version })
    const a = await createEdit(w, 'A')
    let before = fetches(w)
    expect(collabError(await claim(w, a, declaredOf(w)))).toBe('path_scope_conflict')
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before + 1) // it synced first, then Collab refused
    // A lost race: the task was open when the hub read it, and an Air session claimed it before the forward. The
    // seat's expected_version predates that claim, so Collab answers version_conflict (its CAS runs first).
    const b = await createEdit(w, 'B', { scopes: ['docs'] })
    const race = recording(w.remote, { name: 'collab_task_claim', run: async () => {
      await airOk(w.air, 'collab_task_claim', { workspace_id: w.ws, task_id: 'B', idempotency_key: key(), expected_version: b.version })
    } })
    before = fetches(w)
    expect(collabError(await claim(w, b, declaredOf(w), { child: race.child }))).toBe('version_conflict')
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before + 1)
    expect(await mirrorBusy(w.remote, w.ws, w.handle.worktreeId, 'C')).toEqual({ busy: false })
    expect(taskOf(await claim(w, await createEdit(w, 'C', { scopes: ['src'] }), declaredOf(w))).status).toBe('claimed')
  }, T)

  test('a claim while another edit task awaits review from the mirror is mirror_busy, and nothing is fetched', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const a = await claimed(w, 'A')
    commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'a\n' }, 'a')
    taskOf(await complete(w, a, declaredOf(w)))
    const b = await createEdit(w, 'B', { scopes: ['docs'], base: null })
    const before = fetches(w)
    expect(await claim(w, b, declaredOf(w))).toMatchObject({ kind: 'refuse', code: 'mirror_busy', extra: { holder_task_id: 'A', reason: 'pending_review' } })
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before)
  }, T)

  test('after request_changes a re-claim of the old task is expected_base_mismatch', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    const n1 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'first try\n' }, 'first try')
    const done = taskOf(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w)))
    const back = await airReview(w, done, 'request_changes')
    expect([back.status, back.expected_base_sha]).toEqual(['open', w.base])
    expect(await claim(w, back, declaredOf(w))).toMatchObject({ kind: 'refuse', code: 'expected_base_mismatch' })
    // The creator reissues on the rejected commit (§7.2); the old task holds nothing, so the reissue is not mirror_busy.
    const again = taskOf(await claim(w, await createEdit(w, 'T2', { base: n1 }), declaredOf(w)))
    expect([again.status, again.base_checkpoint.head_sha]).toEqual(['claimed', n1])
  }, T)
})

describe('complete', () => {
  test('a complete syncs, stamps limits and writes the tasks ref', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    const n1 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'hello from nuance\n' }, 'notes: hello')
    const before = fetches(w)
    const done = taskOf(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w), { limits: 'only notes/a.md changed' }))
    expect([done.status, done.review_status, done.result_checkpoint.head_sha]).toEqual(['completed', 'pending', n1])
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before + 1)
    expect(mirrorAt(w)).toBe(n1)
    expect(syncedAt(w)).toBe(n1)
    expect(tasksRef(w, 'T')).toBe(n1)
    expect(await completionLimits(w, done)).toBe(stampOf(n1, { seat: 'only notes/a.md changed' }))
  }, T)

  test('a completion whose tasks ref cannot be written still answers Collab\'s result and ledgers tasks_ref', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    repoGit(w.airClone, ['update-ref', mirrorRefs(w.spec).task('T'), w.base]) // a stale ref with another value
    const n1 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'applied\n' }, 'applied')
    const done = taskOf(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w)))
    expect(done.result_checkpoint.head_sha).toBe(n1) // the completion applied, so it is never reported as refused
    expect(tasksRef(w, 'T')).toBe(w.base)
    expect(w.ledger.filter((f) => f.event === 'tasks_ref')).toEqual([{ event: 'tasks_ref', device: 'nuance', user: 'macair', code: 'mirror_tampered', outcome: 'refused' }])
  }, T)

  test("an edit task without expected_base_sha diffs against its claim's base checkpoint head and completes", async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w, 'T', { base: null })
    expect([t.expected_base_sha, t.base_checkpoint.head_sha]).toEqual([null, w.base])
    const n1 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'no expected base\n' }, 'notes')
    const done = taskOf(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w)))
    expect(done.result_checkpoint.head_sha).toBe(n1)
    expect(await completionLimits(w, done)).toBe(stampOf(n1))
  }, T)

  test('a dirty complete is remote_uncommitted', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    const before = fetches(w)
    expect(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w, true))).toMatchObject({ kind: 'refuse', code: 'remote_uncommitted' })
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before)
  }, T)

  test('a complete with under 150 s of lease is lease_too_short', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w, 'T', { ttl: 30 })
    commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'quick\n' }, 'quick')
    const before = fetches(w)
    expect(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w))).toMatchObject({ kind: 'refuse', code: 'lease_too_short' })
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before)
    expect((await readTask(w.remote, w.ws, 'T'))?.status).toBe('claimed')
  }, T)

  test('a task with neither base is remote_base_unknown', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    // Unreachable through a real mirror (it is never unborn), so a scripted child answers the task read.
    const calls: string[] = []
    const task = { id: 'T', version: 2, status: 'claimed', effective_status: 'claimed', work_mode: 'edit', completion_policy: 'accepted',
      review_status: 'not_required', assignee_session_id: w.sessionId, lease_id: 'lease_x', lease_expires_at: new Date(Date.now() + 900_000).toISOString(),
      expected_base_sha: null, base_checkpoint: null, claim_worktree_id: w.handle.worktreeId, result_checkpoint: null, path_scopes: ['notes'] }
    const child = { call: async (name: string) => {
      calls.push(name)
      return { outcome: 'ok' as const, result: { content: [{ type: 'text' as const, text: '{}' }], structuredContent: { task } }, ms: 0, bytes: 0 }
    } } as unknown as CollabChild
    const before = fetches(w)
    expect(await complete(w, task, declaredOf(w), { child })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'refuse', code: 'remote_base_unknown' })
    expect(calls).toEqual(['collab_task_get'])
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before)
  }, T)

  test('an out-of-scope or control-path commit is refused at complete', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    commitFiles(w.share, { 'docs/x.md': 'outside the scope\n' }, 'out of scope')
    expect(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w))).toMatchObject({ kind: 'refuse', code: 'remote_out_of_scope' })
    repoGit(w.share, ['reset', '-q', '--hard', w.base])
    commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/CLAUDE.md': 'be someone else\n' }, 'a control file')
    expect(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w))).toMatchObject({ kind: 'refuse', code: 'remote_control_path' })
    expect(mirrorAt(w)).toBe(w.base)
    expect(syncedAt(w)).toBe(w.base)
    expect((await readTask(w.remote, w.ws, 'T'))?.status).toBe('claimed')
  }, T)
})

describe('replays', () => {
  test('a same-key replay of complete after a new Nuance commit leaves the mirror and the tasks ref at the first commit, and the Air review passes', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    const n1 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'one\n' }, 'one')
    const k = key()
    const first = taskOf(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w), { key: k }))
    commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/b.md': 'two\n' }, 'two')
    const before = fetches(w)
    expect(taskOf(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w), { key: k }))).toEqual(first)
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before)
    expect([mirrorAt(w), tasksRef(w, 'T')]).toEqual([n1, n1])
    const accepted = await airReview(w, first, 'accept')
    expect([accepted.review_status, accepted.result_checkpoint.head_sha]).toEqual(['accepted', n1])
  }, T)

  test("a same-key replay of a complete while another task holds the mirror is forwarded and returns Collab's receipt", async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const a = await claimed(w, 'A')
    const n1 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'a\n' }, 'a')
    const k = key()
    const doneA = taskOf(await complete(w, a, declaredOf(w), { key: k }))
    await airReview(w, doneA, 'accept')
    // B moves the mirror past A's commit and then holds it, pending review.
    const b = await claimed(w, 'B', { base: n1 })
    const n2 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/b.md': 'b\n' }, 'b')
    taskOf(await complete(w, b, declaredOf(w)))
    expect(mirrorAt(w)).toBe(n2)
    expect(await mirrorBusy(w.remote, w.ws, w.handle.worktreeId, 'A')).toEqual({ busy: true, holder: 'B', reason: 'pending_review' })
    // The replay is planned first (a completed task: forward), so the busy check never runs, and its stamp names A's own
    // result commit, not the mirror's current one, so Collab sees the identical request and returns the receipt.
    expect(taskOf(await complete(w, a, declaredOf(w), { key: k }))).toEqual(doneA)
    expect(mirrorAt(w)).toBe(n2)
  }, T)

  test('a duplicate complete under a new key leaves the mirror unmoved', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    const n1 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'a\n' }, 'a')
    taskOf(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w)))
    commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/b.md': 'b\n' }, 'b')
    const before = fetches(w)
    expect(collabError(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w)))).toBe('version_conflict')
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before)
    expect([mirrorAt(w), tasksRef(w, 'T')]).toEqual([n1, n1])
  }, T)

  test('a complete after the lease expired is forwarded without a sync, and a later takeover passes', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'late\n' }, 'late')
    expireLease(w.journal, 'T')
    const before = fetches(w)
    expect(collabError(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w)))).toBe('lease_expired')
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before)
    expect(mirrorAt(w)).toBe(w.base)
    const expired = (await readTask(w.remote, w.ws, 'T'))!
    expect(expired.effective_status).toBe('recovery_required')
    const back = taskOf(await takeover(w, expired, declaredOf(w), 'back after a drop'))
    expect([back.status, back.assignee_session_id, back.base_checkpoint.head_sha]).toEqual(['claimed', w.sessionId, w.base])
  }, T)

  test('a same-key claim replay leaves the mirror at the base', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const task = await createEdit(w, 'T')
    const k = key()
    const first = taskOf(await claim(w, task, declaredOf(w), { key: k }))
    commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'after the claim\n' }, 'work')
    const before = fetches(w)
    expect(taskOf(await claim(w, task, declaredOf(w), { key: k }))).toEqual(first)
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before)
    expect(mirrorAt(w)).toBe(w.base)
  }, T)

  test('a first-time complete still syncs', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    const n1 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'first\n' }, 'first')
    const before = fetches(w)
    taskOf(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w)))
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before + 1)
    expect(mirrorAt(w)).toBe(n1)
  }, T)

  test('the stamp is rebuilt identically on a replay', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    const n1 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'stamped\n' }, 'stamped')
    const rec = recording(w.remote)
    const k = key()
    const first = taskOf(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w), { key: k, limits: 'seat note\u202e', child: rec.child }))
    commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/b.md': 'moved on\n' }, 'moved on')
    const again = taskOf(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w), { key: k, limits: 'seat note\u202e', child: rec.child }))
    expect(again).toEqual(first)
    const sent = rec.calls.filter((c) => c.name === 'collab_task_complete').map((c) => c.args)
    expect(sent).toHaveLength(2)
    expect(sent[1]).toEqual(sent[0]!)
    expect(sent[0]!.limits).toBe(stampOf(n1, { seat: 'seat note' })) // N2 dropped the bidi override
  }, T)
})

describe('takeover, review and the mirror', () => {
  test('takeover is never synced and carries the recovery stamp', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    await claimed(w)
    const n1 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'work in progress\n' }, 'wip')
    expireLease(w.journal, 'T')
    const before = fetches(w)
    const expired = (await readTask(w.remote, w.ws, 'T'))!
    taskOf(await takeover(w, expired, declaredOf(w), 'picking it up again'))
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before)
    expect(mirrorAt(w)).toBe(w.base)
    const events = (await airOk(w.air, 'collab_events_since', { workspace_id: w.ws })).events as any[]
    const recovered = events.filter((e) => e.type === 'task.recovered').map((e) => e.payload.recovery_note)
    expect(recovered).toEqual([`hub-observed: mirror at ${w.base}, not refetched; device HEAD ${n1} self-declared\npicking it up again`])
  }, T)

  test('a takeover is refused mirror_busy while another edit task awaits review from the mirror', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const a = await claimed(w, 'A')
    commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'a\n' }, 'a')
    taskOf(await complete(w, a, declaredOf(w)))
    // B was claimed by an Air session and its lease ran out; the remote seat may not take it over onto a busy mirror.
    const b = await createEdit(w, 'B', { scopes: ['docs'], base: null })
    await airOk(w.air, 'collab_task_claim', { workspace_id: w.ws, task_id: 'B', idempotency_key: key(), expected_version: b.version })
    expireLease(w.journal, 'B')
    const expired = (await readTask(w.remote, w.ws, 'B'))!
    const rec = recording(w.remote)
    expect(await takeover(w, expired, declaredOf(w), 'taking B', { child: rec.child }))
      .toMatchObject({ kind: 'refuse', code: 'mirror_busy', extra: { holder_task_id: 'A', reason: 'pending_review' } })
    expect(rec.calls.map((c) => c.name)).not.toContain('collab_task_recover')
  }, T)

  test('a takeover of a reported-policy edit task is remote_review_required', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const task = await createEdit(w, 'R', { policy: 'reported' })
    const rec = recording(w.remote)
    expect(await takeover(w, task, declaredOf(w), 'mine now', { child: rec.child })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'refuse', code: 'remote_review_required' })
    expect(rec.calls.map((c) => c.name)).toEqual(['collab_task_get'])
  }, T)

  test('the checkpoint is stable across two syncs of the same commit', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    const before = fetches(w)
    const done = taskOf(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w))) // Nuance's HEAD is still the base: the same commit again
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before + 1)
    const pick = (c: any) => [c.head_sha, c.index_sha256, c.state_sha256]
    expect(pick(done.result_checkpoint)).toEqual(pick(t.base_checkpoint))
    expect(await completionLimits(w, done)).toBe(stampOf(w.base, { equalsBase: true }))
  }, T)

  test('remote_head_moved then a retry works', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'one\n' }, 'one')
    const stale = declaredOf(w)
    const n2 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/b.md': 'two\n' }, 'two')
    expect(await complete(w, t, stale)).toMatchObject({ kind: 'refuse', code: 'remote_head_moved' })
    expect(mirrorAt(w)).toBe(w.base)
    expect(taskOf(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w))).result_checkpoint.head_sha).toBe(n2)
  }, T)

  test('a failed checkout then a resync works', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    const n1 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'one\n' }, 'one')
    w.faults.checkoutOf = n1
    expect(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w))).toMatchObject({ kind: 'refuse', code: 'checkout_failed' })
    expect([mirrorAt(w), syncedAt(w)]).toEqual([w.base, w.base])
    expect(taskOf(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w))).result_checkpoint.head_sha).toBe(n1)
    expect(mirrorAt(w)).toBe(n1)
  }, T)

  test('no sync happens before review', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    const n1 = commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/a.md': 'reviewed\n' }, 'reviewed')
    const done = taskOf(await complete(w, t, declaredOf(w)))
    commitFiles(w.share, { 'notes/b.md': 'later work\n' }, 'later work')
    const before = fetches(w)
    expect((await airReview(w, done, 'accept')).review_status).toBe('accepted')
    expect(fetches(w)).toBe(before)
    expect(mirrorAt(w)).toBe(n1)
  }, T)

  test('an edit flow on a mirror whose HEAD cannot be read refuses mirror_tampered', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const task = await createEdit(w, 'T')
    writeFileSync(join(w.spec.mirrorPath, '.git'), 'gitdir: /nonexistent/collab-bridge-test\n')
    const rec = recording(w.remote)
    expect(await claim(w, task, declaredOf(w), { child: rec.child })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'refuse', code: 'mirror_tampered' })
    expect(rec.calls).toEqual([])
  }, T)

  test('artifact_attach is forwarded once and waits for the mirror lock', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    let release!: () => void
    const held = w.handle.lock.run(() => new Promise<void>((r) => { release = r }))
    const rec = recording(w.remote)
    const attach = runEditFlow(ctxOf(w, 'attach', 'collab_artifact_attach', { workspace_id: w.ws, task_id: t.id, lease_id: t.lease_id,
      idempotency_key: key(), expected_version: t.version, kind: 'file', uri: 'notes/a.md' }, undefined, { child: rec.child }))
    await Bun.sleep(200)
    expect(rec.calls).toEqual([])
    release()
    await held
    const r = await attach
    expect(r.kind === 'outcome' && r.outcome.outcome).toBe('ok')
    expect(rec.calls.map((c) => c.name)).toEqual(['collab_artifact_attach'])
  }, T)

  test('an attach whose deadline passes while the mirror lock is held is refused hub_away and never forwarded', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    let release!: () => void
    const held = w.handle.lock.run(() => new Promise<void>((r) => { release = r }))
    const rec = recording(w.remote)
    const clock = { mono: 5_000 }
    const attach = runEditFlow(ctxOf(w, 'attach', 'collab_artifact_attach', { workspace_id: w.ws, task_id: t.id, lease_id: t.lease_id,
      idempotency_key: key(), expected_version: t.version, kind: 'file', uri: 'notes/a.md' }, undefined,
      { child: rec.child, notAfterMono: 64_000, mono: () => clock.mono }))
    await Bun.sleep(50) // the held run has the lock; the attach waits behind it
    expect(rec.calls).toEqual([])
    clock.mono = 64_000 // the forwarder's notAfter: timeout_ms less TIMING.callMinRemainingMs
    release()
    await held
    expect(await attach).toEqual({ kind: 'refuse', code: 'hub_away', message: FLOW_MESSAGES.late, extra: { reason: 'deadline_passed' } })
    expect(rec.calls).toEqual([])
  }, T)

  test('an attach whose child stops while it waits for the mirror lock is refused hub_away and never forwarded', async () => {
    const w = await world()
    const t = await claimed(w)
    let release!: () => void
    const held = w.handle.lock.run(() => new Promise<void>((r) => { release = r }))
    const rec = recording(w.remote)
    const attach = runEditFlow(ctxOf(w, 'attach', 'collab_artifact_attach', { workspace_id: w.ws, task_id: t.id, lease_id: t.lease_id,
      idempotency_key: key(), expected_version: t.version, kind: 'file', uri: 'notes/a.md' }, undefined, { child: rec.child }))
    await Bun.sleep(50) // the held run has the lock; the attach waits behind it
    const stopping = w.remote.stop(2000) // a park, an end or a drain while the call waits (Task 37's accepting())

    expect(await attach).toEqual({ kind: 'refuse', code: 'hub_away', message: FLOW_MESSAGES.childStopped })
```

`/Users/yuai/Projects/.worktrees/agenttool-collab-bridge/packages/collab-bridge/src/air/edit-flows.ts`:

```ts
// The four remote calls that capture a mirror (C11, C12, spec §7.2–§7.6): claim, complete, takeover and artifact_attach.
// Each runs whole under the mirror's lock, so only one hub child captures a mirror at a time (K15) and the lock is held
// from the sync until the forwarded call returns, outside Collab's write transaction. The order, from §7.2:
//   1. the mirror must sit clean at its synced commit, or nothing is sent (mirror_tampered: a non-git mirror would
//      let review pass with no git evidence, K17);
//   2. read the task through the lineage's own child (a failed read is mirror_busy, never "free");
//   3. plan (Task 44) before anything else, so a replay or any other forwarded state reaches Collab and gets its stored
//      receipt (K61) even while another task holds the mirror;
//   4. the one-task rule only before a sync for task X or a takeover of X (R36);
//   5. the sync (Task 42), which refuses rather than repairs;
//   6. the stamp of what the Air saw, in the same Collab write (R14), rebuilt from oids and labels only, so a same-key
//      replay sends identical bytes (K24);
//   7. one forward, never retried (R18), and the tasks ref for a new completion.
// Every refusal before the forward is a definite "not sent".
import type { AgentCode } from '../failure.ts'
import type { Declared } from '../link/messages.ts'
import { mirrorBusy } from './busy.ts'
import type { CallOutcome, CollabChild } from './children.ts'
import { mirrorHead, syncedOid, syncMirror, writeTaskRef, type MirrorDeps, type SyncResult } from './mirror.ts'
import { normalizeText } from './normalize.ts'
import { completeLimitsStamp, takeoverNoteStamp } from './stamp.ts'
import { baseOf, planClaim, planComplete, planTakeover, PLAN_MESSAGES, type MirrorHandle, type Plan } from './sync-points.ts'
import { readTask, taskFromResult } from './tasks.ts'

export interface EditFlowCtx { flow: 'claim' | 'complete' | 'takeover' | 'attach'; name: string; args: Record<string, unknown>; declared: Declared | undefined;
  device: string; user: string; sessionId: string; workspaceId: string; child: CollabChild; mirror: MirrorHandle; mirrorDeps: MirrorDeps; nowMs: number;
  /** The forwarder's deadline on the hub's monotonic clock (§5.4): past it nothing is sent. null: no deadline. */
  notAfterMono: number | null; mono: () => number }
export type EditFlowOutcome = { kind: 'outcome'; outcome: CallOutcome } | { kind: 'refuse'; code: AgentCode; message: string; extra?: Record<string, unknown> }

export const FLOW_MESSAGES = {
  tampered: 'The mirror of this folder on the Air is not at its last synced commit; nothing was sent. Ai looks on the Air.',
  readFailed: 'The hub could not read this task, so it cannot tell whether the mirror is free; nothing was sent.',
  busy: 'Another edit task holds this folder\'s mirror on the Air; nothing was sent. Finish, release or block your claimed task, or wait for its review.',
  syncFault: 'The mirror sync failed unexpectedly; nothing was sent. Ai looks on the Air.',
  late: 'This call waited on the Air past its deadline and was not sent; nothing was applied.',
  childStopped: "This session's Collab child on the Air was stopping, so nothing was sent; call again if you choose.",
} as const

const refuse = (code: AgentCode, message: string, extra?: Record<string, unknown>): EditFlowOutcome =>
  extra === undefined ? { kind: 'refuse', code, message } : { kind: 'refuse', code, message, extra }

export function runEditFlow(ctx: EditFlowCtx): Promise<EditFlowOutcome> {
  return ctx.mirror.lock.run(() => flow(ctx))
}

const late = (ctx: EditFlowCtx) => ctx.notAfterMono !== null && ctx.mono() >= ctx.notAfterMono
const lateRefusal = () => refuse('hub_away', FLOW_MESSAGES.late, { reason: 'deadline_passed' })
// accepting() in the same synchronous turn as call() (Task 37): a child stopped while this call waited (for the lock, a
// read, a sync) is never written to, so the agent hears "not sent", never hub_outcome_unknown (§9.3 item 3).
const stoppedRefusal = () => refuse('hub_away', FLOW_MESSAGES.childStopped)

async function flow(ctx: EditFlowCtx): Promise<EditFlowOutcome> {
  const { spec } = ctx.mirror
  const deps = ctx.mirrorDeps
  // The lock may have been held for minutes by another lineage's capture: a call whose deadline passed is never sent.
  if (late(ctx)) return lateRefusal()
  // artifact_attach stores a uri and reads no file (K18); it only has to wait for any capture of this mirror (§7.2).
  if (ctx.flow === 'attach') {
    if (!ctx.child.accepting()) return stoppedRefusal()
    return { kind: 'outcome', outcome: await ctx.child.call(ctx.name, ctx.args) }
  }

  const head = await mirrorHead(spec, deps)
  const synced = await syncedOid(spec, deps)
  if (head === null || synced === null || head !== synced) return refuse('mirror_tampered', FLOW_MESSAGES.tampered)

  const taskId = ctx.args.task_id
  const task = typeof taskId === 'string' ? await readTask(ctx.child, ctx.workspaceId, taskId) : null
  if (!task) return refuse('mirror_busy', FLOW_MESSAGES.readFailed, { reason: 'read_failed' })

  let plan: Plan
  if (ctx.flow === 'claim') plan = planClaim(task, { sessionId: ctx.sessionId, mirrorWorktreeId: ctx.mirror.worktreeId, declared: ctx.declared })
  else if (ctx.flow === 'complete') plan = planComplete(task, { sessionId: ctx.sessionId, leaseId: ctx.args.lease_id, nowMs: ctx.nowMs, declared: ctx.declared })
  else plan = planTakeover(task)
  if (plan.kind === 'refuse') return refuse(plan.code, plan.message)

  const editTakeover = ctx.flow === 'takeover' && task.work_mode === 'edit'
  if (editTakeover && !ctx.declared) return refuse('fetch_failed', PLAN_MESSAGES.noDeclared)
  if (plan.kind === 'sync' || editTakeover) {
    const busy = await mirrorBusy(ctx.child, ctx.workspaceId, ctx.mirror.worktreeId, task.id)
    if (busy.busy) return refuse('mirror_busy', busy.reason === 'read_failed' ? FLOW_MESSAGES.readFailed : FLOW_MESSAGES.busy,
      { holder_task_id: busy.holder, reason: busy.reason })
  }

  let fetched: string | null = null
  if (plan.kind === 'sync') {
    if (late(ctx)) return lateRefusal()
    let r: SyncResult
    try {
      r = await syncMirror(spec, { declaredHead: ctx.declared!.head, atComplete: plan.atComplete }, deps)
    } catch {
      return refuse('mirror_tampered', FLOW_MESSAGES.syncFault)
    }
    if (!r.ok) return refuse(r.code, r.message)
    fetched = r.oid
  }

  const args: Record<string, unknown> = { ...ctx.args }
  if (ctx.flow === 'complete' && task.work_mode === 'edit' && (args.limits === undefined || typeof args.limits === 'string')) {
    // A new completion names what was just fetched; anything else (a replay, a duplicate, an expired lease) names what
    // Collab already holds, so the same key rebuilds the same request (§7.6). The policy already applied N2 (Task 36);
    // N2 is idempotent, so it changes nothing then and keeps a direct caller's bytes deterministic too.
    const oid = fetched ?? task.result_checkpoint?.head_sha ?? synced
    const base = baseOf(task)
    args.limits = completeLimitsStamp({ oid, device: ctx.device, user: ctx.user, headEqualsBase: base !== null && oid === base,
      seatLimits: typeof args.limits === 'string' ? normalizeText(args.limits) : undefined })
  }
  if (editTakeover && typeof args.recovery_note === 'string') {
    // Never refetched: the mirror stays at its last synced commit, and the device HEAD is only what the pipe declared.
    args.recovery_note = takeoverNoteStamp({ syncedOid: synced, declaredHead: ctx.declared!.head, seatNote: normalizeText(args.recovery_note) })
  }

  // After a sync this leaves the mirror at the fetched commit with nothing forwarded, as Collab's own refusal would (§12.2).
  if (late(ctx)) return lateRefusal()
  if (!ctx.child.accepting()) return stoppedRefusal()
  const outcome = await ctx.child.call(ctx.name, args)

  if (ctx.flow === 'complete' && plan.kind === 'sync' && outcome.outcome === 'ok') {
    // Written once, for a new completion only, from what Collab captured; the call has already applied, so a refusal
    // here is ledgered and the reviewer reads the result checkpoint's head instead (§7.7).
    const done = taskFromResult(outcome.result)
    const resultHead = done?.result_checkpoint?.head_sha ?? null
    let ref: 'ok' | 'mirror_tampered' | 'missing' = 'missing'
    try {
      if (resultHead !== null) ref = await writeTaskRef(spec, task.id, resultHead, deps)
    } catch {
      ref = 'mirror_tampered'
    }
    if (ref !== 'ok') deps.ledger({ event: 'tasks_ref', device: ctx.device, user: ctx.user, code: ref, outcome: 'refused' })
  }
  return { kind: 'outcome', outcome }
}
```

### Task 46: ssh failure classifier

**Kind:** [implementer] (bridge worktree) · **Group:** 15 · **Spec:** §5.5 first bullet (a copy of Summon's mapSshFailure, `Can't open user config file` and `Bad configuration option` mapped to `config`), §12.2 Link "`Can't open user config file` stops as `config`"; K34, K36, K45 (the Local Network case).

Summon's classifier is copied, not imported (spec §4.2), from `/Users/yuai/Projects/.worktrees/agenttool-mesh-spec/packages/summon/src/ssh.ts:1-188` at `b3ef7c95` (verbatim in `plan-facts/summon.md:795-1014`): the comment block on reading only ssh's own CRLF lines, `LOSS`, the kex pair, the host-key block patterns, `KNOWN`, `linesOf`, `patterns`, the host-key reader and mapSshFailure's order. The test fixtures are OpenSSH 9.9p2's own lines, as Summon's C review captured them (`packages/summon/tests/cli.test.ts:547-561, 979-1002`). What changes from Summon, and why:

- It returns a `DialFailure` for the dialer, not a `GateResponse`, and a host-key mismatch carries the presented fingerprint on its own, because Task 48 ledgers it and the sticky warning shows it (spec §5.5). No hint strings: the hub's status words say what to do (Task 47).
- Summon's `local` patterns are split. `Can't open user config file <config>: …` and `<config>: line N: Bad configuration option: …` are `config` (needs Yu, never retried), because a dial loop can never heal a broken config. `ssh: connect to host <host> port N: Operation not permitted` stays `unreachable`/`no_route`: that is this Mac's Local Network privacy refusing the caller (K45), which an Allow at the prompt heals.
- The paired entry is `Host <alias>` (the hub's `collab-<device>`) instead of `Host summon-<device>`, and the context always names the `-F` config, so only that file's errors are `config`.
- `sshCall` is not copied: the dialer spawns ssh itself (Task 48).

```ts
// src/air/ssh.ts
export type DialFailure =
  | { status: 'unreachable'; reason: 'no_route' | 'timeout'; detail: string }
  | { status: 'config'; detail: string }
  | { status: 'auth_refused'; detail: string }
  | { status: 'host_key_mismatch'; detail: string; fingerprint: string | null }
  | { status: 'unknown'; detail: string }                   // a loss, or nothing ssh is known to print: back off, never stop
export interface SshContext { host?: string; user?: string; identityFile?: string; config: string }
export function targetOfConfig(configText: string, alias: string): { host?: string; user?: string; identityFile?: string } | null   // Summon's targetOf for `Host <alias>`
export function classifySshFailure(stderr: string, ctx: SshContext): DialFailure
//   Summon's order; its `local` patterns split: `Can't open user config file <config>: …` and `<config>: line N: Bad configuration
//   option: …` → config; `connect … Operation not permitted` stays unreachable no_route (the Local Network hint)
```
  What later tasks rely on (Tasks 48 and 61): every `detail` is one line of printable ASCII, at most 200 characters, and is either the whole ssh line that decided, a closed whole line ssh is known to print, or the fixed text `ssh exited 255 without a line it is known to print`; never a line that may carry the remote session's text. A connection lost after a session existed (found anywhere in any line) wins over every other line and is `unknown`. A host-key mismatch's `fingerprint` is `SHA256:<43 base64>` only when ssh's exact changed-key block is there, else null. `targetOfConfig` reads only the alias's block, first value wins, and returns null when no line is exactly `Host <alias>`.

```ts
// b3ef7c95: the patterns, linesOf, the host-key block reader and mapSshFailure's order. Changes from Summon:
// - it returns a DialFailure for the dialer instead of a GateResponse, and carries the presented host-key fingerprint
//   on its own, so the hub can ledger it and show it in the sticky warning (spec §5.5);
// - Summon's `local` patterns are split: `Can't open user config file <config>: …` and `<config>: line N: Bad
//   configuration option: …` are `config` (needs Yu, never retried), while `connect … Operation not permitted`
//   stays unreachable(no_route): that is this Mac's Local Network privacy refusing the caller (K45, §13 S1);
// - the paired entry is read from `Host <alias>` (the hub's `collab-<device>`), and the context names the -F config.
// sshCall is not copied: the dialer spawns ssh itself (Task 48).

export type DialFailure =
  | { status: 'unreachable'; reason: 'no_route' | 'timeout'; detail: string }
  | { status: 'config'; detail: string }
  | { status: 'auth_refused'; detail: string }
  | { status: 'host_key_mismatch'; detail: string; fingerprint: string | null }
  | { status: 'unknown'; detail: string }                   // a loss, or nothing ssh is known to print: back off, never stop

/** What a failure is read against: the paired entry's HostName, User and IdentityFile, and the config given with -F. */
export interface SshContext { host?: string; user?: string; identityFile?: string; config: string }

/**
 * The `Host <alias>` entry of the bridge's ssh config, or null when no line is exactly `Host <alias>`. Only what the
 * classifier needs is read, up to the next Host or Match line; as in ssh, the first value wins.
 */
export function targetOfConfig(configText: string, alias: string): { host?: string; user?: string; identityFile?: string } | null {
  const lines = configText.split('\n')
  const at = lines.indexOf(`Host ${alias}`)
  if (at < 0) return null
  const t: { host?: string; user?: string; identityFile?: string } = {}
  for (const line of lines.slice(at + 1)) {
    if (/^\s*(Host|Match)\s/i.test(line)) break
    const m = /^\s*(HostName|User|IdentityFile)(?:\s*=\s*|\s+)(\S+)\s*$/i.exec(line)
    if (!m) continue
    const key = m[1]!.toLowerCase()
    if (key === 'hostname') t.host ??= m[2]
    else if (key === 'user') t.user ??= m[2]
    else t.identityFile ??= m[2]
  }
  return t
}

/*
 * ssh's stderr also carries the remote session's stderr (sshd runs the forced command through macair's login shell, so
 * Nuance's ~/.zshenv runs first), and a remote that exits 255 or is killed by a signal makes ssh exit 255 with no line of
 * its own. So a transport status is read only from ssh's own lines (Summon's rules, unchanged):
 * - Each ends \r\n, with no other \r in it. ssh writes every line it prints itself that way (log.c's do_log, the client
 *   loop's quit_message); the remote session's stderr passes through as the remote wrote it, which for a shell or script
 *   is a bare \n. A line without \r\n may be the remote's, so it never gives a transport status.
 * - Each is matched whole, start and end, in the exact form OpenSSH 9.9p2 prints it, and where ssh names the host, only
 *   when it names the paired one. Remote stderr left without a newline joins the head of ssh's next line, so a
 *   classifier that matched only a line's start could take remote text for ssh's.
 * - A line saying a connection existed and was lost wins over all of them, wherever in the line it is and whatever its
 *   line ending: that link may have carried frames, so the dialer only backs off (unknown), never stops.
 */
// Printed only once a session existed: the client loop's read error, EOF, keepalive timeout and write failures. And drops
// that can come before authentication or after the session started. Matched anywhere in a line (a remote head may precede).
const LOSS = [/Read from remote host /, /Connection to .* closed by remote host/, /Timeout, server\b.*not responding/, /client_loop: /,
  /Broken pipe/, /Connection reset/, /Connection closed by /, /packet_write_(wait|poll)/]
// The one kex failure 9.9p2 prints: a reset after the banners were exchanged, before authentication. Its two lines are
// the only loss-shaped lines that do not read as a loss, and only both, exactly, in this order.
const KEX = /^kex_exchange_identification: read: Connection reset by peer$/
const KEX_PEER = /^Connection reset by \S+ port \d+$/
// Every 9.9p2 host-key failure ends in this line (a changed key and an unknown host); it alone decides.
const VERIFY_FAILED = /^Host key verification failed\.$/
const BANNER_TIMEOUT = /^Connection timed out during banner exchange$/
// The changed-key block, for its fingerprint: the bar/warning/bar header, then the fingerprint as one ssh message over
// two lines (the first ends a bare \n, the second \r\n).
const BAR = /^@{59}$/
const WARNING = /^@ {4}WARNING: REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED! {5}@$/
const FP_INTRO = /^The fingerprint for the (ED25519|ECDSA|RSA|DSA) key sent by the remote host is$/
const FP = /^(SHA256:[A-Za-z0-9+/]{43})\.$/
const ERRNO = '(Broken pipe|Connection reset by peer|Connection refused|Host is down|Network is down|Network is unreachable|No route to host|Operation not permitted|Operation timed out)'
const OPEN_ERRNO = '(No such file or directory|Operation not permitted|Permission denied)' // a file ssh could not open
// Whole lines ssh prints that the detail of an `unknown` may show. All closed (no open-ended tail), so remote text at a
// line's head never comes along. Anything else is shown as fixed text.
const KNOWN = [
  /^Connection to \S+ closed by remote host\.$/, /^Timeout, server \S+ not responding\.$/, /^Connection (closed|reset) by \S+ port \d+$/,
  new RegExp(`^Read from remote host \\S+: ${ERRNO}$`), new RegExp(`^client_loop: send disconnect: ${ERRNO}$`),
  new RegExp(`^client_loop: ssh_packet_write_poll: Connection to \\S+ port \\d+: ${ERRNO}$`),
  new RegExp(`^(packet_write_wait|banner exchange): Connection to \\S+ port \\d+: ${ERRNO}$`),
  /^Connection to \S+ port \d+ timed out$/, /^Disconnected from \S+ port \d+$/,
  /^Unable to negotiate with \S+ port \d+: no matching [a-z ]+ found\. Their offer: [A-Za-z0-9@.,+-]+$/,
]
const FIXED_DETAIL = 'ssh exited 255 without a line it is known to print'

const esc = (s: string) => s.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&')
/** One line, printable ASCII only, clipped: the target controls banners, and a detail can reach a hash-chained ledger. */
const clean = (line: string): string => line.slice(0, 200).replace(/[^\x20-\x7e]/g, '?')

/** One line of stderr as it arrived: its text, and whether it was ssh's own (ended \r\n, no other \r) or maybe the remote's. */
interface Line { text: string; crlf: boolean }
/**
 * Split on raw bytes, before any normalisation: the line ending is what tells ssh's lines from the remote's. Only the
 * terminator is stripped (\r\n or \n): a classifier sees the line exactly, so a trailing space, tab or BOM is not ssh's line.
 */
function linesOf(stderr: string): Line[] {
  const parts = stderr.split('\n')
  const tail = parts.pop()! // after the last \n: '' when stderr ends with one, else a line with no terminator
  const out = parts.map((p) => {
    const body = p.endsWith('\r') ? p.slice(0, -1) : p
    return { text: body, crlf: p.endsWith('\r') && !body.includes('\r') } // `\r\r\n`, an inner \r: not ssh's
  })
  if (tail !== '') out.push({ text: tail, crlf: false })
  return out.filter((l) => l.text !== '')
}

/** The whole lines that carry a transport status for this paired entry. With no HostName to anchor to, the host ones are none. */
function patterns(ctx: SshContext) {
  const host = ctx.host ? esc(ctx.host.toLowerCase()) : null // ssh prints the HostName lowercased
  const connect = (errs: string) => (host ? [new RegExp(`^ssh: connect to host ${host} port \\d+: (${errs})$`)] : [])
  const config = esc(ctx.config)
  return {
    config: [new RegExp(`^Can't open user config file ${config}: ${OPEN_ERRNO}$`), new RegExp(`^${config}: line \\d+: Bad configuration option: \\S+$`)],
    localNetwork: connect('Operation not permitted'),
    missingKey: ctx.identityFile ? [new RegExp(`^no such identity: ${esc(ctx.identityFile)}: ${OPEN_ERRNO}$`)] : [],
    auth: host ? [new RegExp(`^${ctx.user ? esc(ctx.user) : '[^@\\s]+'}@${host}: Permission denied \\([a-z,-]+\\)\\.$`)] : [],
    noRoute: [...connect('No route to host|Network is unreachable|Network is down'),
      ...(host ? [new RegExp(`^ssh: Could not resolve hostname ${host}: nodename nor servname provided, or not known$`)] : [])],
    // Asleep, off, away (the ARP reject window answers Host is down), or Remote Login off (refused).
    timeout: [...connect('Operation timed out|Host is down|Connection refused'), ...(host ? [BANNER_TIMEOUT] : [])],
  }
}

/**
 * ssh's verification line, and the fingerprint of the key the host presented only when ssh's exact changed-key block is
 * there: the CRLF bar/warning/bar header, then after it the fingerprint message (a bare-\n line, then the CRLF SHA256 one).
 */
function hostKeyOf(lines: Line[], verify: Line): { detail: string; fingerprint: string | null } {
  const at = (i: number, re: RegExp, crlf: boolean) => lines[i] !== undefined && lines[i]!.crlf === crlf && re.test(lines[i]!.text)
  const h = lines.findIndex((_, i) => at(i, BAR, true) && at(i + 1, WARNING, true) && at(i + 2, BAR, true))
  const f = h < 0 ? -1 : lines.findIndex((_, i) => i > h + 2 && at(i, FP_INTRO, false) && at(i + 1, FP, true))
  if (f < 0) return { detail: clean(verify.text), fingerprint: null }
  const fingerprint = FP.exec(lines[f + 1]!.text)![1]!
  return { detail: clean(`${verify.text} Presented ${FP_INTRO.exec(lines[f]!.text)![1]} key: ${fingerprint}`), fingerprint }
}

/**
 * Tells ssh's failures apart (ssh exited 255). Only ssh's own whole (CRLF) line for a failure known to come before any
 * session keeps a transport status; a connection lost after one (found anywhere in a line), and anything this does not
 * recognise, is `unknown`. The detail is the line that decided, a closed whole ssh line, or fixed text: never a line that
 * may carry the remote session's text. Order matters: a loss wins over every pre-connect line.
 */
export function classifySshFailure(stderr: string, ctx: SshContext): DialFailure {
  const lines = linesOf(stderr)
  // A transport status comes only from ssh's own (CRLF) whole line.
  const at = (res: RegExp[]) => lines.find((l) => l.crlf && res.some((re) => re.test(l.text)))
  const known = (l: Line) => l.crlf && KNOWN.some((re) => re.test(l.text))
  const detailOf = (l: Line | undefined) => (l && known(l) ? clean(l.text) : FIXED_DETAIL)
  const k = lines.findIndex((l, i) => l.crlf && KEX.test(l.text) && lines[i + 1]?.crlf === true && KEX_PEER.test(lines[i + 1]!.text))
  // Only a real kex pair is exempt (k is -1 when there is none, so the first line is checked like any other).
  const losses = lines.filter((l, i) => !(k >= 0 && (i === k || i === k + 1)) && LOSS.some((re) => re.test(l.text)))
  if (losses.length > 0) return { status: 'unknown', detail: detailOf(losses.find(known)) }
  const p = patterns(ctx)
  const config = at(p.config)
  if (config) return { status: 'config', detail: clean(config.text) }
  const local = at(p.localNetwork)
  if (local) return { status: 'unreachable', reason: 'no_route', detail: clean(local.text) }
  const verify = at([VERIFY_FAILED])
  if (verify) return { status: 'host_key_mismatch', ...hostKeyOf(lines, verify) }
  // Printed during user authentication, after the connection: the key ssh was told to offer is not there to offer.
  const missingKey = at(p.missingKey)
  if (missingKey) return { status: 'auth_refused', detail: clean(missingKey.text) }
  const auth = at(p.auth)
  if (auth) return { status: 'auth_refused', detail: clean(auth.text) }
  if (k >= 0) return { status: 'unreachable', reason: 'timeout', detail: clean(lines[k]!.text) }
  const noRoute = at(p.noRoute)
  if (noRoute) return { status: 'unreachable', reason: 'no_route', detail: clean(noRoute.text) }
  const timeout = at(p.timeout)
  if (timeout) return { status: 'unreachable', reason: 'timeout', detail: clean(timeout.text) }
  return { status: 'unknown', detail: detailOf(lines.at(-1)) }
}
```

### Task 47: Device file and status files

**Kind:** [implementer] (bridge worktree) · **Group:** 15 · **Spec:** §4.3 (the device file's fields; `devices/nuance.status.json`), §9.2 status vocabulary, §9.9 (the skew warning above 60 s), §5.5 sticky warning, §10.4 exits "writes hub status"; P22, P30, P51, P52, P55, P58.

```ts
export interface DeviceShare { remote_realpath: string; remote_gitdir: string | null; air_clone: string; mirror_id: string;
```
